summary: Target-level plan of both of Pan's papers on locally analytic vectors in the completed cohomology of modular curves. Paper I (Forum Math. Pi 2022): the relative Sen operator and locally analytic coverings (LA.0); the perfectoid modular curve, the sheaf O^la_{K^p} on the flag variety, the vanishing of the horizontal nilpotent action and the horizontal Cartan action θ_h (LA.1); the power-series structure of O^la and the identification of the locally analytic vectors of completed cohomology with H^i(Fl, O^la) (LA.2); θ_h as the Sen operator and the LB topology of the cohomology (LA.3); n-cohomology and the μ-isotypic decomposition into overconvergent forms (LA.4); weight-one classicality, the irregular Fontaine–Mazur conjecture and Gouvêa's conjecture (LA.5). Paper II (Annals 2026, read in arXiv v1): the differential operators d_{k+1} and d̄_{k+1} and the intertwining operator I_k (LA.6); the n-invariants of ker I¹_k (LA.7); the computation of ker and coker over the Newton strata P¹(Q_p) (LA.8) and Ω (LA.9); the spectral decomposition, the de Rham complexes DR_k and the p-adic vanishing-cycle sequence (LA.10); the comparison of I_k with Fontaine's operator (LA.11); and the classicality theorem with the geometric descriptions of Π_ρ^la (LA.12). Items other roadmaps already own are imported by node id; Fontaine's almost de Rham theory, the general theory of locally analytic vectors and the supersingular uniformization at infinite level are requested from their owners. Independent review REV-DESIGN-PAN leaves the packet partial: geometric Čech strictness, relative module decompletion, Drinfeld Higgs compatibility, compact-support duality, the second-comparison highest-weight input and the Igusa crystalline comparison require the explicit repairs recorded in gaps. Downstream applications are targets conditional on these inputs.

nodes.title: Log G-Galois pro-étale perfectoid coverings of a small affinoid curve
nodes.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field of characteristic zero whose norm restricts to the p-adic norm, X = Spa(A, A⁺) a one-dimensional smooth affinoid adic space over Spa(C, O_C) and G a compact p-adic Lie group. A log G-Galois pro-étale perfectoid covering of X is an affinoid perfectoid X̃ = Spa(B, B⁺) over C together with a finite set S of classical points of X and an inverse system (X_i)_{i∈I} of finite Galois coverings X_i = Spa(B_i, B_i⁺) → X unramified outside S, such that X̃ ~ lim X_i in Scholze's sense, B⁺ is the p-adic completion of colim B_i⁺, and lim Gal(X_i/X) = G; when S is nonempty, the ramification index of X_i → X at each point of S is a power of p and these indices are unbounded in i. The affinoid X is small when S has at most one element and there is an étale map X → T¹ = Spa(C⟨T^{±1}⟩, O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩) (if S is empty) or X → B¹ = Spa(C⟨T⟩, O_C⟨T⟩) sending S to 0 (otherwise) that factors as a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps. G acts continuously on the Banach algebra B, so B is a Q_p-Banach representation of G.
hypotheses: C is complete and algebraically closed of characteristic zero, with |p| = 1/p.
X is smooth of dimension one over Spa(C, O_C); the étale map to T¹ or B¹ is part of the data of smallness.
proofSteps: Form the inverse system and its tilde-limit; the perfectoid condition is on the completed colimit B⁺, not on any finite level.
Record G as the inverse limit of the finite Galois groups, with its profinite topology and p-adic Lie structure.
Record smallness as the existence of the chart X → T¹ or B¹; the construction of the element θ depends on that chart only up to a unit of A (LA.0/differential-equation).
acceptance: Pan I Example 3.1.6 (the torus with all p-power roots of T, G ≅ Z_p) is an instance with S empty.
A finite Galois covering with bounded ramification at a point of S is not an instance.

sources.match: The setup: a smooth affinoid curve over C, a compact p-adic Lie group G and a 'log G-Galois pro-étale perfectoid covering' with ramification of p-power order along a finite set S; the smallness condition through an étale chart to the torus or the disc.

nodes.title: The Kummer tower satisfies the Tate–Sen conditions
nodes.statement: Let X̃ = Spa(B, B⁺) → X be a log G-Galois pro-étale perfectoid covering of a small affinoid curve, with chart f₁: X → Y ∈ {T¹, B¹}. Let Y_n = Spa(C⟨T^{±1/p^n}⟩) (resp. Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩)), Y_∞ their completed limit with Galois group Γ ≅ Z_p, and X_n = X ×_Y Y_n, X_∞ = X ×_Y Y_∞, X̃_∞ = Spa(B_∞, B_∞⁺) the completed colimit of the normalised fibre products X_{G_0,n}. Then: (1) the completed tensor product of A_n⁺ with R⁺ over R_n⁺ injects into A_∞⁺ with cokernel killed by p^{C_n}, C_n → 0, and (A_∞, A_∞⁺) is perfectoid; (2) Tate's normalised traces tr_{X,m}: A_∞ → A_m are continuous A_m-linear Γ-equivariant left inverses with tr_{X,m}(x) → x, and for a generator γ of p^mΓ the operator γ − 1 is invertible on ker(tr_{X,m}) with inverse of norm at most p^{c_m}, c_m → 0; (3) the p^nΓ-analytic vectors of A_∞ are A_n; (4) B_∞ satisfies the Tate–Sen conditions of Berger–Colmez for the group G × Γ with H_0 = G, Λ_{H,n} = B_{H,n} and R_{H,n} the normalised traces, with arbitrarily small constants; (5) (B_∞)^Γ = B.
hypotheses: X̃ → X is a log G-Galois pro-étale perfectoid covering of a small affinoid curve with a fixed chart f₁.
proofSteps: (1) is Scholze's Lemma 4.5 of 'p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties' applied along the rational embeddings and finite étale maps of f₁ (Pan I Lemma 3.2.3).
The traces on the standard tower send T^{l/p^k} ((l, p) = 1) to p^{n−m}T^{l/p^k} for k ≤ m and to 0 otherwise; normalise and base change along f₁ (Pan I §3.2.1–3.2.2).
(3): apply the trace to an analytic vector; the action of p^nΓ on A_m factors through the finite quotient, so analyticity forces invariance (Pan I Lemma 3.2.5).
By the rigid Abhyankar lemma X_{G_0,n} → Y_n is unramified for n large, so the finite levels are finite étale and the traces extend; almost purity gives (TS1) (Pan I §3.2.6 and Proposition 3.2.7).
(5) follows from almost purity applied to the Γ-covering X̃_∞ → X̃ (Pan I Lemma 3.2.9).
acceptance: For X = T¹ and G trivialised to the Kummer tower itself, (3) recovers the statement that the Γ-locally analytic vectors in C⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ are the smooth vectors.

sources.match: Construction of the base-changed Kummer tower, its normalised traces, the identification of analytic vectors with finite levels, the Tate–Sen conditions for G × Γ and the invariants (B_∞)^Γ = B.

nodes.title: The relative Sen operator φ_V
nodes.statement: In the situation of LA.0/tate-sen-for-the-kummer-tower, for every finite-dimensional continuous representation V of G over Q_p there is a unique B_∞-linear action φ_V: Lie(Γ) → End_{B_∞}(B_∞ ⊗_{Q_p} V) extending the natural action of Lie(Γ) on the G-smooth, Γ-locally analytic vectors of B_∞ ⊗ V. It commutes with G × Γ, is functorial in V and satisfies φ_{V₁⊗V₂} = φ_{V₁} ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ φ_{V₂}; it depends only on the restriction of V to an open subgroup of G and descends to a B-linear action on (B_∞ ⊗ V)^Γ = B ⊗ V. Construction: for a G-stable lattice T ⊂ V and G_0 acting trivially on T/pT, the Tate–Sen decompletion gives for n ≥ n(G_0) a unique free B⁺_{G_0,n}-submodule D⁺_{G_0,n}(T) of (B_∞)° ⊗ T of rank dim V, fixed by G_0, G × Γ-stable, spanning after base change, with a basis moved by Γ − 1 into p^cD⁺ (c < 1/2); then (γ − 1)^m D⁺ ⊂ pD⁺ for m large, so p^{m′}Γ acts analytically on D⁺ ⊗ Q_p for m′ large by Amice's criterion, and φ_V is the B_∞-linear extension of the derived action.
hypotheses: V is a finite-dimensional continuous Q_p-representation of the compact p-adic Lie group G.
The chart f₁ is fixed; a change of chart rescales the result by a unit of A (LA.0/differential-equation).
proofSteps: Apply Berger–Colmez's decompletion (BC08 Proposition 3.3.1) to (B_∞)° ⊗ T with constants c₁, c₂, c₃ = c small (Pan I Proposition 3.2.11). This requires the relative Banach-algebra module theorem, not merely classical finite-dimensional Sen theory; its supplier contract remains open.
Use Amice's criterion that (γ − 1)^m(B°) ⊂ pB° makes the action analytic on p^hZ_p (Pan I Example 2.1.9).
Identify the p^mΓ-analytic vectors of (B_∞ ⊗ V)^{G_0} with B_{G_0,m} ⊗ D⁺ (Pan I Lemma 3.2.12) and extend scalars.
Check functoriality and the tensor rule on the Γ-locally analytic G-fixed vectors (Pan I Propositions 3.2.13–3.2.14).
acceptance: For V the unipotent representation of Γ = G with γ ↦ (1 1; 0 1), φ_V is multiplication by the element a ∈ A^× comparing two charts (Pan I Lemma 3.4.3).

sources.match: Decompletion of B_∞ ⊗ T by the Tate–Sen formalism and the construction of the Lie(Γ)-action φ_V, with its uniqueness, commutation, functoriality and tensor compatibility.

nodes.title: Locally analytic vectors satisfy the relative Sen differential equation
nodes.statement: Let X̃ = Spa(B, B⁺) be a log G-Galois pro-étale perfectoid covering of a small affinoid curve X = Spa(A, A⁺) with a fixed chart. There is an element θ = θ_X̃ ∈ B ⊗_{Q_p} Lie(G), the image of a generator of Lie(Γ) under a map φ_X̃: Lie(Γ) → B ⊗ Lie(G), such that: (1) θ annihilates the G-locally analytic vectors B^la, for the B-linear extension of the Lie(G)-action; (2) for a closed normal subgroup H with X̃^H a covering, θ_X̃ ≡ θ_{X̃^H} modulo B ⊗ Lie(H); (3) a different chart changes θ by a unit of A, so A^×θ is intrinsic; (4) for every finite-dimensional V, the Lie(Γ)-action on B_∞ ⊗ V induced by θ through the infinitesimal G-action equals φ_V; (5) a D ∈ B_∞ ⊗ Lie(G) killing the G × Γ-locally analytic vectors of B_∞ is 0, and a D ∈ B_∞ ⊗ Lie(G × Γ) killing them is a multiple bd with b ∈ B_∞ and d in the image of φ_{X̃_∞}.
hypotheses: X̃ → X is a log G-Galois pro-étale perfectoid covering of a small affinoid curve; θ is determined only up to A^×.
proofSteps: Apply LA.0/relative-sen-operator to the finite-dimensional, two-sided-translation-stable subspaces V_k of C^an(G_0, Q_p) whose union is dense and multiplicative (Pan I Proposition 2.1.3), and pass to the completed limit, obtaining φ_{G_0} on B_∞ ⊗̂ C^an(G_0, Q_p) (Pan I §3.3.1).
The multiplicativity of the V_k makes φ_{G_0}(x) a right-invariant derivation commuting with Γ, hence an element of B ⊗ Lie(G_0) (Pan I Proposition 3.3.3, Corollary 3.3.4, using (B_∞)^Γ = B).
On B^{G_0-an} = (B_∞ ⊗̂ C^an(G_0))^{G_0 × Γ} the Lie(Γ)-action is trivial, giving (1) (Pan I Corollary 3.3.5).
Matrix coefficients V ⊗ V* → C^an(G_0) give (4) (Pan I Corollary 3.3.6); (2) is functoriality of the construction (Corollary 3.3.9); (5) is Proposition 3.3.10 and Corollary 3.3.11.

For (3), compare the two Γ-cohomology identifications of H¹(G' × Γ, B'_∞) through the two charts; the discrepancy a ∈ A^× is computed by the unipotent representation (Pan I Lemma 3.4.3, Proposition 3.4.5).
acceptance: For X = T¹ and X̃ the Kummer tower with G ≅ Z_p, θ = (dT/T) ⊗ 1, a generator of Lie(G) (Pan I Example 3.1.6).
On the perfectoid modular curve θ is the explicit matrix of LA.1/theta-on-the-modular-curve.

sources.match: Statement of the differential equation: an element θ of B ⊗ Lie(G) annihilating the locally analytic vectors, functorial in (G, X̃), nonzero for locally analytic coverings, well defined up to A^×; its construction from the Tate–Sen decompletion and its uniqueness.
θ is naturally a log Higgs field in B ⊗_A Ω¹_A(S) ⊗ Lie(G)(−1), the Higgs field of the p-adic Simpson correspondence in the Tannakian sense.

nodes.title: Locally analytic coverings
nodes.statement: Let X̃ → X be a log G-Galois pro-étale perfectoid covering of a small affinoid curve with chart f₁ and Kummer group Γ = Z_pγ. Let V₁ = Q_p² with γ acting by (1 1; 0 1), an extension of Q_p by Q_p. Tensoring with B_∞ and taking Γ-invariants gives a G-equivariant exact sequence (FE) of Banach spaces (exact by almost purity and continuous, hence strict by the open mapping theorem): 0 → B → (B_∞ ⊗ V₁)^Γ → B → 0, whose connecting map B^{G_0} → H¹_cont(G_0, B) is an isomorphism for every open subgroup G_0; up to a unit of A it is independent of f₁, and when X is defined over a finite extension of Q_p it is the log Faltings extension of X̃, with the quotient identified with B ⊗_A Ω¹_A(S). X̃ is a locally analytic covering of X if the following equivalent conditions hold: (1) (FE) stays exact on G_0-analytic vectors for some uniform open G_0; (2) (FE) stays exact on G-locally analytic vectors; (3) there is a G-locally analytic z ∈ B_∞ with γ(z) = z − 1. Equivalently, H¹_cont(G, B^la) → H¹_cont(G, B) is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: X is small with a fixed chart; the notion does not depend on the chart.
proofSteps: Exactness of (FE) is almost purity; the connecting map is computed through H^i_cont(G, B) ≅ H^i_cont(G × Γ, B_∞) ≅ H^i_cont(Γ, A) (Pan I §3.5.1).
The three conditions all say that 1 ∈ B lifts to a G-locally analytic vector (z, 1) of (B_∞ ⊗ V₁)^Γ (Pan I Proposition 3.5.3).
The intrinsic reformulation uses Hochschild–Serre for {1} × Γ ⊂ G × Γ and the vanishing of H¹_cont(G, (B_∞)^la) (Pan I Remark 3.5.5).
acceptance: The perfectoid modular curve over a small affinoid whose Hodge–Tate image lies in an affinoid of Fl is a locally analytic covering (LA.1/modular-coverings-are-locally-analytic).

sources.locator: §3.5.1 with the sequence (FE), Remark 3.5.2, Proposition 3.5.3, Definition 3.5.4, Remark 3.5.5, pp. 25–26
sources.match: The extension (FE) obtained from the unipotent representation of Γ, its relation with the log Faltings extension, the three equivalent conditions and the definition of a locally analytic covering, with the intrinsic H¹ criterion.

nodes.title: The differential operator is nonzero on locally analytic coverings
nodes.statement: If X̃ → X is a locally analytic covering, then φ_X̃: Lie(Γ) → B ⊗ Lie(G) is nonzero; equivalently θ_X̃ ≠ 0.
hypotheses: X̃ → X is a locally analytic covering of a small affinoid curve.
proofSteps: If φ_X̃ = 0, Lie(Γ) acts trivially on the Γ-locally analytic vectors of (B_∞)^{G_0-an} for all small G_0 (Pan I Lemma 3.3.2).
Then no G_0-analytic z with γ(z) = z − 1 exists, contradicting condition (3) of LA.0/locally-analytic-covering (Pan I Proposition 3.5.6).
acceptance: For the Kummer tower θ = (dT/T) ⊗ 1 ≠ 0.

sources.match: Nonvanishing of φ_X̃ for locally analytic coverings.

nodes.title: Taking locally analytic vectors of B is exact exactly for locally analytic coverings
nodes.statement: Let X̃ = Spa(B, B⁺) be a log G-Galois pro-étale perfectoid covering of a small affinoid curve X. Then R^iLA(B) = 0 for all i ≥ 1 if and only if X̃ is a locally analytic covering, and in that case B is strongly LA-acyclic. More precisely H^i_cont(G_0, B ⊗̂ C^an(G_0, Q_p)) ≅ H^i_cont(Γ, (B_∞)^{G_0-an}) functorially in G_0, so these vanish for i ≥ 2, and R¹LA(B) = colim_{n,k} H¹_cont(Γ, (B_∞)^{(G_n × p^kΓ)-an}).
hypotheses: X is small; LA-acyclicity is with respect to the uniform subgroups G_n of G.
proofSteps: Tensoring (FE) with C^an(G_n) and taking G_n-cohomology shows that LA-acyclicity forces (FE) to stay exact on locally analytic vectors (Pan I §3.6.2).
Hochschild–Serre for {1} × Γ and G_0 × {1} in G_0 × Γ, with almost purity, gives the isomorphism of Pan I Lemma 3.6.4; Γ ≅ Z_p has cohomological dimension one.
Replace (B_∞)^{G_0-an} by its p^kΓ-analytic part using that γ − 1 is invertible on the kernel of the trace (Pan I Lemma 3.6.6).

Given z with γ(z) = z − 1, approximate it by z_0 at finite level and solve φ_γ(y) = x by the convergent series −Σ φ_γ^{(m)}(x)(z − z_0)^{m+1}/(m+1)!; then x ∈ (γ − 1)(…) because φ_γ = (γ − 1)Σ(−1)^m(γ − 1)^m/(m + 1) (Pan I §3.6.7, Lemma 3.6.8).
acceptance: For the Kummer tower, B = A_∞ is strongly LA-acyclic for Γ (Berger–Colmez, Théorème 3.4, as Pan I Remark 3.6.9 notes).

sources.match: The equivalence between vanishing of R^iLA(B) and the locally analytic covering condition, with strong LA-acyclicity, proved by reduction to Γ-cohomology of analytic vectors and an explicit primitive.

nodes.title: Locally analytic sections and Čech cohomology on non-small affinoids
nodes.statement: Let X̃ = Spa(B, B⁺) → X = Spa(A, A⁺) be a log G-Galois pro-étale perfectoid covering of a (not necessarily small) affinoid curve, and suppose X is covered by small rational opens X_1, …, X_k whose preimages are locally analytic coverings. Let π: X̃ → X, Õ = π_*O_X̃, Õ_n its subsheaf of G_n-analytic sections and Õ^la = colim Õ_n. Then (1) R^iLA(B) = H^i(X, Õ^la) = Ȟ^i(X, Õ^la) for all i, so B is LA-acyclic iff Ȟ^i(X, Õ^la) = 0 for i ≥ 1; (2) if the Čech systems {Ȟ^i(𝔘_0, Õ_n)}_n are essentially zero for i > 0 (𝔘_0 = {X_i}), then B is strongly LA-acyclic.
hypotheses: X admits a finite cover by small rational opens with locally analytic preimages.
proofSteps: Let 𝔅 be the small rational opens contained in some X_i: a basis stable under intersection on which Õ^la has vanishing higher Čech cohomology, because B → C•(𝔘, Õ) is strictly exact (almost acyclicity) with LA-acyclic terms (LA.0/acyclicity-of-locally-analytic-vectors).
Cartan's criterion (Godement, Corollaire 4, p. 176) then computes H^i by Čech cohomology for the finite cover 𝔘_0.
Apply the derived-functor transfer of Pan I Lemma 2.2.2(3) to B → C•(𝔘_0, Õ) (Pan I Corollary 3.6.10).
acceptance: On the perfectoid modular curve this gives the strong LA-acyclicity of O_{K^p}(U) for U ∈ 𝔅 (LA.2/la-acyclicity-on-the-basis).

sources.match: Removal of the smallness hypothesis: R^iLA(B) is the (Čech) cohomology of the locally analytic subsheaf, and strong acyclicity follows from essential vanishing of Čech cohomology of the analytic pieces.

nodes.title: The fake Hasse invariants e₁, e₂, the coordinate x and the function t
nodes.statement: Fix a tame level K^p ⊂ GL_2(A_f^p) contained in a level-N subgroup with N ≥ 3 prime to p, and let X_{K^p} be the perfectoid modular curve over C (with cusps, infinite level at p), ω_{K^p} the pull-back of the Hodge bundle ω from finite level, V = Q_p² the standard representation of GL_2(Q_p) and π_HT: X_{K^p} → Fl = P¹ the Hodge–Tate period map defined by the position of ω^{-1}_{K^p}(1) in the relative Hodge–Tate sequence 0 → ω^{-1}_{K^p}(1) → V(1) ⊗ O_{X_{K^p}} → ω_{K^p} → 0. After fixing a generator of Z_p(1), the images of the standard basis e₁, e₂ of V are sections e₁, e₂ ∈ H⁰(X_{K^p}, ω_{K^p}) (the fake Hasse invariants), pulled back from O(1) on Fl; x := e₂/e₁ is the standard coordinate of Fl = P¹. The Weil pairing gives a map X_{K^p} → Isom(Z_p, Z_p(1)) ≅ Z_p^×, hence a function t ∈ H⁰(X_{K^p}, O) well defined up to Z_p^×; G_{Q_p} acts on t, e₁, e₂ through the cyclotomic character, GL_2(Q_p) acts on t through ε_p ∘ det with ε_p(x) = x|x|, and GL_2(A_f) acts on t through ε ∘ det. Write u₊ = (0 1; 0 0), h = diag(1, −1), z = diag(1, 1); then u₊ · x = 1, h · e₁ = e₁, u₊ · e₁ = 0, z · t = 2t. For n ≥ 1 fix t_n at level Γ(p^n) with ‖t − t_n‖ ≤ p^{−n}.
hypotheses: K^p is neat and contained in the principal level-N subgroup for some N ≥ 3 prime to p.

Pan's normalisation: the étale local system attached to V is the first relative étale cohomology of the universal elliptic curve, so the Tate module is V(1) = V*; the cyclotomic character has Hodge–Tate weight −1.
proofSteps: The perfectoid curve and its tower are those of PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S5 (Pan I Theorem 4.1.2).
The relative Hodge–Tate sequence and π_HT come from Scholze's period map on the anticanonical tower, with the quotient-line description of S3 (Pan I Theorem 4.1.6).
Evaluate the surjection V(1) ⊗ O → ω on e₁, e₂ ∈ V with the fixed basis of Z_p(1); the GL_2(Q_p)- and Galois-actions are read off from the twist (Pan I §4.2.1, p. 35).
Construct t from the Weil pairing on each finite level and pass to the limit; compute its transformation laws (Pan I §4.3.1, p. 38).
acceptance: On U₁ = {|x| ≤ 1}, e₁ generates ω_{K^p} and the matrix θ of LA.1/theta-on-the-modular-curve is (x x²; −1 −x).
The derivatives u₊ · x = 1 and z · t = 2t hold on every U ∈ 𝔅.

sources.match: The perfectoid modular curve, the relative Hodge–Tate sequence and π_HT; the fake-Hasse invariants e₁, e₂ as images of the standard basis; the function t from the Weil pairing with its Galois, GL_2(Q_p) and adelic transformation laws; the basis u₊, h, z of b with u₊·x = 1, h·e₁ = e₁, z·t = 2t.
The same function t, obtained from the second exterior power of the Hodge–Tate sequence after fixing a basis of Q_p(1), and the coordinate x = e₂/e₁.

nodes.title: The bundles g⁰ ⊃ b⁰ ⊃ n⁰ on the flag variety
nodes.statement: Let g = gl_2(C), Fl the flag variety of GL_2 over C (also its adic space). For a C-point x of Fl let b_x ⊃ n_x be the corresponding Borel and nilpotent subalgebras. Put g⁰ := O_Fl ⊗_C g, b⁰ := {f ∈ g⁰ : f_x ∈ b_x for all x} and n⁰ := {f ∈ g⁰ : f_x ∈ n_x for all x}, GL_2-equivariant vector bundles of ranks 4, 3, 1 for the adjoint action. Fix the rational Borel b of upper triangular matrices, its nilradical n and the Cartan h of diagonal matrices. Then b⁰/n⁰ ≅ O_Fl ⊗_C h canonically, the global sections of b⁰/n⁰ being h with trivial GL_2-action. On the chart x = e₂/e₁ of U₁ the line n⁰ is generated by the matrix (x x²; −1 −x).
hypotheses: GL_2 acts on Fl on the right through its action on the total space (Pan I §4.1.5).
proofSteps: Define the subbundles pointwise by the incidence condition and check local freeness on the two standard charts.
Compute that the section (x x²; −1 −x) of g⁰ over U₁ lies in n_x at every point (it is nilpotent with kernel the line of x).

Write the flag variety as B\GL_2 with the chosen convention. Conjugation by B is trivial on b/n, so the associated quotient bundle is O_Fl ⊗ h; the two chart matrices verify the ranks and the equivariance (Pan I §4.2.6, p. 37).
acceptance: The section (x x²; −1 −x) is nilpotent: its square is 0.
Over U₂ the generator of n⁰ is obtained by applying the Weyl element (0 1; 1 0).

sources.match: Definition of g⁰, b⁰, n⁰ on Fl following Beilinson–Bernstein, the natural action of g⁰ on O^la_{K^p}, and the identification b⁰/n⁰ = O_Fl ⊗ h.
On a chart where e₁ generates ω, the operator θ is (x x²; −1 −x), a generator of n⁰.

nodes.title: Faltings's extension is the relative Hodge–Tate sequence, up to sign
nodes.statement: On the pro-Kummer-étale site of X = X_{K^pGL_2(Z_p)} (log structure from the cusps C), let OB⁺_{dR,log} be the positive log structural de Rham sheaf. The first graded piece of the Poincaré sequence 0 → B⁺_dR → OB⁺_{dR,log} → OB⁺_{dR,log} ⊗ Ω¹_X(C) → 0 is the log Faltings extension 0 → Ô_X(1) → gr¹OB⁺_{dR,log} → Ô_X ⊗ Ω¹_X(C) → 0. After tensoring with ω^{-1} and using the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism ω ≅ ω^{-1} ⊗ Ω¹_X(C), it becomes an extension of ω ⊗ Ô_X by ω^{-1} ⊗ Ô_X(1). There is an isomorphism of Ô_X-modules ω^{-1} ⊗ gr¹OB⁺_{dR,log} ≅ V̂_log(1) ⊗ Ô_X under which this extension class is −1 times the class of the relative Hodge–Tate sequence 0 → ω^{-1} ⊗ Ô_X(1) → V̂_log(1) ⊗ Ô_X → ω ⊗ Ô_X → 0.
hypotheses: The relative log de Rham comparison V̂_log ⊗ OB_{dR,log} ≅ D_{dR,log} ⊗ OB_{dR,log} holds with D_{dR,log} the canonical extension (unipotent monodromy at the cusps).
proofSteps: Tensor V̂_log with the Poincaré sequence and take gr¹; use the inclusion of gr¹(D_{dR,log} ⊗ OB⁺_{dR,log}) and Griffiths transversality (Pan I proof of Theorem 4.2.2).
The composite gr¹D_{dR,log} ⊗ Ô → gr⁰D_{dR,log} ⊗ Ô ⊗ Ω¹(C) is the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism, so ∇ is surjective and V̂_log(1) ⊗ Ô ≅ gr⁰(D_{dR,log}) ⊗ gr¹OB⁺_{dR,log}.
Compare the two projections of gr¹(D_{dR,log} ⊗ OB⁺_{dR,log}) to get the sign −1.
acceptance: Restricted to the ordinary locus over a finite extension, this is Faltings's Theorem 5 of 'p-adic Hodge theory' (1988), as Pan I §4.2 notes.

sources.match: The relative log de Rham comparison with the canonical extension, the relative Hodge–Tate filtration obtained from Scholze's Proposition 7.9 in the log setting, the log Faltings extension, and the identification of the two extensions up to −1 through Kodaira–Spencer.

nodes.title: Preimages of small affinoids in the perfectoid modular curve are locally analytic coverings
nodes.statement: Let K_p ⊂ GL_2(Q_p) be open, X an affinoid of X_{K^pK_p} containing at most one cusp, small in the sense of LA.0/log-galois-perfectoid-covering, whose preimage X̃ ⊂ X_{K^p} is a log K_p-Galois pro-étale perfectoid covering, and suppose π_HT(X̃) is contained in an affinoid open of Fl. Then X̃ is a locally analytic covering of X. Such X form a basis of the topology of X_{K^pK_p}.
hypotheses: π_HT(X̃) lies in an affinoid of Fl, so ω_{K^p} is generated on X̃ by some e ∈ V(1) ⊗ C.
proofSteps: Global sections of the relative Hodge–Tate sequence on X̃ stay exact since H¹(X̃, ω^{-1} ⊗ Ô(1)) = 0 (Diao–Lan–Liu–Zhu, Theorem 5.4.3).

The middle term is V(1) ⊗ H⁰(X̃, Ô), on which K_p acts algebraically, and a vector e ∈ V(1) ⊗ C maps to a generator of ω; so the sequence stays exact on K_p-locally analytic vectors, and after multiplying by e so does the twisted one.
By LA.1/faltings-extension-is-hodge-tate-sequence this twisted sequence is Faltings's extension (FE) up to −1; apply criterion (2) of LA.0/locally-analytic-covering.
acceptance: Every U ∈ 𝔅 gives such coverings after shrinking to small rational subsets (Scholze 2015 Lemma 5.2).

sources.match: On a small affinoid with Hodge–Tate image in an affinoid, the global sections of the relative Hodge–Tate sequence stay exact after taking locally analytic vectors, so the preimage is a locally analytic covering.
Small affinoids with at most one cusp whose preimages are log K_p-Galois pro-étale perfectoid coverings form a basis, by Theorem 4.1.2 and Scholze's Lemma 5.2.

nodes.title: The relative Sen operator of the modular tower
nodes.statement: In the situation of LA.1/modular-coverings-are-locally-analytic, let e generate ω_{K^p} on X̃ and view e₁/e, e₂/e as functions on X̃. Then, up to a unit of O(X̃), the element θ ∈ O(X̃) ⊗_{Q_p} Lie(K_p) of LA.0/differential-equation is (1/e²)·(e₁e₂  e₂²; −e₁²  −e₁e₂) ∈ gl_2(O(X̃)). When e = e₁ this is (x x²; −1 −x) with x = e₂/e₁.
hypotheses: X is small with a fixed chart; the identification of Z_p(1) with Z_p is fixed.
proofSteps: Compute θ through the standard representation V, as Pan I Remark 3.3.7 allows: φ_V is determined on (B_∞ ⊗ V)^{K_p, Γ-la}.

By LA.1/faltings-extension-is-hodge-tate-sequence the sequence 0 → B·e^{-1} → B ⊗ V → B·e → 0, base-changed to B_∞ and K_p-invariants, is Faltings's extension on X_∞, which is A_∞ ⊗ (a nonsplit self-extension of Q_p) by Diao–Lan–Liu–Zhu §2.
So φ_V(x) kills B·e^{-1} and maps B ⊗ V onto B·e^{-1}; f = (e₂/e)e₁ − (e₁/e)e₂ generates B·e^{-1}; normalise φ_V(x)(e) = f and read off the matrix (Pan I proof of Theorem 4.2.4).
acceptance: The matrix is nilpotent of rank one with kernel the line ω^{-1}(1) of the Hodge–Tate filtration, as a point of n⁰ must be.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.2.4 with proof and Remark 4.2.5, p. 36
sources.match: Explicit formula for θ on the modular tower, computed from the standard representation and Faltings's extension; θ is the Higgs field attached by the p-adic Simpson correspondence to the universal local system.

nodes.title: The sheaves O_{K^p}, O^la_{K^p} and O^sm_{K^p} on the flag variety
nodes.statement: Let O_{K^p} := π_{HT*}O_{X_{K^p}}, a sheaf of C-Banach algebras on the analytic site of Fl with a GL_2(Q_p)-action and prime-to-p Hecke action. For a quasi-compact open U ⊂ Fl choose an open subgroup K_p ⊂ GL_2(Q_p) stabilising U and let O^la_{K^p}(U) be the K_p-locally analytic vectors of the Q_p-Banach representation O_{K^p}(U) (independent of K_p); this is a sheaf, GL_2(Q_p)- and Hecke-equivariant, with a natural action of Lie(GL_2(Q_p)) and of g⁰ = O_Fl ⊗ g by (f ⊗ X)·s = f(X·s). O_Fl → O_{K^p} lands in O^la_{K^p}. The subsheaf O^sm_{K^p} of GL_2(Q_p)-smooth sections is colim_{K_p} π_{HT*}π_{K_p}^{-1}O_{X_{K^pK_p}}. More generally, for a sheaf ω^k_{K^p} = ω_{K^p}^{⊗k}, ω^{k,la}_{K^p} and ω^{k,sm}_{K^p} are its locally analytic and smooth subsheaves of π_{HT*}ω^k_{K^p} (the Banach structure on sections over U ∈ 𝔅 coming from a generator of ω_Fl on U).
hypotheses: The locally analytic vectors are taken for the Q_p-analytic structure of GL_2(Q_p) (not a C-analytic one).
proofSteps: Existence of K_p stabilising U follows from compactness; independence of K_p from Pan I Remark 2.1.7.
Left exactness of taking locally analytic vectors and the sheaf property of π_{HT*}O⁺ give the sheaf property.
O_Fl(U) is a continuous quotient of a Tate algebra on which some K_p acts trivially modulo p, so it consists of analytic vectors by Amice's criterion (Pan I §4.2.6).
acceptance: H⁰(Fl, O^la_{K^p}) = H̃⁰(K^p, C)^la (Pan I Theorem 4.4.6, p. 45). The SL_2-action is trivial, but the determinant action can be locally analytic and non-smooth.

sources.match: Definition of O_{K^p} = π_{HT*}O and of its subsheaf O^la_{K^p} of locally analytic sections, its g⁰-action and the inclusion of O_Fl.
The subsheaf of GL_2(Q_p)-smooth sections of π_{HT*}ω^k and its description as push-forward of the colimit of finite-level pull-backs.
O^sm_{K^p}, Ω^{1,sm}_{K^p}(C) and the sheaves ω^{k,la}_{K^p}, ω^{k,sm}_{K^p}.

nodes.title: The horizontal nilpotent subalgebra annihilates O^la
nodes.statement: n⁰ acts trivially on O^la_{K^p}: for every open U and every local section f of n⁰ and s of O^la_{K^p}, f·s = 0.
hypotheses: Statement on the sheaf level; it suffices to check it on U ∈ 𝔅.
proofSteps: On U ∈ 𝔅 shrink to small affinoids whose preimages are locally analytic coverings (LA.1/modular-coverings-are-locally-analytic).
By LA.0/differential-equation θ kills the locally analytic vectors, and by LA.1/theta-on-the-modular-curve θ is a generator of n⁰ (up to a unit).
Conceptually: φ_V kills ω^{-1}(1) and maps ω isomorphically onto it, and π_HT is defined by the position of ω^{-1}(1), so O·θ ⊃ n⁰ tautologically (Pan I proof of Theorem 4.2.7).
acceptance: Pan I Lemma 4.3.3: a section of O^la killed by the rational Borel b is fixed by an open subgroup of GL_2(Q_p) (LA.2/borel-invariants-are-smooth).

sources.locator: Theorem 4.2.7 with proof, p. 37; Theorem 1.0.10, p. 7
sources.match: n⁰ acts trivially on O^la_{K^p}, deduced from the explicit θ.

nodes.title: The horizontal Cartan action θ_h and the weight sheaves
nodes.statement: Since n⁰ acts trivially on O^la_{K^p}, b⁰/n⁰ = O_Fl ⊗ h acts, and h → H⁰(Fl, b⁰/n⁰) gives an action θ_h of h on O^la_{K^p} commuting with g. −θ_h extends the action of Z(U(sl_2)) to S(h₀) through the Harish-Chandra isomorphism (with the sign coming from n_x-coinvariants), and θ_h restricted to the centre z of g is the action of z ⊂ g. On U ⊂ U₁ (e₁ a generator) θ_h(diag(a, d)) acts as the element (d  (d − a)x; 0  a) of O_Fl(U) ⊗ g. For a weight χ: h → C, χ(diag(a, d)) = n₁a + n₂d, written χ = (n₁, n₂), O^{la,χ}_{K^p} is the χ-isotypic subsheaf (θ_h(H)s = χ(H)s); likewise ω^{k,la,χ}_{K^p}. On ω^{k,sm}_{K^p} θ_h is trivial and on ω_Fl it is the character diag(a, d) ↦ d.
hypotheses: Weights are C-linear functionals on h; Pan II uses only integral weights.
proofSteps: Global sections of b⁰/n⁰ are GL_2-invariant, so the induced action commutes with g (Pan I Corollary 4.2.8).
The Harish-Chandra compatibility is Beilinson–Bernstein's computation for twisted D-modules on Fl, applied to coinvariants.
The coordinate formula follows from [ (d (d−a)x; 0 a), (x x²; −1 −x) ] = (a − d)(x x²; −1 −x) and [diag(a,d), u₊] = (a − d)u₊ (Pan I §5.1.1).
acceptance: On t: θ_h(diag(a, d))t = (a + d)t, so t ∈ O^{la,(1,1)}_{K^p}; on e₁ (as section of ω) the weight is (0, 1), consistent with ω_Fl having character d.

nodes.title: Twists of O^la by automorphic bundles and the Hecke-equivariant Hodge–Tate sequence
nodes.statement: Fix k ∈ Z. On U ∈ 𝔅 a generator of ω_Fl identifies O_{X_{K^p}}(π_HT^{-1}U) with ω^k_{K^p}(π_HT^{-1}U), giving a Banach structure independent of the generator and hence ω^{k,la}_{K^p}. There is an h-equivariant flag-variety twist: ω^{k,la}_{K^p}(−k) = O^la_{K^p} ⊗_{O_Fl} ω_Fl^{⊗k}. The smooth modular-curve tensor description is proved in LA.2/analytic-banach-algebras after the local expansion is constructed. Hecke-equivariantly, the relative Hodge–Tate sequence must be written 0 → ∧²D ⊗ ω^{-1}(1) → V(1) ⊗ O → ω → 0 with D the canonical extension of H¹_dR of the universal elliptic curve, since the implicit trivialisation of ∧²D shifts the prime-to-p Hecke action by the adelic norm.
hypotheses: k is an integer; U ∈ 𝔅.
proofSteps: The Banach structure is transported by a generator; independence because two generators differ by a unit of O_Fl(U) acting by an analytic automorphism.
The flag-variety twist is the pull-back π_HT*ω_Fl = ω(−1) (S3/elliptic-hodge-tate-and-O1).
The Hecke-equivariant form is the import S3/hecke-equivariant-hodge-tate-sequence (Pan II §4.2.3).
acceptance: θ_h acts on the flag line ω_Fl through diag(a,d) ↦ d; tensor powers add this character.

nodes.title: Borel-invariant locally analytic sections are smooth
nodes.statement: Let U ∈ 𝔅 with e₁ generating ω_{K^p} on π_HT^{-1}(U). If f ∈ O^la_{K^p}(U) is annihilated by the rational Borel subalgebra b of gl_2(Q_p), then f is annihilated by gl_2(Q_p), i.e. f is fixed by an open subgroup of GL_2(Q_p).
hypotheses: U ∈ 𝔅 and e₁ generates ω_{K^p} on π_HT^{-1}(U); the case where e₂ generates follows by the Weyl element.
proofSteps: θ(f) = 0 by the differential equation, with θ = (x x²; −1 −x) (LA.1/theta-on-the-modular-curve).
Since b·f = 0, θ(f) = (0 0; −1 0)·f, so the lower nilpotent kills f too and gl_2 = b + C·(0 0; 1 0) kills f (Pan I Lemma 4.3.3).
An alternative avoids θ: Tate's normalised traces on the anticanonical tower descend a b-invariant section to finite level (Pan I Remark 4.3.4).
acceptance: Applied to e₁/e_{1,n}-free expansions, it shows the coefficients c_{i,j,k} of LA.2/power-series-expansion come from finite level.

sources.match: A locally analytic section killed by the upper-triangular Borel subalgebra is killed by gl_2(Q_p), by the differential equation, or alternatively by Tate traces on the anticanonical tower.

nodes.title: Power-series expansion of locally analytic functions on the perfectoid modular curve
nodes.statement: Let U ∈ 𝔅 with e₁ generating ω_{K^p} on V_∞ = π_HT^{-1}(U), V_∞ the preimage of an affinoid V_{K_p}, G_0 ⊂ K_p uniform with G_n = G_0^{p^n}, V_{G_n} the preimage at level G_n, and choose r(n) increasing and approximations x_n, e_{1,n}, t_n at level G_{r(n)} with ‖x − x_n‖, ‖e₁ − e_{1,n}‖, ‖t − t_n‖ ≤ p^{−n} (also in the G_{r(n)}-analytic norms). For every G_m-analytic f ∈ O^la_{K^p}(U) there is N = N(f), bounded in terms of m, and for every n ≥ N unique c^{(n)}_{i,j,k}(f) ∈ H⁰(V_{G_{r(n)}}, O) with ‖c^{(n)}_{i,j,k}(f)‖ ≤ p^{(n−1)(i+j+k)}‖f‖_{G_m} such that f = Σ_{i,j,k≥0} c^{(n)}_{i,j,k}(f) (x − x_n)^i (log(e₁/e_{1,n}))^j (log(t/t_n))^k in the G_{r(n)}-analytic vectors. Conversely any family c_{i,j,k} at level G_{r(n)} with ‖c_{i,j,k}‖ ≤ C′p^{(n−1)(i+j+k)} defines a G_{r(n)}-analytic section with these coefficients.
hypotheses: U ∈ 𝔅, e₁ generates ω on V_∞; n ≥ N(f).
proofSteps: Expand along n: D_x(s) = Σ_l (−1)^l(x − x_{n″})^l(u₊)^l s/l! kills u₊ and f = Σ_i D_x((u₊)^i f/i!)(x − x_{n″})^i, using u₊·x = 1 and the Lie-action bound (Pan I §4.3.6).
Expand the u₊-invariant coefficients along h with log(e₁/e_{1,n′}) (h·log = 1, u₊·log = 0), then along z with log(t/t_n) (z·log = 2) (Pan I §§4.3.7–4.3.8).
The resulting coefficients are killed by b, hence smooth by LA.2/borel-invariants-are-smooth, hence at finite level; uniqueness from applying the same operators (Pan I proof of Theorem 4.3.9).
acceptance: For f = (t/t_n)^{a} with a ∈ Z_p the expansion has c_{0,0,k} = a^k/k! and all other coefficients zero, since (t/t_n)^a = exp(a log(t/t_n)).

sources.match: Explicit power-series description of the sections of O^la_{K^p} over U ∈ 𝔅 along x − x_n, log(e₁/e_{1,n}), log(t/t_n), with coefficients at finite level, norm bounds and the converse.
The same description restated for the weight-χ parts.

nodes.title: The Banach algebras O_n(U){x, e₁, t} and the spaces A_n
nodes.statement: For U, V_{G_n}, x_n, e_{1,n}, t_n as in LA.2/power-series-expansion and n > 0, O_n(U){x, e₁, t} ⊂ O^la_{K^p}(U) is the set of f = Σ c_{i,j,k}(x − x_n)^i (log(e₁/e_{1,n}))^j (log(t/t_n))^k with c_{i,j,k} ∈ H⁰(V_{G_{r(n)}}, O) and ‖c_{i,j,k}‖ ≤ C′p^{(n−1)(i+j+k)}, normed by ‖f‖_n = sup ‖c_{i,j,k}p^{(n−1)(i+j+k)}‖ (a C-Banach algebra, independent of the choice of x_n, e_{1,n}, t_n). Its unit ball is ∏_{i,j,k} H⁰(V_{G_{r(n)}}, O⁺) with the uniform coefficient topology (the supremum norm, rather than the Tychonoff product topology). For each m there is n with G_m-analytic vectors ⊂ O_n(U){x, e₁, t} ⊂ G_{r(n)}-analytic vectors, so O^la_{K^p}(U) = colim_n O_n(U){x, e₁, t}. In weight χ = (n₁, n₂), A_n ⊂ O^{la,χ}_{K^p}(U) is the subspace of t^{n₁}e₁^{n₂−n₁}Σ_i c_i(x − x_n)^i with ‖e₁^{n₂−n₁}c_i p^{(n−1)i}‖ bounded (c_i ∈ H⁰(V_{G_{r(n)}}, ω^{n₁−n₂})), a Banach space, and O^{la,χ}_{K^p}(U) = colim A_n as LB-spaces; B_n ⊂ ω^{k,la,χ}(U) is defined likewise and H⁰(V_{G_{r(n)}}, ω^k) ⊗ A_n = B_n. Passing the finite-level tensor identifications A_n → B_n to the direct limit proves ω^{k,la,χ} ≅ ω^{k,sm} ⊗_{O^sm} O^{la,χ}, and the same argument before taking a weight gives ω^{k,la} ≅ ω^{k,sm} ⊗_{O^sm} O^la (Pan II Lemma 3.2.8 and Remark 3.2.9, p. 21).
hypotheses: U ∈ 𝔅 with e₁ a generator; the weight χ is integral for A_n.
proofSteps: Norm and completeness follow from the product description of the unit ball (Pan I Definition 4.3.10).
Independence of choices: changing x_n, e_{1,n}, t_n rescales by power series with bounded coefficients (Pan I Remark 4.3.11).
The sandwich between analytic vectors is Theorem 4.3.9 with Remark 4.3.12; A_n is the weight-χ slice (Pan II §3.2.7, displays (3.2.1)–(3.2.2)).
Use finite-level local freeness of ω^k to tensor the coefficient modules, then pass to the direct limit; this proves the smooth tensor description without assuming it in LA.1.
acceptance: A_n ≅ O⁺(V_{G_{r(n)}})[[(x − x_n)/p^{n−1}]] ⊗ Q_p after fixing a generator of ω^{n₁−n₂} at level G_{r(n)} (Pan II (3.2.2)).

sources.match: The Banach algebras of convergent expansions, their norms, the product description of the unit ball, independence of choices and the sandwich between analytic vectors.
The weight-χ Banach spaces A_n and B_n, the LB-structure as their colimit and the formal power series model.

nodes.title: Strong LA-acyclicity of O_{K^p}(U)
nodes.statement: For every U ∈ 𝔅, the K_p-Banach representation O_{K^p}(U) is strongly LA-acyclic. Moreover for a finite rational cover 𝔘 of V_{K_p}, Ȟ^i(𝔘, ∏_{i,j,k} O⁺_{r(n)}) ⊗ Q_p = 0 and the systems {Ȟ^i(𝔘, Õ_n)}_n are essentially zero for i ≥ 1.
hypotheses: U ∈ 𝔅; Õ_n is the sheaf of G_n-analytic sections of the push-forward to V_{K_p}.
proofSteps: The map φ_n from ∏ O⁺_{r(n)} ⊗ Q_p to Õ^la given by the expansion is an isomorphism onto its image, sandwiched between analytic pieces (LA.2/analytic-banach-algebras).
Tate acyclicity at finite level kills Ȟ^i of the unit balls up to bounded p-power (Pan I Lemma 4.3.14).

Cover V_{K_p} by small rational opens whose preimages are locally analytic coverings (LA.1/modular-coverings-are-locally-analytic) and apply LA.0/acyclicity-for-covers-by-small-opens (Pan I Proposition 4.3.15).
acceptance: Consequently H^j(U, O^la_{K^p}) = 0 for j > 0 and U ∈ 𝔅.

sources.match: Sheaf-theoretic form of the expansion, essential vanishing of Čech cohomology of the analytic pieces, and strong LA-acyclicity of O_{K^p}(U) for U ∈ 𝔅.

nodes.title: Completed cohomology is the cohomology of O⁺ on the perfectoid modular curve
nodes.statement: For every i there are natural GL_2(Q_p)- and prime-to-p-Hecke-equivariant almost isomorphisms of O_C-modules H̃^i(K^p, Z/p^n) ⊗ O_C/p^n ≅ H^i(X_{K^p}, O⁺/p^n) (analytic topology) and H̃^i(K^p, Z_p) ⊗̂ O_C ≅ H^i(X_{K^p}, O⁺). Hence H̃^i(K^p, C) := H̃^i(K^p, Z_p) ⊗̂ C ≅ H^i(X_{K^p}, O), a Q_p-Banach representation of GL_2(Q_p).
hypotheses: K^p is as in LA.1/fake-hasse-invariants; X_{K^p} is the compactified perfectoid curve, which is harmless because the restriction from compactified to open curves is an isomorphism on colim_{K_p} H^i(−, Z/p^n).
proofSteps: Compare singular and étale cohomology at finite level and apply the (log) primitive comparison theorem, then pass to the colimit over K_p, as in Scholze's Theorem IV.2.1 (Pan I Theorem 4.4.2).

Compute H^i(X_{K^p}, O⁺) and H^i(X_{K^p}, O⁺/p^n) by one Čech complex on a finite affinoid perfectoid cover (almost acyclicity) and pass to the limit with the bounded-torsion lemma CC.2/complete-torsion-free-complex-control (Pan I Corollary 4.4.3, Lemma 4.4.4).
H̃^i(K^p, Z_p) is p-torsion free here (Pan I Remark 4.4.5), which simplifies the limit argument.
acceptance: In degree zero, completed integral cohomology gives continuous O_C-valued functions on the profinite component set lim π_0(X_{K^pK_p}); the perfectoid comparison is up to almost zero. Modulo p^m these functions factor through finite component sets.

sources.match: Completed cohomology of modular curves, its almost identification with the analytic cohomology of O⁺/p^n and O⁺ on the perfectoid modular curve via the primitive comparison theorem, and the limit lemma for bounded torsion.

nodes.title: Locally analytic vectors of completed cohomology as cohomology on the flag variety
nodes.statement: For every i there are natural GL_2(Q_p)- and Hecke-equivariant isomorphisms H̃^i(K^p, C) ≅ H^i(Fl, O_{K^p}) and H̃^i(K^p, C)^la ≅ H^i(Fl, O^la_{K^p}), both computed by the Čech complex of any finite cover of Fl by elements of 𝔅 (for instance {U₁, U₂}).
hypotheses: The locally analytic vectors are for GL_2(Q_p); H̃^i(K^p, Z_p) is an admissible GL_2(Q_p)-representation.
proofSteps: R^jπ_{HT*}O = 0 for j > 0 by almost acyclicity on the affinoid perfectoid preimages of U ∈ 𝔅, so H^i(X_{K^p}, O) = H^i(Fl, O_{K^p}) (Pan I proof of Theorem 4.4.6).
H^j(U, O^la_{K^p}) = 0 for U ∈ 𝔅, j > 0, by LA.2/la-acyclicity-on-the-basis and Cartan's criterion; so Čech complexes compute both cohomologies.

The Čech complex of O_{K^p} is strict (bounded torsion of H^i(Fl, O⁺_{K^p})), its terms are LA-acyclic and its cohomology H̃^i(K^p, C) is LA-acyclic by admissibility (Schneider–Teitelbaum, Pan I Corollary 2.2.4); Pan I Lemma 2.2.2(2) gives the claim.
acceptance: Pan I Theorem 1.0.9 gives H⁰(Fl,O^la)=H̃⁰(K^p,C)^la. The smooth subspace is the finite-level colimit of H⁰(X_{K^pK_p},O); the full locally analytic space also permits non-smooth determinant characters.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.4.6 with proof, pp. 45–46; Theorem 1.0.9, p. 6
sources.match: The isomorphisms H̃^i(K^p, C) ≅ H^i(Fl, O_{K^p}) and H̃^i(K^p, C)^la ≅ H^i(Fl, O^la_{K^p}), proved by Čech complexes on 𝔅 and the acyclicity of taking locally analytic vectors.

nodes.title: The weight sheaves O^{la,χ} and their sections
nodes.statement: For a weight χ = (n₁, n₂) of h, O^{la,χ}_{K^p} ⊂ O^la_{K^p} is the χ-isotypic subsheaf for θ_h (LA.1/horizontal-cartan-action); likewise ω^{k,la,χ}_{K^p}. On U ∈ 𝔅 with e₁ a generator: H^i(h, O^la_{K^p}(U) ⊗ χ) = 0 for i ≥ 1, and every f ∈ O^{la,χ}_{K^p}(U) is (t/t_N)^{n₁}(e₁/e_{1,N})^{n₂−n₁}Σ_{i≥0} c^{(n)}_i(f)(x − x_n)^i for n > N large, with c^{(n)}_i(f) ∈ H⁰(V_{G_{r(n)}}, O) and ‖c^{(n)}_i(f)‖ ≤ C′p^{(n−1)i}. For integral χ this reads f = t^{n₁}e₁^{n₂−n₁}Σ_i c_i(x − x_n)^i with c_i ∈ H⁰(V_{G_{r(n)}}, ω^{n₁−n₂}), every G_n-analytic vector arises this way and f = 0 iff all c_i = 0; for ω^{k,la,χ} the c′_i lie in H⁰(V_{G_{r(n)}}, ω^{n₁−n₂+k}). The n-finite part, the f with finitely many nonzero c_i at some level, is dense and equals ω^{n₁−n₂+k,sm}_{K^p}(U) ⊗_{Q_p} M^∨_{(n₂,n₁)}, M^∨ the dual Verma-type module of polynomials in x. Multiplication by t^k identifies O^{la,(n₁,n₂)} with O^{la,(n₁+k,n₂+k)}. On the three-variable expansion of LA.2/power-series-expansion, θ_h(diag(a, d)) sends c_{i,j,k} to d(j + 1)c_{i,j+1,k} + (a + d)(k + 1)c_{i,j,k+1} (Pan I §5.1.1, pp. 46–47).
hypotheses: χ is a C-linear functional on h; integrality n₁, n₂ ∈ Z is assumed in Pan II and wherever ω-coefficients are used.
proofSteps: Since θ_h(diag(a, d)) acts on expansion coefficients by c_{i,j,k} ↦ d(j+1)c_{i,j+1,k} + (a + d)(k+1)c_{i,j,k+1}, the χ-isotypic condition fixes the j- and k-dependence as the binomial expansions of (t/t_N)^{n₁}(e₁/e_{1,N})^{n₂−n₁} (Pan I §5.1.1, Lemma 5.1.2).
The h-cohomology vanishing follows from the same coefficient recursion (Pan I Lemma 5.1.2(1)).
For integral weights rewrite with e₁^{n₂−n₁}t^{n₁} and ω-valued coefficients (Pan II Theorem 3.2.2, Corollary 3.2.3, Remark 3.2.4).
acceptance: For χ = (0, 0), O^{la,(0,0)}(U) ⊃ O_Fl(U) ⊗ O^sm(U) with dense image (Pan II Theorem 1.2.7, first claim).

sources.match: θ_h on the expansion coefficients, vanishing of h-cohomology and the explicit form of χ-isotypic sections.
Integral weights, the explicit description of sections of O^{la,χ} and ω^{k,la,χ} with coefficients in ω^{n₁−n₂(+k)} at finite level, the dense n-finite part as ω^{sm} ⊗ M^∨ and twisting by t.

nodes.title: Locally algebraic subsheaves and the twisting isomorphism
nodes.statement: For k ≥ 0 and χ = (0, k), the k-th symmetric power of V(1) → ω_{K^p} gives Sym^k V(k) → ω^k_{K^p}, the natural map from H⁰(Fl, ω_Fl^k)(k), and hence an injective map Sym^k V(k) ⊗ ω^{−k,sm}_{K^p} → O^{la,(0,k)}_{K^p} whose image O^{lalg,(0,k)}_{K^p} is exactly the GL_2(Q_p)-locally algebraic vectors of O^{la,(0,k)}; for χ = (n₁, n₁ + k) twist by t^{n₁}. There is a natural isomorphism ω^{k,sm}_{K^p} ⊗_{O^sm_{K^p}} O^{la,χ}_{K^p} ≅ ω^{k,la,χ}_{K^p} (and without weights ω^{k,sm} ⊗_{O^sm} O^la ≅ ω^{k,la}).

proofSteps: The map is injective and lands in weight (0, k) by the weight computation of e₁, e₂ (Pan II §3.2.5).
Locally algebraic vectors are characterised by the n-finite, algebraic expansions of LA.2/weight-sheaves (Pan II Definition 3.2.6).
The twisting isomorphism is the colimit of H⁰(V_{G_{r(n)}}, ω^k) ⊗ A_n = B_n (Pan II Lemma 3.2.8, Remark 3.2.9).

nodes.title: Essential vanishing of Čech cohomology of the analytic pieces, and extension to the larger cover
nodes.statement: Let 𝔘 be a finite cover of some U ∈ 𝔅 by elements of 𝔅 and G_0 = 1 + p^mM_2(Z_p) stabilising its members. For i ≥ 1 and n ≥ 0 the map Ȟ^i(𝔘, O^{G_n-an,χ}_{K^p}) → Ȟ^i(𝔘, O^{G_m-an,χ}_{K^p}) is zero for m large. For the covers 𝔘 = {U₁ = {|x| ≤ 1}, U₂ = {|x| ≥ 1}} and 𝔘′ = {U′₁ = {|x| ≤ |p^{−1}|}, U′₂ = {|x| ≥ |p|}} of Fl, for every n there is m ≥ n such that the image of Ȟ¹(𝔘, O^{G_n-an,χ}) in Ȟ¹(𝔘, O^{G_m-an,χ}) lies in the image of Ȟ¹(𝔘′, O^{G_m-an,χ}): every G_n-analytic section s on U₁ ∩ U₂ has G_m-analytic s_i on U_i with s + s₁ + s₂ extending G_m-analytically to U′₁ ∩ U′₂.
hypotheses: χ integral; U′_i are diag(p, 1)^{±1}-translates of U_i, so the results for 𝔅 apply to them.
proofSteps: Replace sections over each U_I by the Banach spaces A_{I,n}; the Čech complex becomes a countable product of Čech complexes of O⁺ at level G_{r(n)}, killed in positive degree by a power of p by Tate acyclicity (Pan II Proposition 3.2.11).
Apply Proposition 3.2.11 to the cover {U₁, U′₁ ∩ U₂} of U′₁ and then to {U₂, U′₁ ∩ U′₂} of U₂ (Pan II Corollary 3.2.13).
acceptance: In degree 0 there is no essential vanishing: Ȟ⁰ is the sections, which grow with n.

nodes.title: Cohomology of O^{la,χ} against the χ-part of completed cohomology
nodes.statement: (1) θ_h(h) = 0 and θ_h(z) = z on H⁰(Fl, O^la_{K^p}); in particular H⁰(Fl, O^{la,χ}) = 0 if χ(h) ≠ 0. (2) If χ(h) ≠ 0 then H¹(Fl, O^{la,χ}) = H¹(Fl, O^la)_χ, the χ-isotypic part for θ_h. If χ(h) = 0, χ = (n₁, n₁), there is a g-equivariant exact sequence 0 → colim_{K_p} H⁰(X_{K^pK_p}, O)·(t/t_N)^{n₁} → H¹(Fl, O^{la,χ}) → H¹(Fl, O^la)_χ → 0.
hypotheses: The Čech complex of {U₁, U₂} computes both sides (LA.2/locally-analytic-completed-cohomology).
proofSteps: Global sections factor through the determinant on connected components, so the sl_2-action, and hence the horizontal coroot action, vanishes. These functions can be locally analytic without being smooth; the centre can act nontrivially (Pan I Corollary 5.1.3(1), p. 47).
Apply h-cohomology to the two-term Čech complex using the vanishing H^i(h, O^la(U) ⊗ χ) = 0 of LA.2/weight-sheaves (Pan I Corollary 5.1.3(2) and footnote 2).
acceptance: For χ = (0, 0) the extra term is H̃⁰(K^p, C)^sm, the source of the k = 1 discrepancy in Pan II §1.2.5 and (3.4.1).

nodes.title: Sen operators and Hodge–Tate weights of semilinear C-Banach representations
nodes.statement: Let K ⊂ C be a finite extension of Q_p, K_∞ the maximal Z_p-extension of K in K(μ_{p^∞}) (fixed field of the kernel H_K of the projection ε̃_p of the cyclotomic character to 1 + 2pZ_p), so Gal(K_∞/K) ≅ Z_p with Lie algebra identified with Q_p through the cyclotomic character. For a C-Banach space W with continuous semilinear G_K-action let W^K be the K-Banach space of G_{K_∞}-fixed, G_K-analytic vectors and φ_K: C ⊗̂_K W^K → W the induced map. When φ_K is an isomorphism, the action of 1 ∈ Lie Gal(K_∞/K) on W^K is K-linear; its C-linear extension is the Sen operator θ_Sen of W. More generally (Pan I Definition 5.1.5) a continuous C-linear θ_Sen on W is a Sen operator if it extends the action of 1 ∈ Q_p = Lie Gal(Q_p(μ_{p^∞})/Q_p) on the G_{K(μ_{p^∞})}-smooth, G_K-locally analytic vectors, and for W = colim W_n (C-Banach, increasing) θ is a Sen operator if it preserves each W_n and is one there. W is Hodge–Tate of weights {w₁, …, w_n} ⊂ Z if for some finite L ⊃ K, φ_L is an isomorphism and θ_Sen acts semisimply on W^L with eigenvalues −w₁, …, −w_n, all eigenspaces nonzero; then W = ⊕ C ⊗̂_L W^L_{−w_i}, independent of L. W has pure Hodge–Tate–Sen weight k ∈ C if −k is a Sen operator.
hypotheses: Convention (Pan I p. 4 and Pan II): the cyclotomic character has Hodge–Tate weight −1; PadicHodgeTheory R06.2 uses +1, so weights here are the negatives of the R06.2 weights.
proofSteps: For finite-dimensional W this is Sen's operator: Sen proves existence and uniqueness (Pan I Remark 5.1.7; PadicHodgeTheory P7/sen-module).
Base change of a trivial-action Banach space: if X^K = X then (C ⊗̂_K X)^K = X (Pan II Proposition 3.3.3).

Kernels, closed subspaces and strict quotients of maps between representations with φ_K an isomorphism again have φ_K an isomorphism (Pan II Corollary 3.3.4), by exactness of C ⊗̂_K (−) on Banach spaces (orthonormal bases).
Tate's normalised trace gives L ⊗_K W^K = W^L for finite L/K, so the notion does not depend on K (Pan II §3.3.2).
acceptance: For W = C(j), W^K = K·b_j with b_j a basis of Q_p(j), on which 1 ∈ Lie Gal(K_∞/K) acts by j; so θ_Sen = j and C(j) has Hodge–Tate weight −j in this convention.

nodes.title: θ_h(diag(0, 1)) is the Sen operator
nodes.statement: G_{Q_p} acts continuously on X_{K^p}, commuting with GL_2(Q_p) and Hecke operators, hence on O^la_{K^p} and O^{la,χ}_{K^p}; for U ∈ 𝔅 the affinoids V_{G_n} and their preimages are defined over a finite extension K of Q_p. Then θ_h(diag(0, 1)) is the unique Sen operator on O_{K^p}(U)^la, and on H^i(Fl, O^la_{K^p}) = H̃^i(K^p, C)^la for every i. In particular, for every finite-dimensional C-semilinear G_{Q_p}-subrepresentation of H̃^i(K^p, C)^la it agrees with Sen's operator.
hypotheses: U ∈ 𝔅; K is a finite extension over which V_{G_0} is defined (Pan II §3.3.1).
proofSteps: Write sections by the expansion of LA.2/power-series-expansion; G_K acts on t, e₁, e₂ through the cyclotomic character and fixes x (Pan II §3.3.1).
Compute the derivative of the G_K-action on the decompleted expansions and compare with the coordinate formula for θ_h (Pan I Theorem 5.1.8, by explicit calculation; Remark 5.1.10).
Pass to H¹ through the two-term Čech complex of {U₁, U₂} with the bounds of Pan I Lemma 5.1.13 (Pan I Theorem 5.1.11).
acceptance: On t, θ_h(diag(0, 1))t = t and G_{Q_p} acts on t through the cyclotomic character, whose Sen operator is 1: consistent.

sources.match: θ_h(diag(0,1)) is the unique Sen operator on O_{K^p}(U)^la and on H̃^i(K^p, C)^la, proved by explicit calculation.

nodes.title: The analytic vectors of O^{la,(n₁,n₂)} are Hodge–Tate of weight −n₂
nodes.statement: For an integral weight χ = (n₁, n₂) and U ∈ 𝔅, the C-Banach space of G_n-analytic vectors of O^{la,χ}_{K^p}(U) is Hodge–Tate of weight −n₂ for every n ≥ 0, and so is the Banach space A_n of LA.2/analytic-banach-algebras. Consequently the Čech cohomology Ȟ^*(O^{G_n-an,χ}_{K^p}) for {U₁, U₂} is Hodge–Tate of weight −n₂.
hypotheses: K contains μ_{p²} and x_n is defined over K.
The assertion about Čech cohomology requires the closed-range Banach quotient construction of LA.3/lb-topology-on-cohomology; that construction is an open gap here.
proofSteps: G_K acts on t, e₁, e₂ by the cyclotomic character and fixes x, so A_n is G_K-stable; its K-form A_{n,K} of series with G_K-invariant coefficients carries the n₂-th power of the cyclotomic character, and A_n = C ⊗̂_K A_{n,K} by Pan II Proposition 3.3.3 (Pan II Proposition 3.3.8, Lemma 3.3.9).
Taking G_n-analytic vectors commutes with this base change.

Conditional on the strict Čech maps of LA.3/lb-topology-on-cohomology, their Banach kernels and quotients inherit the Hodge–Tate property by Pan II Corollary 3.3.4 (Proposition 3.4.10). This step does not repair the missing strictness proof.
acceptance: Consistency with LA.3/theta-h-is-the-sen-operator: θ_h(diag(0, 1)) acts on O^{la,(n₁,n₂)} by n₂, the Sen operator, i.e. weight −n₂.

nodes.title: Restriction to a strictly smaller open is compact after decompletion
nodes.statement: Let χ be integral and U, U′ ∈ 𝔅 be stable under G_0 = 1 + p^lM_2(Z_p), l ≥ 2, with preimages coming from affinoids defined over a finite extension K, and suppose U is a strict neighbourhood of U′ (the closure of U′ lies in U). Then for every n the G_n-analytic vectors of O^{la,χ}(U) and O^{la,χ}(U′) are the base change from K of their K-forms, and the restriction map from the K-form of level n over U to the K-form of level m over U′ is compact for m ≥ n large.
hypotheses: U′ ⋐ U strictly; the K-forms are those of LA.3/analytic-vectors-are-hodge-tate.
proofSteps: The K-forms are spaces of power series in x − x_n with coefficients in finite-level affinoid algebras over K (LA.3/analytic-vectors-are-hodge-tate).

Restriction along a strict neighbourhood is compact on the finite-level affinoid algebras, and multiplication of the variable by a topologically nilpotent element is compact (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4/pan-tate-compactness).
acceptance: Over C instead of K the restriction is not compact: C is not locally compact over K, which is why the decompletion is needed.

sources.match: Compactness of restriction to a strictly smaller open after passing to the K-forms of the analytic vectors.

nodes.title: The LB-space structure on H^i(Fl, O^{la,χ})
nodes.statement: Let G_0 = 1 + p²M_2(Z_p), G_n = G_0^{p^n}. The restriction O_{K^p}(U₁) → O_{K^p}(U₁₂) is a closed embedding, hence so is the map on G_n-analytic vectors, and the two-term Čech complex of G_n-analytic vectors (of weight χ) for {U₁, U₂} is strict; its cohomology Ȟ^*(O^{G_n-an,χ}_{K^p}) is a C-Banach space with an analytic G_n-action. The colimit over n is the Čech complex of O^{la,χ}_{K^p}, which computes H^i(Fl, O^{la,χ}_{K^p}); give H^i(Fl, O^{la,χ}) the inductive-limit (LB) topology of colim_n Ȟ^i(O^{G_n-an,χ}). For O^la itself (no weight) the same recipe gives an LB structure on H^i(Fl, O^la_{K^p}) equivalent to that of H^i(Fl, O_{K^p})^la = H̃^i(K^p, C)^la (Pan II Remark 3.4.6); a topology on H^i(Fl, ω^{k,la,χ}) is defined the same way (Remark 3.4.7, not used).
hypotheses: χ integral; the cover {U₁, U₂} of Fl.
Planning gap: closed range and strictness of the analytic weight-χ Čech differential require an independent argument replacing Pan II Lemma 3.4.3; see E2 and the strictness gap.
proofSteps: Injectivity of O(U₁) → O(U₁₂): a kernel element extends to a global section vanishing on U₂, which is SL_2(Q_p)-invariant (H̃⁰ has trivial SL_2-action, Emerton) and SL_2(Q_p)·U₂ = Fl (Pan II Lemma 3.4.2).

The required closed-range and strictness argument at analytic level is unresolved here. Pan II Lemma 3.4.3 cannot supply it as stated: the claimed general involution criterion is false (source issue E2). A replacement using the geometry or additional hypotheses is required before this topology construction is accepted.

Taking G_n-analytic vectors preserves closed embeddings (Pan II Lemma 2.3.2), but this alone does not prove that the sum of the two Čech images is closed. Nor is the weight-χ part automatically a topological direct factor. Prove strictness of the actual weight-χ Čech map separately.

Equivalence with the topology of H̃^i(K^p, C)^la for O^la by strong LA-acyclicity of O_{K^p}(U_i) and of H⁰(Fl, O_{K^p}) (Pan II Remark 3.4.6); the twisted sheaves by the same strictness argument (Remarks 3.4.7–3.4.8).
acceptance: For i = 0 the topology is that of H⁰(Fl, O^{la,χ}) as a subspace of the locally analytic vectors of H̃⁰(K^p, C).

sources.match: Closed embedding of restriction maps, the Weyl-involution strictness criterion, strictness of the Čech complexes of analytic vectors and Definition 3.4.5 of the LB-structure, with its comparison to the other natural topology.

nodes.title: H^i(Fl, O^{la,χ}) is a Hausdorff LB-space with compact transition maps
nodes.statement: (1) H^i(Fl, O^{la,χ}_{K^p}) is a Hausdorff LB-space; the map to H^i(Fl, O_{K^p}) is injective except when i = 1 and χ(h) = 0. (2) In weight (0, 0), the transition maps i_{n,m} on the G_K-invariants of Ȟ¹(O^{G_n-an,(0,0)}) are compact for m large, and ker i_{n,m} stabilises to the kernel of the map to H¹(Fl, O^{la,(0,0)}), a closed subspace. (3) For every n the G_n-analytic vectors of H^i(Fl, O^{la,χ}) lie in the image of Ȟ^i(O^{G_m-an,χ}) for some m ≥ n.
hypotheses: χ integral; the K-forms come from a finite extension K over which the opens of the covers are defined.
proofSteps: Away from i = 1, χ(h) = 0 the target is Banach and the map injective (Pan I Corollary 5.1.3(2)); by twisting with t reduce the remaining case to (0, 0) (Pan II Proposition 3.4.11).

Compactness (Cartan–Serre): by LA.2/cech-cohomology-essentially-zero the image of level n lies in the image from 𝔘′ at level m; on G_K-invariants this persists because the images are Hodge–Tate of weight 0, and restriction along the strict neighbourhood U′₁ ∩ U′₂ ⋑ U₁ ∩ U₂ is compact (LA.3/decompleted-restriction-is-compact); conclude by Pan II Lemma 2.2.5 (Pan II Lemma 3.4.13(1)).

Stabilisation of kernels from the exact sequence (3.4.1) whose extra term is smooth, so finite-dimensional on G_{n+1}-invariants (Pan II Lemma 3.4.13(2)); a compact LB-system with closed stabilising kernels is Hausdorff (Pan II Corollary 2.2.4, imported).
(3) via Proposition 2.1.5 of Pan II applied to the Banach subspace of G_n-analytic vectors (Pan II Proposition 3.4.14).
acceptance: Decompletion of degree-one Čech cohomology: Ȟ¹(O^{G_n-an,(0,0)}) is the C-base change of its G_K-invariants (Pan II Lemma 3.4.12).

sources.match: The cohomology of O^{la,χ} is a Hausdorff LB-space, the degree-one transition maps are compact with stabilising kernels, and analytic vectors come from a finite level.

nodes.title: Smooth automorphic sheaves and classical modular forms at infinite level
nodes.statement: For k ∈ Z let ω^{k,sm}_{K^p} ⊂ π_{HT*}ω^k_{K^p} be the GL_2(Q_p)-smooth sections (equivalently π_{HT*} of colim_{K_p} π_{K_p}^{-1}ω^k). Then H^i(Fl, ω^{k,sm}_{K^p}) ≅ colim_{K_p} H^i(X_{K^pK_p}, ω^k) for all i, H¹(Fl, ω^{k,sm}) = 0 for k ≥ 2, and the stalk colim_{U∋∞} ω^{k,sm}(U) is the space M†_k(K^p) of LA.4/overconvergent-modular-forms. The space of classical modular forms of weight k and tame level K^p is M_k(K^p) := H⁰(Fl, ω^{k,sm}_{K^p}) = colim_{K_p} H⁰(X_{K^pK_p}, ω^k); write M_k = colim_{K^p} M_k(K^p) and H¹(ω^k) = colim_K H¹(X_{K,C}, ω^k), with their GL_2(A_f)-actions.
hypotheses: X_{K^pK_p} are the compactified modular curves over C; ω is the Hodge bundle extended over the cusps.
proofSteps: π_{K_p}: X_{K^p} → X_{K^pK_p} has the property that π_{HT*} of the colimit of pull-backs is computed on 𝔅, where the preimages come from finite level (Pan I Remark 5.3.4).

Compute H^i(Fl, ω^{k,sm}) on the Čech complex of {U₁, U₂}: its terms are colimits of finite-level sections over the preimages, so the cohomology is the colimit of finite-level coherent cohomology (Pan I Lemma 5.3.5).
H¹(X_K, ω^k) = 0 for k ≥ 2 on curves (degree of ω^k exceeds that of the canonical bundle; Pan I Corollary 5.3.6).
Stalk at ∞: neighbourhoods of ∞ in Fl pull back to strict neighbourhoods of the canonical locus (Pan I Lemmas 5.2.8–5.2.9, 5.3.7).
acceptance: For k=0, M_0(K^p)=colim H⁰(X_{K^pK_p},O)=H⁰(Fl,O^sm), the locally constant functions on components. Its inclusion into H⁰(Fl,O^la) identifies the smooth subspace.

sources.locator: Definition 5.3.2, Remarks 5.3.3–5.3.4, Lemma 5.3.5, Corollary 5.3.6, Lemma 5.3.7, Definition 5.3.8, pp. 59–60
sources.match: The smooth subsheaf ω^{k,sm}, its cohomology as the colimit of coherent cohomology at finite level, vanishing of H¹ for k ≥ 2, its stalk at ∞ and the definition of M_k(K^p).
M_k and H¹(ω^k) as colimits over all levels, with their GL_2(A_f)-actions.

nodes.title: Overconvergent modular forms of weight χ at infinite level
nodes.statement: For a weight χ, M†_χ(K^p) := H⁰(Fl, O^{la,χ}_{K^p}/m_∞O^{la,χ}_{K^p}), the fibre of O^{la,χ} at ∞ ∈ Fl, with its actions of G_{Q_p}, the upper triangular Borel B ⊂ GL_2(Q_p) and prime-to-p Hecke operators. For k ∈ Z, M†_k(K^p) := colim_n M†_k(K^pΓ(p^n)), where M†_k(K^pΓ(p^n)) is the space of sections of ω^k on strict neighbourhoods of X_{K^pΓ(p^n),c}, the tube of the non-supersingular points of the Katz–Mazur components indexed by surjections (Z/p^n)² → Z/p^n killing (1, 0); then colim_n M†_k(K^pΓ₁(p^n)) = M†_k(K^p)^{N_0} with N_0 = (1 Z_p; 0 1), and M†_k(K^p) is recovered by inverting diag(p^{-1}, 1). For χ = (n₁, n₂) integral with k = n₁ − n₂, multiplication by e₂^{−k}t^{n₁} is an isomorphism φ_χ: M†_k(K^p) → M†_χ(K^p) with (g₁, g₂)·φ_χ(f) = φ_χ((g₁, g₂)·f) d^{−k} ε_p(ad)^{n₁} ε_p(g₂)^{n₁−k} for g₁ = (a b; 0 d) ∈ B and g₂ ∈ G_{Q_p}.
hypotheses: ∞ ∈ Fl is the point whose Borel is the rational upper-triangular Borel; m_∞ is its maximal ideal sheaf.
proofSteps: The fibre at ∞ is computed from the expansions of LA.2/weight-sheaves on neighbourhoods of ∞, where e₂ is a generator.
Preimages of neighbourhoods of ∞ are strict neighbourhoods of the canonical locus at all levels (Pan I Lemmas 5.2.8–5.2.9), identifying the fibre with sections of ω^k (Pan I Proposition 5.2.6).
Comparison with the classical definitions through the Γ₁(p^n) canonical loci (Pan I §5.2.4, Remark 5.2.13 for other definitions in non-integral weight).
acceptance: Classical forms embed: M_k(K^p) ⊂ M†_k(K^p) (LA.4/smooth-automorphic-sheaves).

sources.locator: Definition 5.2.3, §5.2.4, Definition 5.2.5, Proposition 5.2.6, Remark 5.2.7, Lemmas 5.2.8–5.2.9, Remark 5.2.13, pp. 52–57
sources.match: Overconvergent forms of weight χ as the fibre of O^{la,χ} at ∞, the integral-weight definition by strict neighbourhoods of the canonical locus, the comparison with Γ₁(p^n) and the isomorphism φ_χ with its equivariance.
Overconvergent and classical forms at infinite tame level on strict neighbourhoods of the canonical locus, as used for the n-invariants.

nodes.title: The n-coinvariants of O^{la,χ} are a skyscraper at ∞
nodes.statement: Let χ = (n₁, n₂). (1) (O^{la,χ}_{K^p})_n is a skyscraper sheaf supported at ∞, hence has no H¹. (2) n(O^{la,χ}) ⊂ m_∞O^{la,χ}, giving an exact sequence 0 → (i_∞)_*N_χ → (O^{la,χ})_n → (i_∞)_*M†_χ(K^p) → 0, on whose kernel h acts by (n₂ + 1, n₁ − 1); it splits naturally if χ(h) ≠ 1. (3) N_χ = 0 if χ(h) ∉ {0, −1, −2, …} and χ(h) is p-adically non-Liouville. (4) If χ(h) ∈ {0, −1, −2, …}, (O^{la,χ})_n ≅ (i_∞)_*M†_χ ⊕ (i_∞)_*M†_χ·(e₁/e₂)^{1−χ(h)}.
hypotheses: n = C·u₊ is the nilradical of the rational Borel; non-Liouville in Clark's sense.
proofSteps: Away from ∞, u₊ acts on expansions in x by ∂/∂x up to units, which is surjective; so the coinvariants vanish off ∞ (Pan I Proposition 5.2.10(1)).

At ∞ use the coordinate 1/x with e₂ a generator; u₊ acts by a first-order operator with weight shift, whose cokernel is computed coefficientwise; the Liouville condition controls division by χ(h) + j (Pan I Proposition 5.2.10(2)–(4), Remark 5.2.11).

sources.match: Structure of the n-coinvariants of O^{la,χ}: a skyscraper at ∞ built from overconvergent forms, with the extra summand for nonpositive integral χ(h) and its vanishing for non-Liouville weights.

nodes.title: Local form of the n-invariants of O^{la,χ}
nodes.statement: (1) If ∞ ∉ U (e₁ a generator) and N is large, every f ∈ O^{la,χ,n}(U) is (t/t_N)^{n₁}(e₁/e_{1,N})^{n₂−n₁}c with c at finite level G_{r(n)}. (2) If e₂ generates on U ∈ 𝔅 and χ(h) ∈ {0, −1, −2, …}, every f ∈ O^{la,χ,n}(U) is (t/t_N)^{n₁}(e₁/e_{2,N})^{n₂−n₁}c with c at finite level. (3) h acts on O^{la,χ,n}(U) by (n₂, n₁) for every open U. (4) If χ(h) ∉ {0, −1, −2, …} the stalk of O^{la,χ,n} at ∞ is zero. Consequently, for χ(h) = k ≥ 2, multiplication by t^{−n₁}e₁^k gives an exact sequence 0 → O^{la,χ,n} → ω^{k,sm} → (i_∞)_*M†_k(K^p) → 0.
hypotheses: χ integral for (2) and the consequence.
proofSteps: n-invariance kills all positive powers of x − x_n in the expansion of LA.2/weight-sheaves (Pan I Proposition 5.2.12(1)–(2)).
Weights from θ_h on the leading coefficient (Pan I Proposition 5.2.12(3)); at ∞ the polynomial in 1/x cannot be n-invariant unless χ(h) is a nonpositive integer (5.2.12(4)).
The exact sequence: off ∞ the map is an isomorphism onto ω^{k,sm}, and the cokernel is the stalk of ω^{k,sm} at ∞ (Pan I §5.3.10).
acceptance: Taking cohomology for k ≥ 2 gives H¹(Fl, O^{la,χ,n}) ≅ M†_k(K^p)/M_k(K^p) (Pan I §5.3.10).

sources.match: The n-invariant sections of O^{la,χ} come from finite level after twisting by t and e-powers, carry weight (n₂, n₁), and vanish at ∞ for nonintegral or positive χ(h); for k ≥ 2 they embed into ω^{k,sm} with cokernel M†_k at ∞.

nodes.title: n-coinvariants and n-invariants of H¹(Fl, O^{la,χ}) in general weight
nodes.statement: Let χ = (n₁, n₂); (−)_n denotes n-coinvariants and (−)^n n-invariants. (1) The n-coinvariants vanish: (H¹(Fl, O^la)^χ)_n = H¹(Fl, O^{la,χ})_n = 0 if χ(h) ≠ 0. (2) If χ(h) ≠ 0, 1 there is a natural Hecke-equivariant weight decomposition of C[B]-modules of the n-invariants H¹(Fl, O^la)^{χ,n} = H¹(Fl, O^{la,χ})^n = (M†_χ(K^p) ⊗_C n*) ⊕ W₂, where M†_χ ⊗ n* has weight (n₁ − 1, n₂ + 1) and W₂ has weight (n₂, n₁).
hypotheses: n has dimension one, so H⁰(n, −) = (−)^n and H¹(n, −) = (−)_n ⊗ n* are the only n-cohomology groups.
proofSteps: Apply n-cohomology to 0 → O^{la,χ}(U₁) ⊕ O^{la,χ}(U₂) → O^{la,χ}(U₁₂) → H¹(Fl, O^{la,χ}) → 0 (Pan I footnote 3, p. 52); the coinvariants H¹(Fl, O^{la,χ})_n = H¹(Fl, (O^{la,χ})_n) vanish since the coinvariant sheaf is a skyscraper (Pan I proof of Theorem 5.2.15).
Use LA.4/n-coinvariants-at-infinity and LA.4/n-invariants-local, with the weights to separate the two pieces (Pan I §5.2.1, Theorem 5.2.15, Remark 5.2.14).
acceptance: Weight bookkeeping: the two weights (n₁ − 1, n₂ + 1) and (n₂, n₁) are exchanged by the dot action of the Weyl element, as Harish-Chandra predicts for a module with infinitesimal character.

sources.match: n-coinvariants vanish for χ(h) ≠ 0, and the n-invariants of H¹ split into overconvergent forms of weight χ twisted by n* and a second piece of the Weyl-reflected weight.

nodes.title: n-invariants of H¹ in integral weight
nodes.statement: Let χ = (n₁, n₂) be integral and k = χ(h) = n₁ − n₂. All maps are Hecke- and B × G_{Q_p}-equivariant. (k ≥ 2) H¹(Fl, O^la)^{χ,n} = H¹(Fl, O^{la,χ})^n = M†_k(K^p)·e₁^{−1}e₂^{−k+1}t^{n₁} ⊕ (M†_k(K^p)/M_k(K^p))·e₁^{−k}t^{n₁}. (k ≤ −1) H¹(Fl, O^{la,χ})^n = M†_k(K^p)·e₁^{−1}e₂^{−k+1}t^{n₁} ⊕ N_{k,1}·e₁^{−k}t^{n₁} with 0 → colim_{K_p} H¹(X_{K^pK_p}, ω^k) → N_{k,1} → M†_k(K^p) → 0. (k = 0) the n-coinvariants (H¹(Fl, O^la)^χ)_n vanish and the n-invariants are H¹(Fl, O^la)^{χ,n} = N_{2,w}·e₁^{−1}e₂t^{n₁} ⊕ N_{0,1}·t^{n₁} with 0 → M†_0/M_0 → N_{2,w} → M_0 → 0 and 0 → colim H¹(X_{K^pK_p}, O) → N_{0,1} → M†_0/M_0 → 0. (k = 1) there is an exact sequence 0 → N₁·e₁^{−1}t^{n₁} → H¹(Fl, O^la)^{χ,n} → M†_1(K^p)·e₁^{−1}t^{n₁} → 0 with 0 → M†_1/M_1 → N₁ → colim H¹(X_{K^pK_p}, ω) → 0, and the weight-(n₁ − 1, n₁) part is the pull-back of M_1(K^p)·e₁^{−1}t^{n₁}.
hypotheses: χ integral; the twists ·e₁^ae₂^bt^c record the B × G_{Q_p}-action as in Pan I Remark 5.2.7.
proofSteps: Reduce to n₁ = 0 by twisting with t^{−n₁} (Pan I §5.3.9).
k ≥ 2: H¹ of the exact sequence of LA.4/n-invariants-local with H¹(ω^{k,sm}) = 0 (Pan I §5.3.10, Theorem 5.3.11).
k ≤ −1: the same with H⁰(ω^{k,sm}) = 0 and H¹(ω^{k,sm}) = colim H¹(X, ω^k) (Pan I Theorem 5.3.13).
k = 0: compute via F = n(O^{la,0}) and the sequence (5.3.1) from LA.2/cohomology-of-weight-sheaves, tracking the image of M_0 (Pan I Proposition 5.3.15, Theorem 5.3.16).
k = 1: ω^{1,sm} has both H⁰ and H¹ (Pan I §5.3.17, Theorem 5.3.18).
acceptance: For k ≥ 2 the overconvergent part M†_k/M_k is the quotient by classical forms, matching Coleman's classicality: on finite-slope U_p-eigenspaces of small slope it vanishes.

sources.match: Complete determination of the n-cohomology of H¹(Fl, O^{la,χ}) for integral weights in the four ranges k ≥ 2, k ≤ −1, k = 0, k = 1, in terms of classical, overconvergent and coherent H¹ terms.

nodes.title: The μ-isotypic decomposition of H̃¹(K^p, C)^la (p-adic Shimura isomorphism)
nodes.statement: Let μ = (k₁, k₂) ∈ h*, viewed as a character of b, and k := −μ(h) ≠ 1. There is a natural decomposition H̃¹(K^p, C)^la_μ = M_{μ,1} ⊕ M_{μ,w} into pieces of Hodge–Tate–Sen weights −k₁ and 1 − k₂, with M_{μ,w} = M†_{μ+2ρ}(K^p) ⊗_C n* unless k = 2. If k ∈ Z, writing M_{μ,1} = N_{k,1}·e₁^{−k}t^{k₂} and M_{μ,w} = N_{k,w}·e₁^{−1}e₂^{k−1}t^{k₁+1}: (1) N_{k,w} ≅ M†_{2−k}(K^p) for k ≠ 2, and 0 → M†_0/M_0 → N_{2,w} → M_0 → 0; (2) for k ≤ −1, 0 → colim_{K_p} H¹(X_{K^pK_p}, ω^k) → N_{k,1} → M†_k(K^p) → 0; (3) for k = 0, 0 → colim H¹(X_{K^pK_p}, O) → N_{0,1} → M†_0/M_0 → 0; (4) for k ≥ 2, N_{k,1} ≅ M†_k(K^p)/M_k(K^p). All maps are Hecke- and B × G_{Q_p}-equivariant. Passing to the colimit over K^p gives Pan I Theorem 1.0.1: H̃¹(C)^la_{μ_k} = N_{k,1}·e₁^{−k}t^k ⊕ N_{k,w}(k − 1)·e₁^{−1}e₂^{k−1}t for μ_k(a b; 0 d) = kd.
hypotheses: k ≠ 1; for k ∉ Z only the M_{μ,w} half is identified (Pan I Theorem 5.4.2 and p. 4).
proofSteps: The μ-isotypic part for b lies in the n-invariants (μ kills n) and is cut out there by the h-weights: θ_h and the infinitesimal action are related by Harish-Chandra (LA.1/horizontal-cartan-action) (Pan I §5.4.1).
Since θ_h(diag(0, 1)) is the Sen operator (LA.3/theta-h-is-the-sen-operator), the decomposition by θ_h-weights is a Hodge–Tate–Sen decomposition.
Read off the pieces from LA.4/n-cohomology-general-weight and LA.4/n-cohomology-integral-weight (Pan I Theorem 5.4.2).
acceptance: For k = 0 (μ = 0) the weight-0 piece contains colim H¹(X, O), the classical H¹ of the structure sheaf, as in the complex Eichler–Shimura decomposition.

sources.match: The Hodge–Tate–Sen decomposition of the μ-isotypic part of the locally analytic completed cohomology into overconvergent and classical pieces, a p-adic analogue of the Shimura isomorphism.

nodes.title: The singular weight μ(h) = −1 and the nilpotent Sen operator
nodes.statement: Let μ = (k₁, k₁ + 1), so μ(h) = −1. There is an exact sequence 0 → N₁·e₁^{−1}t^{k₁+1} → H̃¹(K^p, C)^la_μ → M†_1(K^p)·e₁^{−1}t^{k₁+1} → 0 with 0 → M†_1/M_1 → N₁ → colim_{K_p} H¹(X_{K^pK_p}, ω) → 0; the weight-(k₁ + 1, k₁) part H̃¹(K^p, C)^{la,(k₁+1,k₁)}_μ is the pull-back of M_1(K^p)·e₁^{−1}t^{k₁+1}. On H̃¹(K^p, C)^la_μ the shifted operator Θ_Sen − k₁ is square-zero. In the normalisation k₁ = 0, Θ_Sen factors through M†_1·e₁^{−1}t and maps it by the quotient map into (M†_1/M_1)·e₁^{−1}t ⊂ N₁·e₁^{−1}t; general k₁ is obtained by the locally analytic character twist of Pan I §5.3.9. Passing to the colimit over K^p, (H̃¹(C)^la_{μ₁})^{G_{Q_p}} lies in H̃¹(C)^{la,(1,0)}_{μ₁} (Pan I Theorem 1.0.2).
hypotheses: μ(h) = −1, the singular weight where Hodge–Tate–Sen weights coincide.
proofSteps: θ_h(h) − 1 = −(h + 1) on the n-part of the auxiliary sheaf F₂ of §5.4.3 (Pan I Lemma 5.4.4); compute the kernels as in §5.4.5.
Combine with LA.4/n-cohomology-integral-weight in the case k = 1 (Pan I Theorem 5.4.6).
Untwist μ = (k₁,k₁+1) to μ₁ = (0,1) using Pan I §5.3.9, pp. 60–61. Twisting changes the Sen operator by the scalar k₁; only Θ_Sen − k₁ is nilpotent in general (Theorem 1.0.2, p. 4).
acceptance: The extension does not split in general, reflecting non-Hodge–Tate representations with equal Hodge–Tate–Sen weights.

sources.match: The μ-isotypic part for μ(h) = −1 as an extension of overconvergent weight-one forms by N₁, the identification of the weight-(k₁+1, k₁) part with the classical pull-back, and the nilpotent Sen operator in the normalisation k₁ = 0, and its shifted version for general μ.

nodes.title: Pro-modular and pro-cohomological Galois representations
nodes.statement: Let T(K^p) be the big Hecke algebra of tame level K^p acting on completed cohomology, D_S its two-dimensional Galois determinant and, for a Z_p-algebra map λ: T(K^p) → Q̄_p, ρ_λ: G_{Q,S} → GL_2(Q̄_p) the attached semisimple odd representation (tr ρ_λ(Frob_l) = λ(T_l)l^{−1}, det ρ_λ = λ∘D_S) and p_λ = ker(λ ⊗ Q̄_p). A continuous ρ: G_Q → GL_2(Q̄_p) is pro-modular if ρ ≅ ρ_λ for some K^p and λ, and pro-cohomological if Hom_{G_Q}(ρ(−1), H̃¹(K^p, Q̄_p)) ≠ 0 for some K^p. An irreducible pro-cohomological ρ is pro-modular; for irreducible pro-modular ρ = ρ_λ the following are equivalent: ρ is pro-cohomological; H̃¹(K^p, Q̄_p)[p_λ] ≠ 0; H̃¹(K^p, C)[p_λ] ≠ 0. Moreover H̃¹(K^p, Q̄_p)[p_λ] ⊗̂ C ≅ H̃¹(K^p, C)[p_λ], and H̃¹(K^p, Q̄_p)[p_λ] = ρ_λ(−1) ⊗ Hom_{G_Q}(ρ_λ(−1), H̃¹(K^p, Q̄_p)) (Boston–Lenstra–Ribet), with the centre A_f^× acting through det(ρ_λ)ε^{−1}.
hypotheses: S is a finite set of primes containing p with K^p = K_SK^S, K^S hyperspecial.
proofSteps: The Hecke algebra and its determinant are imported (R31.3, CC.8).
Eichler–Shimura relation and Boston–Lenstra–Ribet give the ρ_λ(−1)-isotypic decomposition (Pan I §6.1.1).
Lemma 6.1.4: choose generators g_1, …, g_s of p_λ; 0 → H̃¹[p_λ] → H̃¹ → ⊕H̃¹ is strict, so it stays exact after completed tensor product with C (Pan I Lemmas 6.1.3–6.1.4).
acceptance: The representation attached to a cuspidal eigenform of weight k ≥ 2 and tame level K^p is pro-modular and pro-cohomological (its system of eigenvalues occurs in classical cohomology).

sources.match: The big Hecke algebra, the Galois representations ρ_λ, the definitions of pro-modular and pro-cohomological representations, and the equivalent nonvanishing conditions with the completed tensor comparison.

api.name: ProModular
