nodes.title: Infinitesimal character of the locally analytic eigenspaces
nodes.statement: Let ρ = ρ_λ be pro-cohomological and irreducible with Hodge–Tate–Sen weights (a, b) at p. Then H̃¹(K^p, C)^la[p_λ] ≠ 0, and as a representation of GL_2(Q_p) it has infinitesimal character {(−a − 1, −b), (−b − 1, −a)} ⊂ h* (an orbit for the dot action).
hypotheses: Hodge–Tate–Sen weights in Pan's convention (cyclotomic weight −1).
proofSteps: ρ is defined over a finite E; H̃¹(K^p, Q_p)[p_λ] ∩ H̃¹ ⊗ E is a nonzero admissible representation, so it has nonzero locally analytic vectors (Schneider–Teitelbaum, imported).
det ρ has Hodge–Tate–Sen weight a + b, so the centre acts by z ↦ −(a + b) − 1.
The relation between θ_h, Z(U(g)) and the Sen operator (LA.1/horizontal-cartan-action, LA.3/theta-h-is-the-sen-operator) determines the infinitesimal character (Pan I Proposition 6.1.5).
acceptance: For ρ attached to an eigenform of weight k + 1 (weights 0, k), the infinitesimal character is {(−1, −k), (−k − 1, 0)}, that of (Sym^{k−1} of the dual of the standard representation) up to the twist, as in Pan II §1.2.2.

sources.match: Nonvanishing and infinitesimal character of the locally analytic λ-eigenspace, from Schneider–Teitelbaum, the centre and the Sen interpretation of θ_h; compare Dospinescu–Paškūnas–Schraen.

nodes.title: Classicality of weight-one overconvergent eigensystems with a U_p-eigenvector
nodes.statement: Let ρ = ρ_λ be pro-modular of tame level K^p. If M†_1(K^p)^{N_0}[p_λ] contains a nonzero U_p-eigenvector and ρ|G_{Q_p} is Hodge–Tate of weights 0, 0, then ρ comes from a classical weight-one eigenform: M_1(K^p)[p_λ] ≠ 0. The theorem allows U_p-eigenvalue zero. Its finite-slope special case has nonzero U_p-eigenvalue by definition.
hypotheses: ρ_λ|G_{Q_p} Hodge–Tate with weights 0, 0; a nonzero U_p-eigenvector in the N_0-invariants of M†_1(K^p)[p_λ].
proofSteps: If ρ is reducible, finite-order characters give the required classical Eisenstein eigensystem. For irreducible ρ normalise the tame level to Γ₁-type level and extend λ to λ′ including the bad-prime operators and U_p (Pan I §6.2.4 and Lemma 6.2.5).

The q-expansion recurrence for a simultaneous λ′-eigenvector determines its coefficients from a₁; the rigid analytic identity principle on each component and the action on components give dimension one in the chosen ψ-part of M†₁ at Γ₁(p^n)-level (Pan I Lemma 6.2.6). This needs the overconvergent q-expansion contract below.

Assume M₁[p_λ] = 0. Semisimplicity gives M₁ localised at p_λ equal to zero, and Serre duality with logarithmic Kodaira–Spencer then gives H¹(ω) localised at p_λ equal to zero. These are the finite-level coherent inputs in the R15.1 request.

Set λ_t(T_l)=l^{−1}λ(T_l) and μ₁=(0,1). LA.4/weight-one-isotypic-part, after localising at λ_t, identifies the weight-(1,0) part with M†₁[p_λ]·e₁^{−1}t under the preceding vanishing assumption. Hodge–Tate weights 0,0 force the entire μ₁-part to have this weight. Boston–Lenstra–Ribet gives a tensor factor ρ of dimension two, contradicting the one-dimensional simultaneous λ′-eigenspace (Pan I pp. 70–71).
acceptance: In the ordinary case this recovers Buzzard–Taylor's classicality theorem (Pan I Remark 6.2.3).

sources.locator: Theorem 6.2.2, Remark 6.2.3, §6.2.4, Lemmas 6.2.5–6.2.6 and the end of §6.2, pp. 69–71; proof sketch after Theorem 1.0.3, p. 5
sources.match: Classicality of a pro-modular Hodge–Tate weight-(0,0) eigensystem admitting a U_p-eigenvector in weight-one overconvergent forms, by a multiplicity-one comparison through the weight-one isotypic decomposition.

nodes.title: Weak local–global compatibility for completed H¹, including Eisenstein maximal ideals
nodes.statement: Fix K^p, a finite extension E/Q_p with ring O, a central character ζ and a maximal ideal m of T(K^p) ⊗ O with block 𝔅_m. Then H̃¹(K^p, E/O)_{ζ′,m} lies in Mod^{ladm}_{G,ζ}(O)[𝔅_m], so the pseudodeformation ring R^{ps,ζε_p}_{ρ̄_{m,p}} acts on it through the Bernstein centre of the block (τ_p), and this action agrees with the action through the global Hecke algebra and the Galois determinant (τ′_p). Consequently, for ρ = ρ_λ pro-modular and irreducible, H̃¹(K^p, Q̄_p)[p_λ] ≠ 0 (ρ is pro-cohomological) and: if ρ|G_{Q_p} is irreducible, H̃¹(K^p, Q̄_p)[p_λ] ≅ Π(ρ|G_{Q_p})^{⊕d} for some d; if ρ|G_{Q_p} is reducible, H̃¹(K^p, Q̄_p)[p_λ] has an ordinary subrepresentation.
hypotheses: E is enlarged so that m has residue field F and the reduction of the Galois determinant at p comes from a semisimple ρ̄_{m,p}; 𝔅_m is the block attached to ρ̄_{m,p} by the semisimple mod p correspondence, hence a block containing an absolutely irreducible representation, to which Paškūnas–Tung (Pan I Theorem 6.3.3) applies.
ζ′ is a character of A_f^×/det(K^p)Q_{>0}^× whose restriction ζ to Q_p^× is congruent to (det ρ̄_{m,p})ω^{−1}; H̃¹(K^p, −)_{ζ′,m} is the part localised at m on which the centre acts by ζ′.
proofSteps: Import Paškūnas–Tung's map R^{ps} → Z_𝔅 and the faithful exact functor m (Pan I Theorem 6.3.3).
Compare the two R^{ps}-actions on H̃¹_{ζ′,m} using density of GL_2(Z_p)-algebraic vectors and semisimplicity of the Hecke action on them (Pan I Theorem 6.3.5, Lemmas 6.3.8–6.3.9).
Deduce the description of the λ-eigenspace via the Colmez–Dospinescu–Paškūnas bijection (Pan I Corollary 6.3.6, Remark 6.3.7).
acceptance: For m non-Eisenstein this is a weak form of Emerton's local–global compatibility (R31.4); the point of Pan I §6.3 is that it holds after localising at an Eisenstein m.

sources.match: Generalisation of Emerton's local–global compatibility to possibly Eisenstein maximal ideals through Paškūnas–Tung, and its consequence for the λ-eigenspaces of completed H¹.

nodes.title: Nonzero N_0-invariant locally analytic vectors killed by U_p
nodes.statement: Let Π be an irreducible admissible unitary Banach representation of GL_2(Q_p) over a finite extension of Q_p. Then Π^{la,N_0} ≠ 0 and contains a nonzero U_p-eigenvector. For Π = Π(V) attached to a two-dimensional absolutely irreducible V this follows from Colmez's P-equivariant embedding C_c(Q_p^×, D⁻_dif(V))^Γ → Π(V)^la_E: its N_0-invariants contain nonzero vectors annihilated by U_p.
hypotheses: Π irreducible admissible unitary; the ordinary and finite-dimensional cases are treated directly.
proofSteps: Import Colmez's Kirillov model (Pan I Theorem 6.4.3) and compute N_0-invariants of compactly supported functions (Pan I Corollary 6.4.4, Remark 6.4.5).
For the other irreducible Π (characters and ordinary Π) compute directly (Pan I Corollary 6.4.6).
acceptance: A U_p-eigenvector of eigenvalue 0 occurs, which is why Theorem 6.2.2 does not assume a nonzero eigenvalue.

sources.match: Colmez's Kirillov model gives nonzero U_p-eigenvectors (even in the kernel of U_p) among the N_0-invariant locally analytic vectors of irreducible admissible unitary Banach representations.

nodes.title: Hodge–Tate pro-modular representations of weights 0, 0 are classical of weight one
nodes.statement: Let ρ = ρ_λ be pro-modular and irreducible with ρ|G_{Q_p} Hodge–Tate of weights 0, 0. Then ρ is classical: M_1(K^p)[p_λ] ≠ 0 for some tame level K^p.
hypotheses: ρ irreducible, pro-modular; Hodge–Tate (not merely Hodge–Tate–Sen) of weights 0, 0 at p.
proofSteps: By LA.5/local-global-compatibility-at-eisenstein-ideals, H̃¹(K^p, Q̄_p)[p_λ] is a sum of copies of Π(ρ|G_{Q_p}) or has an ordinary subrepresentation.

First twist λ by t and use LA.5/infinitesimal-character-of-eigenspaces to select μ₁=(0,1). In that isotypic part, the weight-one decomposition and Hodge–Tate weights 0,0 put the locally analytic vectors in weight (1,0). Apply the Kirillov-model U_p-eigenvector argument inside this part; the map to M†₁·e₁^{−1}t gives the required eigenvector (Pan I proof of Theorem 6.4.7, p. 77).
Apply LA.5/weight-one-classicality-with-up-eigenvector (Pan I Theorem 6.4.7; Remark 6.4.12 sketches a second proof in the nonordinary case).
acceptance: Conversely the representation of a classical weight-one eigenform is Hodge–Tate of weights 0, 0 at p (Deligne–Serre), so the theorem characterises them among pro-modular ρ.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.4.7 with proof and Remark 6.4.12, pp. 77–79; Theorem 1.0.4, p. 5
sources.match: Every irreducible pro-modular ρ that is Hodge–Tate of weights 0, 0 at p comes from a classical weight-one eigenform.

nodes.title: The Fontaine–Mazur conjecture in the irregular case
nodes.statement: Let p > 2 and ρ: G_Q → GL_2(Q̄_p) continuous, irreducible and odd, unramified outside finitely many primes, with ρ̄|G_{Q(μ_p)} irreducible and (ρ̄|G_{Q_p})^{ss} either irreducible or η₁ ⊕ η₂ with η₁/η₂ ≠ 1, ω^{±1}. Then ρ is pro-modular; if moreover ρ|G_{Q_p} is Hodge–Tate of weights 0, 0, then ρ is the representation attached to a classical cuspidal eigenform of weight one, and in particular has finite image.
hypotheses: p > 2; ρ odd; the two residual conditions of Emerton's promodularity theorem.
proofSteps: Pro-modularity is Emerton's Theorem 1.2.3 (imported from R31.6; Pan I Theorem 6.4.8).
Apply LA.5/weight-one-classicality (Pan I Corollary 6.4.9).
Finite image by Deligne–Serre (R19.1/weight-one-artin-representation).
acceptance: Pilloni–Stroh proved this earlier by other means (Pan I Remark 1.0.6); the conditions could be relaxed via promodularity over totally real fields (Remark 6.4.10).

sources.locator: Theorem 6.4.8, Corollary 6.4.9, Remark 6.4.10, p. 78; Theorem 1.0.5 and Remark 1.0.6, pp. 5–6
sources.match: Promodularity under Emerton's hypotheses and the resulting proof of the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture for Hodge–Tate weights 0, 0.

nodes.title: Gouvêa's conjecture: Hodge–Tate–Sen weights of overconvergent eigenforms
nodes.statement: Let ρ = ρ_λ be irreducible and pro-modular of tame level K^p with Hodge–Tate–Sen weights a, b at p. (1) If M†_{(n₁,n₂)}(K^p)[p_λ] ≠ 0 then (n₁, n₂) = (−a, −b − 1) or (−b, −a − 1); in particular if M†_k(K^p)[p_λ] ≠ 0 for some k ∈ Z then {a, b} = {0, k − 1}. (2) Conversely, if ρ|G_{Q_p} is irreducible, then M†_{(n₁,n₂)}(K^p)[p_λ] ≠ 0 for (n₁, n₂) = (−a, −b − 1) and (−b, −a − 1).
hypotheses: For (2), ρ|G_{Q_p} irreducible (so that the Kirillov-model input applies).
proofSteps: (1): an eigenvector in M†_χ gives, through LA.4/hodge-tate-decomposition-of-isotypic-parts, a vector of H̃¹(C)^la[p_λ] of known θ_h-weight; compare with the infinitesimal character of LA.5/infinitesimal-character-of-eigenspaces and the Sen interpretation.

(2): local–global compatibility gives Π(ρ|G_{Q_p}) inside H̃¹[p_λ], and the Kirillov model gives N_0-invariant locally analytic vectors of the right weights, which LA.4/hodge-tate-decomposition-of-isotypic-parts places in M†_χ (Pan I Theorem 6.4.11).

For the converse do not apply only the regular μ-decomposition: when the two Sen weights coincide use the singular weight-one decomposition; when their difference is one use the k=0,2 exceptional exact sequences. The M₀ terms have abelian Galois eigensystems, so irreducibility excludes them. The Kirillov-model vectors therefore survive in the asserted M† spaces (Pan I proof of Theorem 6.4.11, pp. 78–79).
acceptance: For a classical eigenform of weight k ≥ 2 the Hodge–Tate weights are 0, k − 1, consistent with (1) (Pan I Remark 1.0.8; Howe obtained the easier direction independently).

sources.locator: Theorem 6.4.11, p. 78; Theorem 1.0.7 and Remark 1.0.8, p. 6
sources.match: The Hodge–Tate–Sen weights of the Galois representation of an overconvergent eigenform of weight k are 0, k − 1, with a converse when ρ|G_{Q_p} is irreducible.

nodes.title: The de Rham bundle at finite and infinite level, with Kodaira–Spencer
nodes.statement: Let D be the canonical extension to the compactified modular curve X = X_{K^pK_p} of the relative H¹_dR of the universal elliptic curve, with Hodge filtration Fil¹D = ω, gr⁰D = ∧²D ⊗ ω^{−1}, and logarithmic Gauss–Manin connection ∇: D → D ⊗ Ω¹_X(C) (C the cusps). Kodaira–Spencer: the composite ω → D → D ⊗ Ω¹_X(C) → gr⁰D ⊗ Ω¹_X(C) is an isomorphism, i.e. ω² ⊗ (∧²D)^{−1} ≅ Ω¹_X(C). Since D is compatible with change of K_p, D^sm_{K^p} := π_{HT*}colim_{K_p}π_{K_p}^{-1}D is a locally free O^sm_{K^p}-module on Fl with Fil¹ = ω^{1,sm}_{K^p} and a connection into D^sm ⊗ Ω¹_{K^p}(C)^sm (Ω¹_{K^p}(C)^sm the colimit of log differentials), and Kodaira–Spencer gives ω^{2,sm} ⊗ (∧²D^sm)^{−1} ≅ Ω¹_{K^p}(C)^sm. The line bundle ∧²D^sm_{K^p} is trivial but not Hecke-equivariantly; D₀ := H⁰(Fl, ∧²D^sm_{K^p}) is free of rank one over M_0(K^p), with GL_2(A_f) acting on a generator through the inverse adelic norm of the determinant.
hypotheses: K = K^pK_p neat; D is Deligne's canonical extension of the relative H¹_dR, which carries a logarithmic connection (Pan II §4.1.2).
proofSteps: Import the relative de Rham bundle (A4), its canonical extension with log connection (B3) and the log Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism (R15.1) (Pan II §4.1.2).
Pull back to all finite levels, take the colimit and push forward along π_HT (Pan II §4.1.3).
D₀ and the adelic action: a global horizontal invertible section of ∧²D exists at each finite level and transforms by |det|^{−1} (Pan II Definition 4.4.11).
acceptance: For k = 0 the operator θ₁ built from it (LA.6/theta-operators) is the derivation d: O_X → Ω¹_X(C) composed with Kodaira–Spencer.

sources.match: The canonical extension D with Hodge filtration and Gauss–Manin connection, the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism, and the smooth de Rham bundle D^sm_{K^p} on Fl.
D₀ = H⁰(Fl, ∧²D^sm_{K^p}), free of rank one over M_0(K^p) with the inverse adelic norm action.

nodes.title: The characteristic-zero theta operators θ'_{k+1} and θ_{k+1}
nodes.statement: For k ≥ 0, Kodaira–Spencer makes Fil¹Sym^kD → Sym^kD ⊗ Ω¹_X(C) → (Sym^kD/Fil^k) ⊗ Ω¹_X(C) an isomorphism, so every section s of gr⁰Sym^kD = ω^{−k} ⊗ (∧²D)^k has a unique lift s̃ ∈ Sym^kD with ∇_k(s̃) ∈ Fil^kSym^kD ⊗ Ω¹_X(C) = ω^k ⊗ Ω¹_X(C). This defines θ'_{k+1}: ω^{−k} ⊗ (∧²D)^k → ω^k ⊗ Ω¹_X(C), a logarithmic differential operator of order k + 1; applied to Sym^kD^* it gives θ_{k+1}: ω^{−k} → ω^{k+2} ⊗ (∧²D)^{−k−1}. Both are compatible with change of level and define operators on ω^{−k,sm}_{K^p} and on M†_{−k}(K^p) → M†_{k+2}(K^p) ⊗ D₀^{−k−1}.
hypotheses: k ≥ 0; characteristic zero.
proofSteps: Unique lift by the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism (Pan II §4.1.2).
Order k + 1: in a local coordinate the lift involves k derivatives and ∇_k one more.
Pass to the colimit over K_p and to stalks at ∞ (overconvergent forms).
acceptance: θ₁ = d followed by Kodaira–Spencer; on q-expansions θ_{k+1} is a nonzero multiple of (q d/dq)^{k+1}, Bol's identity.

sources.match: Construction of θ'_{k+1} and θ_{k+1} from Kodaira–Spencer and the Gauss–Manin connection on Sym^kD; θ₁ is the derivation.

nodes.title: The differential operator d_{k+1} along the modular curve
nodes.statement: Let χ = (n₁, n₂) be integral with k = n₂ − n₁ ≥ 0. There is a unique natural continuous operator d_{k+1}: O^{la,χ}_{K^p} → ω^{2k+2,la,χ}_{K^p} ⊗ (∧²D^sm)^{−k−1} = O^{la,χ}_{K^p} ⊗_{O^sm} (Ω¹_{K^p}(C)^sm)^{⊗(k+1)} such that (1) d_{k+1} is O_Fl-linear and (2) d_{k+1}(t^{n₁}e₁^ie₂^{k−i}s) = t^{n₁}e₁^ie₂^{k−i}θ_{k+1}(s) for every smooth s of ω^{−k,sm}_{K^p} and 0 ≤ i ≤ k. It commutes with GL_2(Q_p) and prime-to-p Hecke operators. Twisting by ω_Fl^{−k}(−k) gives the equivalent d′_{k+1}: ω^{−k,la,χ′} → ω^{k+2,la,χ′} ⊗ (∧²D^sm)^{−k−1}, χ′ = (n₁, n₁), with d′_{k+1}(t^{n₁}s) = t^{n₁}θ_{k+1}(s). For k = 0, d₁: O^{la,(0,0)} → O^{la,(0,0)} ⊗_{O^sm} Ω^{1,sm}_{K^p}(C) is the unique continuous O_Fl-linear extension of the derivation d of O^sm. The surjection Sym^kD^{*,(0,0)} → ω^{−k,la,(0,0)} has a unique continuous section r_k with ∇_k∘r_k landing in Fil^k ⊗ Ω¹.
hypotheses: χ integral with n₂ − n₁ = k ≥ 0.
proofSteps: k = 0, locally: on U ∈ 𝔅 with e₁ a generator and f = t^{n₁}Σc_i(x − x_n)^i ∈ A_n, set d_n(f) = t^{n₁}(Σ(x − x_n)^i dc_i − Σ(i + 1)c_{i+1}(x − x_n)^i dx_n); continuity of d bounds p^{(n−1)i}dc_i, and compatibility of d_{n+1}|_{A_n} with d_n follows after passing to a smaller radius where polynomial truncations converge (Pan II proof of Theorem 4.1.4).
O_Fl-linearity: commutes with polynomials in x on U₁ = Spa C⟨x⟩, then with O_Fl(U₁) by continuity, and with rational subdomains by density of C⟨x⟩[1/g].

General k: on D^{χ′} = D^sm ⊗ O^{la,χ′} extend the filtration, use d₁ to build ∇_{χ′} whose Kodaira–Spencer composite is an isomorphism, and repeat the construction of θ_{k+1} on Sym^k of the dual (Pan II proof of Theorem 4.1.4, Remark 4.1.5).

The map r:f↦(f mod Fil¹,∇_kf mod Fil^k) is an isomorphism by Kodaira–Spencer and a topological isomorphism on the Banach coefficient pieces by open mapping. The required section is r_k(f)=r⁻¹(f,0), hence continuous; no isometry is asserted (Pan II Lemma 4.1.6).
acceptance: Uniqueness: two O_Fl-linear continuous extensions agree on the dense image of O^sm ⊗ O_Fl (LA.6/smooth-tensor-flag-is-dense).

sources.locator: Theorem 4.1.4, Remark 4.1.5, proof pp. 35–36, Lemma 4.1.6, p. 37; Theorem 1.2.7(1), p. 8
sources.match: Existence and uniqueness of the O_Fl-linear operator d_{k+1} extending θ_{k+1}, its local formula for k = 0, the twisted d′_{k+1} and the canonical continuous splitting r_k.

nodes.title: The differential operator d̄_{k+1} along the flag variety
nodes.statement: Ω¹_Fl ≅ ω_Fl^{−2} ⊗ det GL_2-equivariantly. The horizontal weight-(0,0) relations glue the local differential operators on Fl acting on O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p}; the derivation d/dx acts as u₊, giving d̄₁: O^{la,(0,0)} → O^{la,(0,0)} ⊗_{O_Fl} Ω¹_Fl, s ↦ u₊(s) ⊗ dx where e₁ is invertible: the O^sm-linear extension of the de Rham differential of Fl. For χ = (n₁, n₂) integral with k = n₂ − n₁ ≥ 0 and −w·(−χ) = (n₂ + 1, n₁ − 1) there is a natural continuous operator d̄_{k+1}: O^{la,χ} → (∧²D^sm)^{k+1} ⊗ ω^{−2k−2,la,−w·(−χ)}(k + 1) = O^{la,χ} ⊗ (Ω¹_Fl)^{⊗(k+1)}, formally the (k + 1)-st power of the derivation of Fl, with (1) d̄_{k+1} O^sm-linear and (2) d̄_{k+1}(s) = c·(u₊)^{k+1}(s) ⊗ (dx)^{k+1} for a nonzero rational c wherever x is regular; it commutes with GL_2(Q_p), Hecke operators and d_{k+1}. Construction (BGG): λ_k denotes the common infinitesimal character of O^{la,(0,0)} ⊗ ω_Fl^k and its twist by (Ω¹_Fl)^{k+1}; the Hodge–Tate sequence gives 0 → ∧²D^sm ⊗ ω^{−1,la,(1,0)} → V ⊗ O^{la,(0,0)} → ω^{1,la,(0,1)}(−1) → 0, its Sym^k-version φ_{k,1}: Sym^kV ⊗ O^{la,(0,0)} → ω^{k,la,(0,k)}(−k) and φ_{k,2}, both isomorphisms on λ_k-isotypic parts; d̄_{k+1} is the λ_k-isotypic part of Sym^kV ⊗ d̄₁ transported along them.
hypotheses: Two weights (n₁, n₂), (k₁, k₂) of O^la have the same infinitesimal character iff n₁ + n₂ = k₁ + k₂ and (n₁ − n₂ − 1)² = (k₁ − k₂ − 1)² (Harish-Chandra with θ_h).
proofSteps: Define d̄₁ = u₊ ⊗ dx on the x-chart, and the analogous expression on the reciprocal chart. The horizontal weight-(0,0) matrix relations of LA.1 show these expressions agree on the overlap, giving the O^sm-linear differential of Fl (Pan II §§4.2.1–4.2.2). This rank-two chart calculation replaces an unprovided general Beilinson–Bernstein localisation theorem.

The λ_1-isotypic part of the middle term of the Hodge–Tate sequence is canonically its quotient; taking λ_1-parts of V ⊗ d̄₁ gives d̄₂, identified with (u₊)² ⊗ (dx)² up to a nonzero rational constant (Pan II §4.2.4, (4.2.4)).
General k with Sym^kV and the filtration by (∧²D^sm)^i ⊗ ω^{k−2i,la,(i,k−i)}(i − k), of which only i = 0 is λ_k-isotypic (Pan II §4.2.5, Lemma 4.2.6).
Properties and commutation with d_{k+1} from the explicit formulae (Pan II Theorem 4.2.7, Remark 4.2.8).
acceptance: On O_Fl ⊂ O^{la,(0,0)}, d̄₁ is the de Rham differential d: O_Fl → Ω¹_Fl.

sources.match: d̄₁ from Beilinson–Bernstein localisation, the BGG construction of d̄_{k+1} through λ_k-isotypic parts of Sym^kV ⊗ O^la, and its properties: O^sm-linear, a rational multiple of (u₊)^{k+1}(dx)^{k+1}, equivariant, commuting with d_{k+1}.

tests.statement: For k = 0, d̄₁ restricted to O_Fl is the exterior derivative of Fl, and d̄₁ kills O^sm.

tests.name: OperatorDbar.polynomial
tests.statement: On U ⊂ U₁, d̄_{k+1}(t^{n₁}e₁^{k}x^j s) = c·j(j − 1)⋯(j − k)t^{n₁}e₁^kx^{j−k−1}s ⊗ (dx)^{k+1} for s ∈ ω^{−k,sm} (u₊ kills t, e₁ and s, and u₊·x = 1), so polynomials of degree ≤ k in x are killed.

tests.name: OperatorDbar.polynomial_sharp
tests.statement: In characteristic zero (d/dx)^{k+1} does not kill x^{k+1}, so on the n-finite part the kernel of d̄_{k+1} is exactly the polynomials of degree ≤ k in x, the shadow of Sym^kV.

tests.name: OperatorDbar.infinitesimal_character
tests.statement: For χ′ = (n₂+1,n₁−1), n₁+n₂ = χ′₁+χ′₂ and (n₁−n₂−1)² = ((n₂+1)−(n₁−1)−1)² = (n₂−n₁+1)². Thus source and target have the same infinitesimal character in the horizontal convention.

uses.how: surjectivity and locally algebraic kernel
on Ω, d̄ is exchanged with d under Lubin–Tate–Drinfeld duality

nodes.title: d̄_{k+1} is surjective with locally algebraic kernel
nodes.statement: For χ = (n₁, n₂) integral with k = n₂ − n₁ ≥ 0, d̄_{k+1}: O^{la,χ} → O^{la,χ} ⊗ (Ω¹_Fl)^{k+1} is surjective, and its kernel is O^{lalg,χ} = Sym^kV(k) ⊗ ω^{−k,sm}·t^{n₁}. Hence the d̄-resolution 0 → Sym^kV(k) ⊗ ω^{−k,sm}_{K^p} → O^{la,(0,k)}_{K^p} → O^{la,(0,k)}_{K^p} ⊗ (Ω¹_Fl)^{k+1} → 0; for k = 0, 0 → O^sm → O^{la,(0,0)} → O^{la,(0,0)} ⊗ Ω¹_Fl → 0.
hypotheses: By equivariance it suffices to argue where e₁ generates.
proofSteps: Surjectivity: u₊ is surjective on O^{la,χ}(U) where e₁ generates (Pan I proof of Proposition 5.2.10, pp. 55–57, expansion in x − x_n).

Kernel: it is gl_2-stable and killed by (u₊)^{k+1}, so locally finite; an infinitesimal-character computation identifies it with the Sym^kV-isotypic part, i.e. LA.2/locally-algebraic-subsheaves (Pan II Proposition 4.2.9, Remark 4.2.10).
acceptance: For k = 0 this is a 'Dolbeault' resolution of O^sm by O^{la,(0,0)}, the analogue of ∂̄ on the complex upper half-plane.

sources.locator: Proposition 4.2.9 with proof and Remark 4.2.10, pp. 40–41
sources.match: Surjectivity of d̄_{k+1} and identification of its kernel with the locally algebraic subsheaf, giving the d̄-resolution.

nodes.title: O^sm ⊗ O_Fl is dense in O^{la,(0,0)}
nodes.statement: The natural map O^sm_{K^p} ⊗_C O_Fl → O^{la,(0,0)}_{K^p} has dense image (on sections over every U ∈ 𝔅).
hypotheses: Weight (0, 0).
proofSteps: Use the weight-(0,0) expansion Σc_i(x−x_n)^i. Weighted coefficients are bounded, so polynomial truncations need not converge in the same A_n. After passing to a later stage with a smaller analytic radius, the extra factor p^{−i} forces the tails to zero. The finite sums belong to O^sm(U) ⊗ O_Fl(U), proving density in the LB limit (Pan II Theorem 3.2.2 and Corollary 3.2.3, pp. 19–20).
acceptance: Hence d₁ and d̄₁ are determined by their values on O^sm (where d̄₁ = 0, d₁ = d) and on O_Fl (where d₁ = 0, d̄₁ = d).

sources.locator: Theorem 1.2.7, first sentence, p. 8; Corollary 3.2.3, p. 20
sources.match: Density of the image of O^sm ⊗ O_Fl in O^{la,(0,0)}, from the n-finite description.

nodes.title: The intertwining operator I_k and I¹_k
nodes.statement: For χ = (n₁, n₂) integral with k = n₂ − n₁ ≥ 0, I_k: O^{la,χ}_{K^p} → O^{la,−w·(−χ)}_{K^p}(k + 1) is d̄′_{k+1} ∘ d_{k+1}, where d̄′_{k+1} = d̄_{k+1} ⊗ 1 (meaningful since d̄_{k+1} is O^sm-linear) and the target is identified through the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphisms Ω¹_{K^p}(C)^sm ≅ ω^{2,sm} ⊗ (∧²D^sm)^{−1}, Ω¹_Fl ≅ ω_Fl^{−2} ⊗ det and π_HT*ω_Fl = ω(−1); equivalently I_k = (d_{k+1} ⊗ 1) ∘ d̄_{k+1}. It commutes with GL_2(Q_p) and Hecke operators. I¹_k := H¹(I_k): H¹(Fl, O^{la,χ}) → H¹(Fl, O^{la,−w·(−χ)})(k + 1); for k > 0 both sides are locally analytic vectors of the Banach cohomology, so I¹_k is a map H̃¹(K^p, C)^{la,χ} → H̃¹(K^p, C)^{la,−w·(−χ)}(k + 1); for k = 0 it factors through the quotient by colim H⁰(X_{K^pK_p}, O) of (3.4.1), giving I′_0.
hypotheses: χ integral, k = n₂ − n₁ ≥ 0; in the introduction's indexing, I_{k−1}: O^{la,(1−k,0)} → O^{la,(1,−k)}(k).
proofSteps: Compose the operators of LA.6/operator-d and LA.6/operator-dbar and identify the target (Pan II Definition 4.3.1, §1.2.9).
Commutation of d and d̄ gives the second description (Pan II Remark 4.2.8).
Cohomology through the Čech complex; the identification of H¹ for k > 0 and the factorisation for k = 0 use LA.2/cohomology-of-weight-sheaves (Pan II Definition 4.3.3, §4.3.4).
acceptance: I_k is a GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant map between sheaves with the same infinitesimal character; Pan II Remark 4.3.2 anticipates that I¹_k is the Fontaine operator (LA.11/intertwining-operator-is-fontaine-operator).

sources.match: The intertwining operator as the composite of the two differential operators, its target through Kodaira–Spencer, the induced map I¹_k on H¹ and its variant I′_0.

api.name: Intertwining.I1

api.name: Intertwining.I1_completed
api.statement: For k > 0, I¹_k is a map H̃¹(K^p, C)^{la,χ} → H̃¹(K^p, C)^{la,−w·(−χ)}(k + 1).

api.name: Intertwining.I0prime
api.statement: I′_0: H̃¹(K^p, C)^{la,(0,0)} → H̃¹(K^p, C)^{la,(1,−1)}(1), the factorisation of I¹_0.

tests.name: Intertwining.kills_flag

tests.name: Intertwining.weights
tests.statement: The weight transformation χ ↦ −w·(−χ) = (n₂+1,n₁−1) is the conjugate of the dot reflection by negation, and is an involution preserving the horizontal infinitesimal character. It is not the ordinary dot action on χ.

tests.name: Intertwining.not_zero
tests.statement: I_0 ≠ 0: on (x − x_n)·s with s ∈ O^sm nonconstant, d̄₁ gives s ⊗ dx and then d₁ gives ds ⊗ dx ≠ 0.

ker I¹_k stratum by stratum and its spectral decomposition
I_{k−1} is the Fontaine operator up to a rational scalar

nodes.title: ker I¹_k = ker H¹(d_{k+1}), and the homological lemma
nodes.statement: For χ = (n₁, n₂) with k = n₂ − n₁ ≥ 0, ker I¹_k = ker H¹(d_{k+1}). More generally, for a map X: F → G of sheaves of abelian groups on a space of cohomological dimension one there are natural maps r: H⁰(G) → H⁰(coker X) and δ: ker r = H⁰(X(F)) → H¹(ker X) and a short exact sequence 0 → coker δ → ker H¹(X) → coker r → 0; in particular (1) if H¹(ker X) = 0 then ker H¹(X) = coker r, and (2) if H⁰(G) = 0 then 0 → H¹(ker X) → ker H¹(X) → H⁰(coker X) → 0. In terms of the hypercohomology H*(X) of the two-term complex, ker H¹(X) = H¹(X)/Fil¹ with Fil¹ the image of H⁰(G).
hypotheses: Fl has cohomological dimension one for sheaves of abelian groups on its analytic site, as used in Pan II §4.4.
proofSteps: Since I_k = d̄′_{k+1} ∘ d_{k+1} and d̄′_{k+1} is surjective (LA.6/dbar-is-surjective-with-locally-algebraic-kernel), it suffices that H¹ of ker d̄′_{k+1} = Sym^kV(k) ⊗ ω^{k+2,sm} ⊗ (∧²D^sm)^{−k−1}-type sheaf vanish, which reduces to H¹(Fl, ω^{k+2,sm}) = 0 for k ≥ 0 (Pan II Lemma 4.4.2, with Pan I Corollary 5.3.6).
The homological lemma is a diagram chase with the factorisation F → X(F) → G (Pan II Lemma 4.4.4, Remark 4.4.5).
acceptance: Applied to X = d_{k+1} it gives the exact sequence for H¹(Fl, O^{la,χ})^n of Pan II §4.4.10.

sources.match: Reduction of ker I¹_k to ker H¹(d_{k+1}) by surjectivity of d̄′ and vanishing of H¹ of its kernel, and the homological lemma for maps of sheaves on a space of cohomological dimension one.

nodes.title: n-invariants and n-coinvariants of O^{la,(0,k)} and the classical theta operator
nodes.statement: For χ = (0, k), k ≥ 0, all isomorphisms O^sm-linear: (1) (O^{la,χ})^n = ω^{−k,sm}·e₁^k via s ↦ e₁^ks; (2) (O^{la,χ})_n = (i_∞)_*M†_{−k}(K^p)·e₂^k ⊕ (i_∞)_*M†_{−k}(K^p)·e₁^{1+k}e₂^{−1}; (3) H⁰(Fl, O^{la,χ}) = 0 unless k = 0, when it is H⁰(Fl, O^sm); hence H⁰(Fl, u₊(O^{la,χ})) = 0. For ω^{2k+2,la,χ}: (O^n) = ω^{k+2,sm}·e₁^k, n-coinvariants built from M†_{k+2}, and H⁰ = Sym^kV(k) ⊗ M_{k+2}(K^p), whose map to the n-coinvariants factors through M_{k+2}·e₂^k → M†_{k+2}·e₂^k. Consequently there is an exact sequence 0 → H¹(Fl, ω^{−k,sm})·e₁^k → H¹(Fl, O^{la,χ})^n → (M†_{−k}/M_{−k})·e₁^{−1}e₂^{k+1} ⊕ M†_{−k}·e₁^k → 0, the n-invariants of H¹(Fl, ω^{2k+2,la,χ}) are (M†_{k+2}/M_{k+2})·e₁^{−1}e₂^{k+1} ⊕ M†_{k+2}·e₁^k, and H¹(d_{k+1}) is compatible with θ_{k+1} ⊕ θ_{k+1} on these descriptions (after trivialising ∧²D^sm).
hypotheses: ∞ ∈ Fl is the zero of e₁; the twists ·e₁^ae₂^b denote B × G_{Q_p}-twists as in Pan II §4.4.6.
proofSteps: (1)–(3) are Pan I Propositions 5.2.6, 5.2.9–5.2.12 and Corollary 5.1.3 in this normalisation (Pan II Proposition 4.4.7, LA.4/n-coinvariants-at-infinity, LA.4/n-invariants-local).
For ω^{2k+2,la,χ} use that H⁰ of the target of d̄′_{k+1} vanishes, so H⁰ is that of ker d̄′_{k+1} (Pan II Corollary 4.4.8, Remark 4.4.9).
Apply LA.7/kernel-of-i-is-kernel-of-hd's homological lemma to u₊ and functoriality to d_{k+1} (Pan II §4.4.10).
acceptance: A constant (non-horizontal) Cartan action on H¹(Fl, O^{la,χ})^n splits it into weights (k, 0) and (−1, k + 1), different from θ_h (Pan II §4.4.10).

sources.match: The n-invariants, n-coinvariants and H⁰ of O^{la,(0,k)} and ω^{2k+2,la,(0,k)}, the resulting description of the n-invariants of H¹ and the compatibility of H¹(d_{k+1}) with θ_{k+1}.

nodes.title: The weight decomposition of (ker I¹_k)^n
nodes.statement: There is a natural Hecke- and B-equivariant weight decomposition (ker I¹_k)^n = A_{(k,0)}·e₁^k ⊕ A_{(−1,k+1)}·e₁^{−1}e₂^{k+1}, where A_{(−1,k+1)} is the kernel of θ_{k+1}: M†_{−k}(K^p)/M_{−k}(K^p) → (M†_{k+2}(K^p)/M_{k+2}(K^p)) ⊗ D₀^{−k−1} and A_{(k,0)} sits in an exact sequence 0 → colim_{K_p} H¹(X_{K^pK_p}, ω^{−k}) → A_{(k,0)} → M†_{−k}(K^p) → M†_{k+2}(K^p) ⊗ D₀^{−k−1}, the last map θ_{k+1}. Moreover ker(θ_{k+1}: M†_{−k} → M†_{k+2} ⊗ D₀^{−k−1}) = M_{−k}(K^p), in particular θ_{k+1} is injective on M†_{−k} for k > 0.
hypotheses: χ = (0, k), k ≥ 0; D₀ as in LA.6/smooth-de-rham-bundle.
proofSteps: Snake lemma applied to the diagram of §4.4.10 (Pan II Proposition 4.4.12).

k = 0: θ₁ is essentially the derivation, whose kernel on a strict neighbourhood of the canonical locus is locally constant functions, i.e. global functions since Igusa curves are irreducible (Pan II Lemma 4.4.13).

k ≥ 1: dim ker θ_{k+1} at level Γ(p^n) ≤ (k + 1)·#π₀ (an order-(k + 1) linear ODE away from the cusps), so the kernel is a finite-dimensional smooth GL_2(A_f^p)-representation factoring through det; a nonzero kernel would give a spherical eigensystem with consecutive Hodge–Tate weights at gap k + 1 > 1, contradicting LA.5/gouvea-conjecture (the Sen-weight theorem quoted as Pan20 in the source) (Pan II Lemma 4.4.14).
acceptance: For k > 0, M_{−k}(K^p) = 0, so A_{(k,0)} = colim H¹(X_{K^pK_p}, ω^{−k}) (Pan II Remark 4.4.16).

sources.match: Snake-lemma decomposition of the n-invariants of ker I¹_k and the kernel of θ_{k+1} on overconvergent forms (classical forms of weight −k).

nodes.title: The n-invariants of ker I¹_k are classical
nodes.statement: For χ = (0, k): (ker I¹_k)^n = A_{(k,0)}·e₁^k ⊕ A_{(−1,k+1)}·e₁^{−1}e₂^{k+1}, where A_{(−1,k+1)} embeds through θ_{k+1} into M_{k+2}(K^p) ⊗ D₀^{−k−1} and 0 → colim_{K_p} H¹(X_{K^pK_p}, ω^{−k}) → A_{(k,0)} → M_{−k}(K^p) → 0. All maps are Hecke- and B-equivariant. In particular every system of Hecke eigenvalues occurring in (ker I¹_k)^n comes from an automorphic form on GL_2(A). For k > 0, A_{(k,0)} = colim H¹(X_{K^pK_p}, ω^{−k}); for k = 0 there is a natural GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant splitting A_{(0,0)} = colim H¹(X_{K^pK_p}, O) ⊕ M_0(K^p).
proofSteps: Combine LA.7/kernel-n-invariants-decomposition with the kernel of θ_{k+1}: its image in M†_{k+2} ⊗ D₀^{−k−1} of the kernel of the quotient map is classical (Pan II Theorem 4.4.15).
Remark 4.4.16 for the shape of A_{(k,0)}; the cokernel of θ_{k+1} (hence a sharper description of A_{(−1,k+1)}) is only known on its primitive part (Coleman), Remark 4.4.17.
acceptance: Through Serre duality, colim H¹(X, ω^{−k}) is dual to cusp forms of weight k + 2, so all eigensystems are those of weight-(k + 2) forms.

sources.match: Classicality of the Hecke action on the n-invariants of ker I¹_k, with the shape of the two weight pieces.

planet.name: n-invariants of ker I¹_k are classical

nodes.title: Finiteness of the analytic n-invariants of ker I¹_k
nodes.statement: Let K_p = 1 + p^lM_2(Z_p), l ≥ 2. Then (1) the n-invariants of the K_p-analytic vectors of ker I¹_k are finite-dimensional, and (2) the n-finite K_p-analytic vectors (killed by a power of u₊) form a finitely generated U(g)-module. Ingredients: (a) there are m > 0 and an affinoid strict neighbourhood V of the canonical locus X_{K^pΓ(p^m),c} such that the K_p-analytic vectors in M†_{−k}/M_{−k}·e₁^{−1}e₂^{k+1} come from H⁰(V, ω^{−k}); (b) after deepening the level, the preimage of each component of V meets each connected component of X_{K^pΓ(p^{m″})} in a connected set or not at all; (c) every fibre of the map from the preimage of V in X_{K^p} to the profinite set S₁ = lim π₀ has at least three classical points in its Hodge–Tate image.
hypotheses: K_p = 1 + p^lM_2(Z_p) with l ≥ 2.
proofSteps: K_p-analytic vectors of a smooth representation are its K_p-invariants, so the K_p-analytic vectors of M_{k+2}(K^p) and of the H¹ term are finite-dimensional coherent cohomology at level K^pK_p (proper curve) (Pan II Corollary 4.4.18).

(a): by LA.3/cohomology-is-hausdorff-lb (Pan II Proposition 3.4.14) the analytic vectors come from a Čech group at level Γ(p^m); only the U₂-term contributes in weight (−1, k + 1), and evaluation at ∞ in the coordinate y = 1/x is the constant term (Pan II Lemma 4.4.19).

(b): sl_2(Q_p) acts trivially on locally analytic functions on S₁, by evaluating the first-order differential equation at three points with distinct coordinates (c) (Pan II Lemmas 4.4.20–4.4.21, Pan I Theorem 4.2.4).
Hence a section in the kernel of H⁰(V, ω^{k+2}) → M†_{k+2}/M_{k+2} is Γ(p^m)-fixed and lies in the finite-dimensional M_{k+2}(K^pΓ(p^m)).
acceptance: This is Pan II Theorem 1.1.14's local input; Dospinescu–Paškūnas–Schraen proved the finiteness by a representation-theoretic method (Pan II Remark 7.1.3).

nodes.title: The Newton stratification of the flag variety and the stalk at ∞
nodes.statement: Fl = P¹ = P¹(Q_p) ⊔ Ω with Ω the Drinfeld upper half-plane; ∞ ∈ P¹(Q_p) is the zero of e₁ with coordinate y = e₁/e₂. The stalk of O_Fl at ∞ is colim_n O_C[[y/p^n]][1/p], each a C-Banach space, and the stalk of ω^{l,sm}_{K^p} at ∞ is M†_l(K^p). Write O_{Fl,∞} ⊗̂ M†_l for the colimit of the completed tensor products, whose elements are Σ_i c_iy^i with c_i ∈ ω^l(U) for a strict affinoid neighbourhood U of some canonical locus and c_ip^{mi} bounded. Then the stalk of O^{la,(n₁,n₂)}_{K^p} at ∞ is ω^{n₂−n₁}_{Fl,∞} ⊗̂ M†_{n₁−n₂}(K^p)(n₂ − n₁)·t^{n₁}, and that of ω^{l,la,(n₁,n₂)} is the same with M†_{n₁−n₂+l}. By GL_2(Q_p)-equivariance the same holds at every point of P¹(Q_p).
hypotheses: Use the modular-curve Hodge–Tate stratification from PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S5; IG.3/newton-strata-correspond supplies the good-reduction interior comparison. At cusps use the compactified modular tower and its explicit boundary charts from S1, rather than extending the good-reduction theorem by assertion.
proofSteps: After the Weyl element, a section near ∞ is t^{n₁}e₂^{n₂−n₁} times a power series in y − y_n by LA.2/weight-sheaves; shrink so that y_n = 0 (Pan II Lemma 5.1.2, as in Pan I Proposition 5.2.10).
GL_2(Q_p) acts transitively on P¹(Q_p).
acceptance: For l = 0, χ = (0, 0): the stalk is O_{Fl,∞} ⊗̂ M†_0(K^p).

nodes.title: The kernel of d_{k+1} over P¹(Q_p)
nodes.statement: Under LA.8/newton-stratification the stalk of d_{k+1} at ∞ is 1 ⊗ θ_{k+1}. Hence (ker d_{k+1})|_{P¹(Q_p)} = 0 for k ≥ 1, and (ker d₁)|_{P¹(Q_p)} = (O_Fl ⊗ M_0(K^p))|_{P¹(Q_p)}·t^{n₁} (an ordinary tensor product).
hypotheses: χ = (n₁, n₂) integral with k = n₂ − n₁ ≥ 0.
proofSteps: θ_{k+1} is injective on M†_{−k} for k ≥ 1 and has kernel the classical weight-zero forms for k = 0 (Pan II Lemma 4.4.13, LA.7/kernel-n-invariants-decomposition); completed tensor product with the stalk of O_Fl preserves this (Pan II §5.1.3, Proposition 5.1.4).
GL_2(Q_p) acts transitively on P¹(Q_p).
acceptance: Consistent with Remark 5.4.17: d₁ computes de Rham cohomology of the fibres, which over P¹(Q_p) are Igusa curves with H⁰_dR = locally constant functions.

sources.match: The kernel of d_{k+1} on the rational points vanishes for k ≥ 1 and is O_Fl ⊗ M_0 for k = 0.

nodes.title: The cokernel of d_{k+1} over P¹(Q_p) and the ordinary sheaf
nodes.statement: Let H¹_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k) be the colimit over the Igusa tower of the rigid cohomology of Igusa curves with coefficients in the overconvergent F-isocrystal Sym^kD (RD.4/igusa-theta-cokernel), finite-dimensional at each finite level (RD.5/igusa-theta-cokernel-finite). (1) The stalk of coker d_{k+1} at ∞ is ω^k_{Fl,∞} ⊗ H¹_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k)(k)·t^{n₁}. (2) Let H¹_ord(K^p, k) be the GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant sheaf on P¹(Q_p) given by smooth induction from B of the smooth B-representation H¹_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k) (sections over U: smooth f on π^{-1}(U) ⊂ GL_2(Q_p) with f(bg) = b·f(g), π the orbit map of ∞). Then (coker d_{k+1})|_{P¹(Q_p)} = (ω^k_Fl ⊗ H¹_ord(K^p, k)(k)·t^{n₁})|_{P¹(Q_p)}, whose global sections are the locally analytic induction from B of H¹_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k)(k)·(e′₂)^kt^{n₁}; for d′_{k+1} with χ = (−k, 0), (coker d′_{k+1})|_{P¹(Q_p)} = (ω_Fl^{−k−2} ⊗ H¹_ord(K^p, k)(k) ⊗ det^{k+1}·t^{−k})|_{P¹(Q_p)} with global sections the locally analytic induction of H¹_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k)(k)·(e′₁)^{k+1}(e′₂)^{−1}t^{−k}. Here e′₁, e′₂ are the characters (a b; 0 d) ↦ a, d of B without Galois action.
hypotheses: The image of θ_{k+1} at each finite level is closed with finite-dimensional cokernel (Coleman, RD.5); the B-action on H¹_rig(Ig, Sym^k)·(e′₂)^l is locally analytic for its LB structure.
proofSteps: Closed image and finite-dimensional cokernel at each level, the open mapping theorem and completed tensor product with the stalk of O_Fl; take the colimit (Pan II Proposition 5.1.8).
Spread over P¹(Q_p) by equivariance as a smooth induction (Pan II §5.1.9, SR.2/l-sheaf-model) and compute global sections as locally analytic inductions (Pan II §5.1.10, Corollaries 5.1.11–5.1.12).
acceptance: For k = 0 the cokernel at ∞ is ω⁰ ⊗ H¹_rig(Ig(K^p)), the rigid cohomology of the (open) Igusa curves (Pan II §1.1.9).

nodes.title: Locally analytic sheaves on Ω from the Lubin–Tate tower
nodes.statement: Let M_{LT,∞} be the Lubin–Tate tower at infinite level for height-two formal groups over F̄_p, with Hodge–Tate period map π_{LT,HT} onto Ω ⊂ Fl and Gross–Hopkins period map, M^{(0)}_{LT,∞} the height-zero part (stable under GL_2(Q_p)⁰ × O_{D_p}^×, GL_2(Q_p)⁰ the determinant-unit subgroup) and π^{(0)}_{LT,HT} its period map to Ω. There is a basis of affinoids of Ω whose preimages are affinoid perfectoid and pulled back from finite level, so LA.0 applies. Define O_LT = π^{(0)}_{LT,HT*}O, O^la_LT (GL_2(Q_p)⁰-locally analytic sections), O^sm_LT (smooth: the colimit of finite levels), the O_{D_p}^×-smooth and D_p^×-locally analytic subsheaves, ω_LT, ω_Dr and their la/sm parts (with ω_{LT,∞}(−1) ≅ ω_{Dr,∞}^{−1}), the action θ_{LT,h} of h (through b⁰/n⁰, using LA.9/lubin-tate-differential-equation), the weight sheaves O^{la,χ}_LT, the GL_2-locally algebraic subsheaf O^{lalg,χ}_LT spanned by t^{n₁}e₁^ie₂^{k−i}s (s smooth, 0 ≤ i ≤ k, k = n₂ − n₁ ≥ 0), equal to Sym^kV(k) ⊗ ω^{−k,sm}_LT·t^{n₁}, its D_p^×-analogue spanned by t^{n₁}f₁^if₂^{k−i}s (s D_p^×-smooth, f₁, f₂ a basis of sections of the tautological bundle of the Drinfeld flag variety Fl′), and Ω¹_LT (the colimit of differentials, ≅ ω^{2,sm}_LT by Kodaira–Spencer) with its derivation d_LT. The coordinates x = e₂/e₁ (e₁ invertible on M_{LT,∞} since the image is Ω), t, and on the Drinfeld side y = f₂/f₁ and t′, admit finite-level approximations x_n, e_{1,n}, t_n, y_n, f_{1,n}, t′_n.
hypotheses: Height two, p-adic; the Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld towers and their period maps are those of ET.6a.
proofSteps: Embed height-zero Lubin–Tate spaces into modular curves and invoke Scholze's Theorem III.1.2 for the affinoid basis (Pan II §5.2.12).
Define the sheaves and the horizontal actions as in LA.1 (Pan II §§5.2.5, 5.2.7, 5.2.12–5.2.14).
The D_p^×-side objects through the Drinfeld tower and Fl′ (Pan II §§5.3.5, 5.3.7, 5.3.12, 5.3.15).
acceptance: O^sm_LT ⊂ O^la_LT and O_Ω ⊂ O^{la,(0,0)}_LT; t is fixed by O_{D_p}^× up to the reduced norm.

nodes.title: The differential equation on the Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld towers
nodes.statement: (1) For an open affinoid X of M_LT with preimage X̃ = Spa(B, B⁺) in M_{LT,∞} (a GL_2(Z_p)-Galois pro-étale perfectoid covering), the element θ_X̃ of LA.0/differential-equation is a generator of n⁰ up to a unit of B; equivalently n⁰ kills B^la. (2) For an affinoid Y of M_Dr whose preimage Ỹ in M_{Dr,∞} has Hodge–Tate image in an affinoid of Fl′ (such Y form a basis), Ỹ is an O_{D_p}^×-Galois pro-étale perfectoid covering and the operator annihilating the D_p^×-locally analytic vectors is a generator of n⁰_{D_p} up to a unit.
hypotheses: Smallness in LA.0 can be removed here (Pan II §5.2.5).

Planning gap: the Drinfeld conclusion requires the deferred comparison between the Liu–Zhu Higgs field and the relative Sen Higgs field, or an independent direct proof. ET.6a/analytic-vectors-under-duality assumes the same compatibility and cannot prove it here.
proofSteps: Embed the height-zero Lubin–Tate space into a modular curve and use LA.1/theta-on-the-modular-curve (Pan II proof of Theorem 5.2.6). The embedding and its identification of period maps are the S5 uniformization request; pass from principal tame level to a neat subgroup by compatible finite-level descent.

Conceptual alternative (Harris): the Higgs field of the standard representation is computed from (D(G), ∇_LT); it kills Fil⁰ = ω_LT^{−1} and induces the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism (Pan II Proposition 5.2.3) on the quotient — this route needs the compatibility of Liu–Zhu's Higgs bundle with Pan I's Higgs field, deferred by the author (footnote 3, p. 58; source issue E3 of the extraction).

The Drinfeld argument in Pan II Theorem 5.3.6 uses the conceptual Higgs-field route. Its compatibility with Pan I’s relative Sen Higgs field is deferred in footnote 3 of Theorem 5.2.6 (p. 58); T6/log-higgs-functor does not state that comparison. The modular-curve proof given for Lubin–Tate alone does not close the Drinfeld case.
acceptance: Hence b⁰/n⁰ acts and θ_{LT,h}, θ_{Dr,h} are defined (LA.9/lubin-tate-locally-analytic-sheaves).

sources.locator: §5.2.5, Proposition 5.2.3, Theorem 5.2.6 with proof and footnote 3, pp. 56–58
sources.match: The relative Sen operator of the Lubin–Tate tower generates n⁰, by reduction to modular curves, with a conceptual Higgs-field proof that rests on a deferred compatibility.
The same on the Drinfeld tower for D_p^×.

nodes.title: Power-series descriptions on both towers and the agreement of the Cartan actions
nodes.statement: (1) (Lubin–Tate) For every n and coefficients c_{i,j,k} at level G_{r(n)} with ‖c_{i,j,k}‖p^{(n−1)(i+j+k)} bounded, Σc_{i,j,k}(x − x_n)^i(log(e₁/e_{1,n}))^j(log(t/t_n))^k converges in the G_{r(n)}-analytic vectors of B, and every G_n-analytic vector arises so; consequently B^la ⊂ B^{D_p^×-la}. (2) (Drinfeld) The same with (y − y_n), log(f₁/f_{1,n}), log(t/t′_n) and H_n = 1 + p^nO_{D_p} describes the H_n-analytic vectors (the coefficients denoted c_{i,j,k}; the displayed series uses c_{i,j,k} while the quantified coefficients and their bound use d_{i,j,k}; these names must agree, extraction E1). (3) θ_{LT,h} = θ_{Dr,h} on O^la_LT: both vanish on the smooth and on the D_p^×-smooth structure sheaves, θ_{LT,h}(h) is 0 on ω^sm_LT and −1 on the D_p^×-smooth part, and symmetrically.
hypotheses: G_n = Γ(p^n); the coordinates of LA.9/lubin-tate-locally-analytic-sheaves.
proofSteps: (1) is the proof of LA.2/power-series-expansion with the Lubin–Tate coordinates (Pan II Theorem 5.2.8); D_p^× fixes x and e₁ and acts on t through the reduced norm, giving the inclusion (Pan II Corollary 5.2.10, Remark 5.2.11).
(2) likewise with roles exchanged (Pan II Theorem 5.3.8).

(3): the centres agree, both are first-order operators, so compare on finite-level sections, x, e₁/e_{1,n} and t, which generate by (1) (Pan II Corollary 5.3.13, Lemma 5.3.14) — by explicit calculation (Remark 5.3.10 notes an intrinsic proof would be preferable).
acceptance: Combined with ET.6a's duality, B^la = B^{D_p^×-la} (Pan II Corollary 5.3.9, owned by ET.6a/analytic-vectors-under-duality).

nodes.title: The operators d_LT, d̄_LT and d̄_Dr on the supersingular stratum
nodes.statement: Let χ = (n₁, n₂) integral with k = n₂ − n₁ ≥ 0. (1) There is a unique natural continuous O_Ω-linear operator d^{k+1}_LT: O^{la,χ}_LT → O^{la,χ}_LT ⊗ (Ω¹_LT)^{k+1} with d^{k+1}_LT(t^{n₁}e₁^ie₂^{k−i}s) = t^{n₁}e₁^ie₂^{k−i}(d_LT)^{k+1}(s) for smooth s ∈ ω^{−k,sm}_LT, 0 ≤ i ≤ k. (2) There is a natural continuous O^sm_LT-linear operator d̄^{k+1}_LT: O^{la,χ}_LT → O^{la,χ}_LT ⊗ (Ω¹_Ω)^{k+1}, equal to c(u₊)^{k+1}(s) ⊗ (dx)^{k+1} for some c ∈ Q^×; it is surjective, GL_2(Z_p)-equivariant, with kernel O^{lalg,χ}_LT. (3) There is a natural continuous operator d̄^{k+1}_Dr: O^{la,χ}_LT → O^{la,χ}_LT ⊗ (Ω¹_LT)^{k+1}, linear over the D_p^×-smooth structure sheaf, equal to c(u′₊)^{k+1}(s) ⊗ (dy′)^{k+1} (u′₊ ∈ Lie D_p^× ⊗ C the nilpotent carrying f₂ to f₁, y′ = f₂/f₁), surjective, O_{D_p}^×-equivariant, with kernel the D_p^×-locally algebraic subsheaf H⁰(Fl′, ω^k_{Fl′}) ⊗ (D_p^×-smooth part of ω^k_LT)·t^{n₁}. Property (1)′ of d̄_Dr is linearity over the D_p^×-smooth sections (the printed subscript LT in Pan II Theorem 5.3.17(1) is a misprint for Dr, extraction E2). The analogue of d along the Drinfeld side is not needed (Remark 5.3.18).
hypotheses: χ integral with k ≥ 0; a basis f₁, f₂ of the tautological sections on Fl′ is fixed for (3).
proofSteps: (1): repeat LA.6/operator-d with the Lubin–Tate data (Pan II Theorem 5.2.15).
(2): repeat LA.6/operator-dbar and LA.6/dbar-is-surjective-with-locally-algebraic-kernel on Ω (Pan II Theorem 5.2.16).
(3): the same on the Drinfeld side, the roles of O_Ω, Ω¹_Ω played by the smooth structure sheaf and Ω¹_LT (Pan II §5.3.16, Theorem 5.3.17).
acceptance: d^{k+1}_LT restricted to O^sm_LT ⊗ ω^{−k} is (d_LT)^{k+1}, the classical operator θ_{k+1} on the Lubin–Tate tower.

nodes.title: Through the supersingular uniformization, ker d on Ω is quaternionic forms
nodes.statement: Let D be the definite quaternion algebra over Q ramified at {p, ∞} with D ⊗ Q_p = D_p and X_{K^p} = D^×\(D ⊗ A_f)^×/K^p ≅ a finite disjoint union of O_{D_p}^×-orbits. Through the supersingular uniformization (requested from PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S5), O_{K^p}|_Ω is the sheaf of O_{D_p}^×-equivariant maps from X_{K^p} to O_LT, and ker d_{k+1}|_Ω the equivariant maps into ker d^{k+1}_LT. Hence: (1) d_{k+1}|_Ω is surjective and coker d_{k+1} is supported on P¹(Q_p), given by LA.8/cokernel-of-d-on-rational-points; (2) coker I_k is supported on P¹(Q_p) and I¹_k is surjective; (3) for χ = (n₁, n₂), k = n₂ − n₁ ≥ 0, there is a Hecke- and GL_2(Q_p)⁰-equivariant isomorphism ker d_{k+1}|_Ω ≅ (A_{D,(−n₁,−n₂)}^{K^p} ⊗ (D_p^×-smooth part of ω^{−k}_Dr))^{O_{D_p}^×}(n₂)·|det|^{n₁}det^{n₁}, where A_{D,−χ} are the quaternionic forms with coefficients in the dual W_{(−n₁,−n₂)} of the algebraic representation of D_p^× of highest weight (n₂, n₁); it extends to a GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant isomorphism after summing the bundle over its Z-translates.
hypotheses: K^p inside a level-N subgroup, N ≥ 3 prime to p, so that O_{D_p}^× acts freely on X_{K^p}.
proofSteps: Uniformization: π_HT^{-1}(Ω) ≅ ⊔ copies of M^{(0)}_{LT,∞} (Pan II Theorem 5.4.2, Lemma 5.4.4) identifies θ_h with θ_{LT,h} and d_{k+1} with d^{k+1}_LT (§5.4.5).

Surjectivity from LA.9/kernel-of-d-on-omega (Pan II Corollaries 5.4.6–5.4.7); I¹_k surjective since H¹ of sheaves on the profinite P¹(Q_p) vanishes and H¹ is right exact on Fl (Pan II Corollary 5.4.8, Remark 5.4.9).

Write equivariant maps as invariants of smooth maps and split off the locally finite coefficient (Pan II §5.4.10, Proposition 5.4.12, Remark 5.4.13); quaternionic forms are those of R17.3 (Pan II Definition 5.4.11).
acceptance: The perversity-type statement: H¹ of the complex I_k is supported on the zero-dimensional P¹(Q_p) and H⁰ on a set of dimension ≤ 1 (Pan II Remark 5.4.9).

nodes.title: The global kernels of d_{k+1} and d′_{k+1}
nodes.statement: Let j: Ω → Fl be the open embedding. For k ≥ 1, ker d_{k+1} = j_!(the sheaf of LA.9/kernel-on-omega-is-quaternionic). For k = 0, ker d₁ = j_!(the same sheaf with A^c_D, the part not factoring through the reduced norm, in place of A_D) ⊕ O_Fl ⊗ M_0(K^p)·t^{n₁}. Twisting by (Ω¹_Fl)^{k+1} gives the analogous descriptions of ker d′_{k+1}. Over Ω, d₁ computes the de Rham cohomology of the profinite fibres of π_HT, and over P¹(Q_p) that of Igusa curves.
hypotheses: χ = (n₁, n₂) integral with k = n₂ − n₁ ≥ 0.
proofSteps: Combine LA.8/kernel-of-d-on-rational-points with LA.9/kernel-on-omega-is-quaternionic (Pan II §5.4.14, Proposition 5.4.15).
For k = 0 identify the image of O_Ω ⊗ M_0 inside the invariants with the A¹-part, A¹ = smooth functions of the reduced norm = M_0 (Pan II Corollary 5.4.16, Remark 5.4.17).
acceptance: The A_D-part being j_! (extension by zero) is why compactly supported cohomology of the Drinfeld tower appears in LA.10.

sources.match: Global description of ker d_{k+1} and ker d′_{k+1} as extension by zero of the quaternionic sheaf on Ω, plus O_Fl ⊗ M_0 for k = 0.

nodes.title: The three-step filtration of ker I¹_k
nodes.statement: For χ = (−k, 0), k ≥ 0, there are natural short exact sequences 0 → ker H¹(d̄_{k+1}) → ker I¹_k → ker H¹(d′_{k+1}) → 0 and 0 → H¹(Fl, ker d′_{k+1}) → ker H¹(d′_{k+1}) → H⁰(coker d′_{k+1}) → 0, with ker H¹(d′_{k+1}) the first hypercohomology of d′_{k+1}. Hence an increasing three-step filtration of ker I¹_k with graded pieces (1) Sym^kV ⊗ H¹(Fl, ω^{−k,sm}_{K^p})·ε^{−k}; (2) H¹(Fl, ker d′_{k+1}) = (H¹(j_!(D_p^×-smooth part of ω^{k+2}_Dr)) ⊗ A_{D,(k,0)})^{O_{D_p}^×} twisted by det^{k+1} and ε_p^{−k}; (3) H⁰(coker d′_{k+1}) = the locally analytic induction from B of H¹_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k)·ε^{−k}(e′₁)^{k+1}(e′₂)^{−1}. For k = 0 the pieces are H¹(O^sm), the A^c-part plus a copy of M_0(K^p), and the induction of H¹_rig(Ig(K^p))·e′₁(e′₂)^{−1}. All Hecke- and GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant.
hypotheses: χ = (−k, 0); ε denotes the twist by t as in Pan II §5.5.3.
proofSteps: Use I_k = d′_{k+1} ∘ d̄_{k+1} with d̄ surjective; H⁰ of the target of d′_{k+1} vanishes; apply the homological lemma (Pan II Lemma 5.5.2, LA.7/kernel-of-i-is-kernel-of-hd).
Identify the pieces with LA.6/dbar-is-surjective-with-locally-algebraic-kernel, LA.9/global-kernel-of-d and LA.8/cokernel-of-d-on-rational-points (Pan II Theorem 5.5.4).
acceptance: Taking k = 0 and a weight-two cuspidal eigensystem λ with π_p supercuspidal, piece (3) vanishes at λ (LA.10/vanishing-cycle-sequence).

sources.match: The two factorisations of I_k, the filtration from d′ ∘ d̄ and the three graded pieces: coherent H¹ of smooth forms, compactly supported quaternionic cohomology on Ω, and the induction of rigid cohomology of Igusa curves.

nodes.title: Systems of spherical Hecke eigenvalues of weight k
nodes.statement: Let S ∋ p be finite with K_l maximal for l ∉ S, T_l, S_l the double-coset operators and T^S the Z_p-algebra they generate; T^S acts on O^la_{K^p}, commuting with θ_h, I_k, d_{k+1}, d̄_{k+1}. σ^{K^p}_k is the spectrum of T^S on M_k(K^p) (semisimple), σ^{K^p}_{k,n} that on M_k(K^p)·t^n. For k ≥ 2, H¹(Fl, ω^{2−k,sm}) decomposes over the eigensystems of cuspidal automorphic representations whose infinitesimal character at ∞ matches the algebraic representation of highest weight (k − 2, 0), a subset of σ^{K^p}_{k,k−1}; on quaternionic forms A_{D,(k,0)} (k ≥ 1) the action is semisimple and the eigensystems are those of cuspidal π with matching infinitesimal character and π_p special or supercuspidal (Jacquet–Langlands), a subset of σ^{K^p}_{k+2,1}; for k = 0 a quaternionic eigenform either factors through the reduced norm (weight zero) or transfers to a weight-two cuspidal eigenform. For an eigensystem λ: T^S → C and a T^S-module M, M[λ] and M̃[λ] are the eigenspace and generalised eigenspace. D₀ = M_0(K^p)·c with GL_2(A_f) acting on c through ‖det‖^{−1}.
hypotheses: S contains p and the primes where K^p is not maximal.
proofSteps: Semisimplicity on classical forms (Petersson) and on coherent H¹ (Hodge–Tate decomposition of étale cohomology with Sym^{k−2} coefficients) (Pan II §5.5.5).
Jacquet–Langlands for the quaternionic forms (R17.3).
acceptance: The eigensystem of a weight-two newform f of level prime to S lies in σ^{K^p}_{2,1}.

sources.match: The spherical Hecke algebra T^S, its semisimple spectra σ^{K^p}_{k,n} on classical forms, on coherent H¹ and on quaternionic forms, with the Jacquet–Langlands description; D₀ explicitly.

nodes.title: Spectral decomposition of ker I¹_k
nodes.statement: For χ = (−k, 0), ker I¹_k has a natural generalised eigenspace decomposition ker I¹_k = ⊕_λ (ker I¹_k)~[λ] indexed by σ^{K^p}_{k+2,1} for k ≥ 1 and by σ^{K^p}_{2,1} ∪ σ^{K^p}_0 for k = 0; the same holds for ker I′_0. Moreover, for every λ in the spectrum of H¹_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k), the n-invariants of H⁰(Fl, (coker d′_{k+1})~[λ]) are nonzero. This is Theorem 1.2.3: ker N decomposes over eigensystems of eigenforms of weight k + 1 and those of colim H⁰(Y(K^pK_p)(C), Q_p) (in the introduction's indexing).
proofSteps: By LA.10/three-step-filtration decompose each graded piece: the first two by LA.10/hecke-eigensystems; the third is a colimit of finite-dimensional Hecke-stable spaces (RD.5), so it decomposes (Pan II proof of Theorem 5.5.7).

Bound the spectrum: if λ lay outside, Fil² would vanish at λ and the generalised eigenspace would be H⁰ of the cokernel, whose n-invariants are nonzero (Pan II Lemma 5.5.8); but LA.7/n-invariants-are-classical forces λ classical — contradiction.
For I′_0, pass to the quotient (Pan II Corollary 5.5.9).
acceptance: Alternatively the third piece could be bounded by Coleman's results or by independence of l for Igusa curves (Pan II remark in the proof of Theorem 5.5.7).

sources.locator: Theorem 5.5.7, Lemma 5.5.8, Corollary 5.5.9, pp. 76–77; Theorem 1.2.3, p. 7
sources.match: The generalised eigenspace decomposition of ker I¹_k over classical eigensystems, with the spectrum bounded through the classicality of n-invariants.

nodes.title: The de Rham complexes DR_k and D_k and the Hodge filtration
nodes.statement: For k ≥ 0 let DR_k be the two-term complex d_{k+1}: O^{la,(−k,0)}_{K^p} → (target of d_{k+1}) on Fl, DR′_k that of d′_{k+1}, and D_k the two-term complex θ_{k+1}: ω^{−k,sm}_{K^p} → ω^{k+2,sm} ⊗ (∧²D^sm)^{−k−1}. Fil¹DR_k is the target placed in degree 1. Then ker H¹(d_{k+1}) = H¹(DR_k)/Fil¹H¹(DR_k), H⁰(d_{k+1}) = 0, and Fil¹H¹(DR_k) = H⁰(target) ≅ Sym^kV ⊗ M_{k+2}(K^p)(k) ⊗ D₀^{−k−1}·t^{−k}, embedded by i_H through the locally algebraic inclusion. D_k is quasi-isomorphic to the logarithmic de Rham complex Sym^kD^{*,sm} → Sym^kD^{*,sm} ⊗ Ω¹(log cusps), H¹(D_k) = colim of finite-level de Rham cohomology H¹_dR,log(X_{K^pK_p}, Sym^kD^*) with 0 → H⁰(target) → H¹(D_k) → H¹(ω^{−k,sm}) → 0, H²(D_k) = 0, and T^S acts semisimply on H¹(D_k). d̄_{k+1} gives an exact triangle D_k ⊗ Sym^kV·ε^{−k} → DR_k → DR′_k, so 0 → H¹(D_k) ⊗ Sym^kV·ε^{−k} → H¹(DR_k) → H¹(DR′_k) → 0, and i_H describes the classical Hodge filtration of H¹(D_k).
hypotheses: k ≥ 0; hypercohomology on the analytic site of Fl.

At finite level use the canonical logarithmic connection at the cusp divisor. After localising at a cuspidal eigensystem the boundary contribution vanishes, so the usual cuspidal de Rham interpretation is recovered.
proofSteps: Hodge filtration via Remark 4.4.5; H⁰(d_{k+1}) = 0 since H⁰ of the source vanishes for k ≠ 0 and is M_0·t^{n₁}, killed by d₁, for k = 0 (Pan II §5.5.10, Lemma 5.5.11, Definition 5.5.12).

D_k and its semisimplicity: the inclusion ω^{−k,sm} ⊂ Sym^kD^{*,sm} is a quasi-isomorphism onto the logarithmic de Rham complex; Hecke semisimplicity from the Shimura isomorphism over C (Pan II §5.6.1, Proposition 5.6.2).
The triangle from d̄ commuting with d (Pan II §5.6.3, Remark 5.6.12).
acceptance: For k=0, H¹(D_0) is the finite-level colimit of logarithmic de Rham cohomology. Its Fil¹ is colim H⁰(X_{K^pK_p},Ω¹(log cusps))=colim H⁰(X_{K^pK_p},ω²), using logarithmic Kodaira–Spencer (Pan II Remark 1.1.13).

nodes.title: H¹(DR_k) and the eigenspaces in the supercuspidal and principal series cases
nodes.statement: There is a natural exact sequence 0 → (H¹(j_!(D_p^×-smooth part of ω^{−k}_Dr)) ⊗ A^c_{D,(k,0)})^{O_{D_p}^×}·ε_p^{−k} → H¹(DR_k) → H⁰(Fl, ω^k_Fl ⊗ H¹_ord(K^p, k))·ε^{−k} → 0, the quotient being the locally analytic induction from B of H¹_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k)·ε^{−k}(e′₂)^k. Let λ ∈ σ^{K^p}_{k+2,1} come from a cuspidal π. (1) If π_p is supercuspidal, H¹_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k)·t^{−k}[λ] = 0 and (ker I¹_k)~[λ] = (ker I¹_k)[λ] = (quaternionic term)[λ]/i_H(Fil¹)[λ], an extension of the invariants term by Sym^kV ⊗ H¹(ω^{−k,sm})·ε^{−k}[λ]. (2) If π_p is a principal series (the cuspidal quaternionic part vanishes at λ), (ker I¹_k)~[λ] = (ker I¹_k)[λ] = (induction of H¹_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k)·ε^{−k}(e′₂)^k)[λ]/i_H(Fil¹)[λ]. In both cases H¹(DR_k)[λ] is its own generalised eigenspace and ker I¹_k[λ] = H¹(DR_k)[λ]/Fil¹. The special case (π_p a twist of Steinberg) is expected but not proved directly (Pan II Remark 5.5.15).
hypotheses: λ comes from a cuspidal π with π_p supercuspidal or principal series; the honesty of Igusa eigenspaces (LA.10/vanishing-cycle-sequence).
proofSteps: Proposition 5.5.13 from the three-step filtration and Lemma 5.5.11.
Corollary 5.5.14 using the vanishing of the Igusa term at supercuspidal λ and the honesty of eigenspaces from Corollary 5.6.11 (LA.10/vanishing-cycle-sequence).
The uniform sheaf-theoretic reading with j_!ν_*(L_ss ⊗ ω^k) and i_!(L_ord ⊗ ω^k) is Remark 5.5.16.
acceptance: The two cases exhibit Π_ρ^la-type objects as quotients by the Hodge filtration, matching Pan II Theorems 7.3.2 and 7.3.7.

sources.match: Two-step description of H¹(DR_k) by compactly supported quaternionic cohomology on Ω and the induction of Igusa rigid cohomology, and the honest eigenspaces of ker I¹_k when π_p is supercuspidal or a principal series.

nodes.title: Compactly supported de Rham cohomology of the Drinfeld tower
nodes.statement: Let DR_dR be the complex d: (D_p^×-smooth structure sheaf on Ω) → Ω¹_Dr (≅ ω²_Dr ⊗ det by Kodaira–Spencer) and j: Ω → Fl. H^i_{dR,c}(M^{(0)}_{Dr,∞}) := H^i(Fl, j_!DR_dR); since only H¹ of each term is nonzero, H^i_{dR,c} is the (i − 1)-st cohomology of H¹(j_!O^{D-sm}) → H¹(j_!Ω¹_Dr). The same recipe at finite level gives H^i_{dR,c}(M^{(0)}_{Dr,n}) with H^i_{dR,c}(M^{(0)}_{Dr,∞}) = colim_n. GL_2(Q_p)⁰ acts on H²_{dR,c} through det and O_{D_p}^× through the reduced norm.
hypotheses: At finite level the Drinfeld curve is finite étale over the Stein upper half-plane, hence quasi-Stein; coherent acyclicity, rather than partial properness alone, permits the naive de Rham complex. The topological Serre-duality comparison with compact supports is a separate input.
proofSteps: Definition by j_! (Pan II Definition 5.6.5).

The identification with finite-level compactly supported de Rham cohomology and topological Serre duality need the curve/tower duality theorem discussed in Pan II §5.6.9, p. 83 (Colmez–Dospinescu–Nizioł §4.3). No listed prerequisite supplies it. Until the proposed ProetaleCohomologyOfPAdicCurvesAndTowers has such a node, this interpretation and the H² action are conditional; the j_! hypercohomology definition itself is well specified.
H⁰_dR is the continuous functions on π₀, so H²_{dR,c} is abelian (Pan II Lemma 5.6.10).
acceptance: H²_{dR,c} is finite-dimensional at each finite level.

sources.match: Compactly supported de Rham cohomology of the height-zero Drinfeld tower as hypercohomology of j_! of the de Rham complex, its finite-level interpretation and the abelian action on H²_{dR,c}.

nodes.title: The p-adic vanishing-cycle exact sequence and honest Igusa eigenspaces
nodes.statement: For k ≥ 1 there is a natural exact sequence 0 → (H¹_{dR,c}(M^{(0)}_{Dr,∞}) ⊗ A_{D,(k,0)})^{O_{D_p}^×} → H¹(D_k) → Ind_B^{GL_2(Q_p)}H¹_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k) → (H²_{dR,c} ⊗ A_{D,(k,0)})^{O_{D_p}^×} → 0 (with the displayed untwisted normalisation of Pan II Theorem 5.6.7; the induction is smooth, the global sections of H¹_ord), and for k = 0 the same with A^c and an extra summand M_0(K^p) in the last term. Consequently, if λ comes from a cuspidal π and the generalised λ-eigenspace of H¹_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^k) is nonzero, then (1) it is an honest eigenspace and (2) π_p is a principal series or special.
hypotheses: k ≥ 0; cuspidal eigensystems λ.
proofSteps: Snake lemma for d̄_{k+1} on the kernel–cokernel sequences of DR_k and DR′_k gives (5.6.1) with maps SS_k, ORD_k (Pan II §5.6.3).

ker ORD_k = Sym^kV ⊗ the induction (Pan II Lemma 5.6.4); the supersingular map is quasi-isomorphic to Sym^kV ⊗ DR_dR on the λ_k-isotypic part, identifying ker SS_k and coker SS_k with H¹_{dR,c}, H²_{dR,c} terms (Pan II Lemma 5.6.6); remove Sym^kV by taking smooth parts after tensoring with its dual (Pan II Theorem 5.6.7).

At λ the outer terms are Hecke-semisimple; non-semisimplicity in the middle would force a full induction from B in the last term, contradicting LA.10/compactly-supported-de-rham-drinfeld's abelian H²_{dR,c}; a nonzero map from π_p to the induction excludes supercuspidal π_p (Pan II Corollary 5.6.11).
acceptance: This is the p-adic analogue of Carayol's l-adic vanishing-cycle sequence for modular curves (Pan II Remark 5.6.8), comparable through Colmez–Dospinescu–Nizioł.

sources.locator: §5.6.3, Lemma 5.6.4, Lemma 5.6.6, Theorem 5.6.7, Remark 5.6.8, Corollary 5.6.11, pp. 80–83
sources.match: The p-adic vanishing-cycle sequence relating de Rham cohomology of modular curves, compactly supported de Rham cohomology of the Drinfeld tower with quaternionic forms, and the induction of Igusa rigid cohomology; honesty of Igusa eigenspaces and exclusion of supercuspidal π_p.

nodes.title: Truncated relative period sheaves and their locally analytic isotypic parts
nodes.statement: On X_{K^p}, A_inf assigns to an affinoid perfectoid V the Witt vectors of the tilt of O⁺(V), with θ onto O⁺; B⁺_dR is the ker θ-adic completion of A_inf[1/p], with Fontaine's t generating the relative kernel, so gr^iB⁺_dR = O(i). Push forward along π_HT to get B⁺_dR on Fl with gr^i = O_{K^p}(i), and truncate: B⁺_{dR,k} = B⁺_dR/(t^k). For U ∈ 𝔅, B⁺_{dR,k}(U) is a flat Banach B⁺_dR/(t^k)-module with unit ball the image of A_inf, with GL_2(Q_p)- and (for K large) G_K-action; B^{+,la}_{dR,k} is the locally analytic subsheaf, with g-action, and for an infinitesimal character χ̃ of Z = Z(U(g)), B^{+,la,χ̃}_{dR,k} its χ̃-isotypic part. Then gr^iB^{+,la}_{dR,k} ≅ O^la_{K^p}(i) and gr^iB^{+,la,χ̃}_{dR,k} ≅ O^{la,χ̃}_{K^p}(i) for 0 ≤ i ≤ k − 1; both sheaves are flat over B⁺_dR/(t^k). The restriction B⁺_{dR,k}(U₁) → B⁺_{dR,k}(U₁₂) is a closed embedding, strict for the t-adic filtration; so are the maps on G_n-analytic χ̃-isotypic sections (closed embeddings) and on locally analytic χ̃-isotypic sections (closed embeddings, strict for the t-adic filtration); their Čech cohomology for {U₁, U₂} computes H*(Fl, B⁺_{dR,k}) and H*(Fl, B^{+,la,χ̃}_{dR,k}), flat over B⁺_dR/(t^k) with gr^iH* = H*(gr^i), and H*(Fl, B^{+,la,χ̃}_{dR,k}) is Hausdorff.
hypotheses: B⁺_dR is the ker θ-adic completion of A_inf[1/p] on affinoid perfectoid opens, as in Scholze 2013 §6; χ̃ an infinitesimal character, viewed as a W-orbit in h* by Harish-Chandra.
Planning gap: the asserted closed-range/topological cohomology package depends on the unresolved geometric strictness argument (source issue E2).
proofSteps: Construction and graded pieces from Scholze's period sheaves (Pan II §6.2.1).

gr^i commutes with locally analytic vectors by LA-acyclicity of O_{K^p}(U) (LA.2/la-acyclicity-on-the-basis); with χ̃-parts by a Koszul-complex vanishing of Ext_Z(χ̃, −) after Harish-Chandra embeds Z in a polynomial ring in two variables, using the h-cohomology vanishing of LA.2/weight-sheaves (Pan II Lemma 6.2.2).

The strictness and Hausdorff cohomology assertions are conditional on repairing LA.3/lb-topology-on-cohomology. Pan II Corollaries 6.2.10–6.2.11 use the invalid general Lemma 3.4.3 via the graded Čech maps; flatness of the local modules and the existence of their graded pieces do not prove closed range. Prove the actual period Čech strictness and filtration strictness geometrically.
acceptance: For k = 1, B⁺_{dR,1} = O_{K^p} and the statements reduce to LA.2–LA.3.

sources.locator: §6.2.1, Lemma 6.2.2, §6.2.8, Lemma 6.2.9, Corollaries 6.2.10–6.2.11, Definition 6.2.12, Proposition 6.2.13, pp. 92–96
sources.match: The relative period sheaves B⁺_{dR,k} on the infinite-level modular curve and Fl, their locally analytic χ̃-isotypic subsheaves with graded pieces O^{la,χ̃}(i), flatness, strict Čech complexes and their cohomology.

nodes.title: The infinitesimal character χ̃_k and the Hodge–Tate decomposition
nodes.statement: For k ≥ 1, χ̃_k is the dot-orbit {(0, 1 − k), (−k, 1)} ⊂ h*, the infinitesimal character of Sym^{k−1} of the dual of the standard representation. On the χ̃_k-isotypic part, θ_h satisfies a quadratic relation, giving O^{la,χ̃_k}_{K^p} = O^{la,(1−k,0)}_{K^p} ⊕ O^{la,(1,−k)}_{K^p}, Hodge–Tate of weights 0 and k respectively, so the χ̃_k-isotypic part is Hodge–Tate of weights 0, k. Correspondingly B^{+,la,χ̃_k}_{dR,k+1}(U), a Hausdorff LB-space module over B⁺_dR/(t^{k+1}) (a colimit of flat Banach modules), is Hodge–Tate of weights 0, k in the terminology of Pan II Definition 6.1.9 (a condition on its gr⁰ = W/tW), and satisfies the hypotheses of the LB Fontaine construction (Pan II §6.1.17). This does not assign weights 0,k to all t-adic graded pieces: grⁱW ≅ gr⁰W(i), with the corresponding shifted Sen eigenvalues.
hypotheses: Harish-Chandra: Z(U(g)) ≅ S(h)^{W·}; θ_h relates to Z as in LA.1/horizontal-cartan-action.
proofSteps: Compute the Harish-Chandra image of Sym^{k−1}(V*) (Pan II §6.2.3).
The two θ_h-weights in the orbit give the decomposition; Hodge–Tate weights from LA.3/analytic-vectors-are-hodge-tate (weight −n₂: 0 for (1 − k, 0), k for (1, −k)).
acceptance: For k = 1, χ̃_1 = {(0, 0), (−1, 1)}, the trivial infinitesimal character, and O^{la,χ̃_1} = O^{la,(0,0)} ⊕ O^{la,(1,−1)}.

nodes.title: The Fontaine operator N_k on O^{la,(1−k,0)}
nodes.statement: For U ∈ 𝔅 the module B^{+,la,χ̃_k}_{dR,k+1}(U) satisfies the hypotheses of the LB-space Fontaine construction (requested from the PadicHodgeTheory Part II), giving a Fontaine operator O^{la,(1−k,0)}_{K^p}(U) → O^{la,(1,−k)}_{K^p}(U)(k); by functoriality these glue to N_k: O^{la,(1−k,0)}_{K^p} → O^{la,(1,−k)}_{K^p}(k). Concretely: on the G_{K_∞}-fixed G_K-analytic vectors, the action ∇ of 1 ∈ Lie Gal(K_∞/K) on the generalised 0-eigenspace E_0 is an extension of the weight-0 graded piece by the twisted weight-k piece on which ∇ acts trivially, and ∇ induces the map between them, extended C-linearly. On cohomology, H¹(Fl, B^{+,la,χ̃_k}_{dR,k+1}) is Hodge–Tate of weights 0, k in the gr⁰ sense of Definition 6.1.9 and its Fontaine operator is H¹(N_k); for k ≥ 2, H¹(Fl, B^{+,la,χ̃_k}_{dR,k+1}) = H¹(Fl, B⁺_{dR,k+1})^{la,χ̃_k}, and for k = 1 these differ by Ext¹_Z, Ext²_Z(χ̃_1, H⁰(Fl, B⁺_{dR,2})^la).
hypotheses: k ≥ 1; U ∈ 𝔅 with G_K acting.
proofSteps: Apply the LB Fontaine construction of Pan II §6.1.19 to B^{+,la,χ̃_k}_{dR,k+1}(U) (Pan II §6.2.4, Definition 6.2.5).
On Čech complexes use Proposition 6.1.20 and Corollary 6.1.21 (with B⁺_dR/(t^{k+1})) (Pan II §6.2.14).
The comparison with Banach cohomology follows Pan I Theorem 4.4.6 and Corollary 5.1.3; the Ext terms vanish for k ≥ 2 because sl_2(Q_p) acts trivially on H⁰ (Pan II §6.2.16, Proposition 6.2.17).
acceptance: For W = V ⊗ B⁺_dR/(t^{k+1}) with V two-dimensional of Hodge–Tate weights 0, k, the same recipe gives Fontaine's N_W, which vanishes iff V is de Rham (Pan II Theorem 6.1.16).
