nodes.title: The log de Rham period sheaf on the modular curve: Kodaira–Spencer presentation
nodes.statement: Let V₀ ⊂ X_{K^pK_p} be an affinoid with preimage V_∞ = π_HT^{-1}(U), U ∈ 𝔅, and OB⁺_dR (log, of Diao–Lan–Liu–Zhu) with its Poincaré sequence 0 → B⁺_dR → OB⁺_dR → OB⁺_dR ⊗ Ω¹_{V₀}(C) → 0 and log Faltings extension. By Kodaira–Spencer, Ω¹_{V₀}(C) ≅ ω², hence O(V_∞) ⊗ Ω¹_{V₀}(C) ≅ O(V_∞) after a choice of generator; gr^kOB⁺_dR(V_∞) = Sym^k(gr¹) is filtered with graded pieces O(V_∞)(i), i = 0, …, k; and for X ∈ Fil¹OB⁺_dR(V_∞) mapping to a generator of O(V_∞) ⊗ Ω¹_{V₀}(C), B⁺_dR(V_∞)[[X]] → OB⁺_dR(V_∞) is an isomorphism, of filtered groups with X in degree one. The truncations OB⁺_{dR,k}(U) are finite B⁺_{dR,k}(U)-modules and Banach algebras with unit ball the image of A_inf(V_∞)[[X]]; their locally analytic and χ̃-isotypic parts have graded pieces as in CP.6/pan-graded-analytic-decompletion.
hypotheses: The log structure of the cusps; V₀ small enough that ω is trivial on it.
proofSteps: Import OB⁺_dR,log, its connection, Poincaré lemma and the toric power-series model (T6:comparison) (Pan II §6.3.5–6.3.6).
Kodaira–Spencer makes Ω¹_{V₀}(C) trivial, and Sym of Faltings's extension gives the filtration; the toric model gives the presentation (Pan II (6.3.3)).
Graded pieces commute with analytic vectors and decompletion (CP.6/pan-graded-analytic-decompletion, Pan II Proposition 6.3.9).
acceptance: For k = 1, gr¹OB⁺_dR(V_∞) is the log Faltings extension of O(V_∞) ⊗ Ω¹ by O(V_∞)(1), identified by LA.1/faltings-extension-is-hodge-tate-sequence with the Hodge–Tate sequence.

sources.match: The structural log de Rham period sheaf on the modular curve, its Poincaré sequence and Faltings extension, the Kodaira–Spencer trivialisation of Ω¹, the filtration of gr^k and the presentation B⁺_dR[[X]] ≅ OB⁺_dR, and the truncated sheaves OB⁺_{dR,k}.

nodes.title: Reduction of N_k = c_kI_{k−1} to two comparisons
nodes.statement: Let M be an abelian group with an endomorphism N, N² = 0, M′ ⊂ ker N a subgroup containing N(M), M″ = M/M′, so N induces N_{M′}: M″ → M′. Suppose M₁ ⊃ M carries N₁ with N₁² = 0 and N₁|_M = N, θ: M₁ → M″ extends the quotient map, M′₁ ⊂ ker θ is N₁-stable with M′₁ ∩ M = M′ and N₁(M′₁) ⊂ M′, M′₂ = M′₁/M′ ⊂ M₂ = M₁/M with quotient map π, and s: M″ → ker N₁ is a right inverse of θ with π∘s(M″) ⊂ M′₂; then N_{M′} = −N_{1,M′} ∘ (π ∘ s) as maps M″ → M′. Applied to E_0 of the χ̃_k-isotypic decompleted period module, the truncated Poincaré sequence and its gr^k-part, and a section s_{k+1} of E_0(θ_log) (LA.11/first-comparison), this gives N_k(U) = −N′_k ∘ (E_0(∇_log) ∘ s_{k+1}), where N′_k is the Lie-algebra action on the middle term of the gr^k sequence. Hence Theorem 6.2.6 follows from (A) E_0(∇_log) ∘ s_{k+1} = d_k on O^{la,(1−k,0)}(U)^{G_K} and (B) N′_k = c_kd̄′_k for some c_k ∈ Q_p^×.
hypotheses: U ∈ 𝔅 with e₁ invertible on its preimage and G_K acting.
proofSteps: Linear algebra (Pan II §6.3.2, Lemma 6.3.3, Remark 6.3.4).
Generalised eigenspace decomposition for 1 ∈ Lie Gal(K_∞/K) on the decompleted isotypic sections and the main diagram of two exact rows (Pan II §§6.3.10–6.3.11).
Read off the reduction (Pan II §6.3.12, Propositions 6.3.13–6.3.14); the case k = 1 is sketched first in §6.3.1.
acceptance: For k = 1, (A) reads E_0(∇_log) ∘ s₂ = d₁ and (B) N′_1 = c₁d̄′₁.

sources.match: The linear-algebra mechanism expressing an operator through a section, and the reduction of the identity N_k = c_kI_{k−1} to the comparison of E_0(∇_log) ∘ s_{k+1} with d_k and of N′_k with d̄′_k.

nodes.title: The p-adic Legendre relation and the period x̃
nodes.statement: The relative de Rham comparison provides O_{V₀}-linear period maps l_n: Sym^nD ⊗ Sym^n(V*) → OB⁺_dR(U). (1) An element of OB⁺_dR(U) is invertible iff its image under θ_log is; if θ_log(y) has norm ≤ 1 and a_n → 0 in O_{V₀}, Σa_ny^n converges in OB⁺_{dR,k}(U). (2) For k = 1 and e₁ invertible on the preimage, with f₁ a section of D generating gr⁰, x̃ := −l₁(f₁ ⊗ e₁*)/l₁(f₁ ⊗ e₂*) is G_K-fixed with θ_log(x̃) = x. (3) (Legendre) For g₁, g₂ ∈ D and v₁, v₂ ∈ V*, l₁(g₁ ⊗ v₁)l₁(g₂ ⊗ v₂) − l₁(g₁ ⊗ v₂)l₁(g₂ ⊗ v₁) ∈ t·OB⁺_dR(U); hence ∇_log of φ₁(x) lies in t·OB⁺_dR(U) ⊗ Ω¹, and x̃ mod t is independent of f₁. (4) There is a G_K × G_0-equivariant map φ₁ from the decompleted weight-(0, 0) sections to OB⁺_dR(U) with θ_log ∘ φ₁ = id, linear over finite-level functions, continuous into each truncation, with φ₁(x) ≡ x̃ mod t.
hypotheses: U ∈ 𝔅 with e₁ invertible on the preimage; f₁ fixed.
proofSteps: (1): completeness for the ker θ_log-adic topology and a Teichmüller-type splitting, as Berger–Colmez Lemme 4.9 (Pan II Lemmas 6.4.2–6.4.3).
(2): l₁(f₁ ⊗ e₂*) has invertible θ_log-image, so is invertible (Pan II §6.4.4).
(3): the determinant of the de Rham bundle lands in t times the determinant of V — Scholze's lattice comparison (requested) (Pan II §6.4.5, Lemma 6.4.6, §6.4.7).
(4): build φ₁ from x̃ and the expansion of LA.2/weight-sheaves (Pan II Proposition 6.4.8).
acceptance: The name: over C the analogous relation between periods of an elliptic curve is Legendre's relation ω₁η₂ − ω₂η₁ = 2πi, with t playing 2πi.

sources.match: Period maps from the relative de Rham comparison, invertibility and convergence in OB⁺_dR, the period x̃ lifting the coordinate x, the p-adic Legendre relation and the section φ₁ in weight zero.

nodes.title: First comparison: E_0(∇_log) ∘ s_{k+1} = d_k
nodes.statement: For k ≥ 1 define s_{k+1} := (l′_{k−1} mod Fil^{k+1}) ∘ ψ_{k−1}, where l′_n extends l_n linearly over the decompleted weight-(0, 0) sections using φ₁ and ψ_{k−1} is the canonical splitting of LA.6/operator-d (Pan II Lemma 4.1.6) transported to the period side; it takes values in the locally analytic χ̃_k-isotypic part with θ_log ∘ s_{k+1} = id. Then ∇_log ∘ s_{k+1} lands in Fil^{k−1} of the truncated structural sheaf tensor Ω¹_{V₀}(C) and equals d_k under the identification with O^{la,(1−k,0)}(U) ⊗ (Ω¹_{V₀}(C))^{⊗k}.
hypotheses: k ≥ 1; the choices of LA.11/p-adic-legendre-relation.
proofSteps: Construct s_{k+1} following §4.1 (Pan II §6.4.9, Definition 6.4.10).
It suffices to prove the identity modulo t, since reduction mod t is injective on G_K-invariants of the truncated isotypic structural sheaf (Pan II Lemma 6.4.12).
Modulo t it is the commutativity of an explicit diagram, using that l′_{k−1} mod t extends C-linearly (Pan II Lemma 6.4.13, Proposition 6.4.11).
acceptance: For k = 1, s₂ = φ₁ and the identity says ∇_log(φ₁(f)) ≡ d₁(f) — the derivative along the modular curve is the log connection on periods.

sources.match: Construction of the section s_{k+1} and the proof that ∇_log ∘ s_{k+1} = d_k, by reduction modulo t to an explicit diagram.

nodes.title: Second comparison: N′_k = c_kd̄′_k with c_k ∈ Q^×
nodes.statement: The gr^k Poincaré sequence 0 → gr^kB^{+,la}_dR(U) → gr^kOB^{+,la}_dR(U) → gr^{k−1}OB^{+,la}_dR(U) ⊗ Ω¹_{V₀}(C) → 0 stays exact after taking the scalar z_k-part for the Lie-algebra centre and G_K-invariants (Pan II Proposition 6.5.2), before extracting the generalised full-Z character; Z acts on gr^kB^{+,la}_dR(U)^{G_K,z_k} through χ̃_k, and on gr^{k−1}OB^{+,la}_dR(U)^{G_K,z_k} the χ̃_k-generalised eigenspace is honest and equals O^{la,(1−k,0)}(U)^{G_K} ⊗ Ω¹_{V₀}(C)^{⊗(k−1)}. The shifted Casimir induces Ñ_k between the outer terms O^{la,(1−k,0)}(U)^{G_K} ⊗ Ω¹_{V₀}(C)^{⊗k} and O^{la,(1,−k)}(U)(k)^{G_K}, N′_k = Ñ_k/(2k), and Ñ_k = c d̄′_k for some c ∈ Q^×. Hence N′_k = c_kd̄′_k with c_k ∈ Q^×. Full-Z generalised eigenspaces in the middle term need not be honest eigenspaces: the nontrivial shifted Casimir action produces Ñ_k. Exactness after full-Z ordinary eigenspaces is not asserted.
hypotheses: U ∈ 𝔅 with e₁ invertible; the trivialisation of ∧²D fixed.
proofSteps: Exactness by an equivariant splitting of the locally analytic Faltings extension (Faltings) for k = 1 and symmetric powers in general (Pan II Proposition 6.5.2, Lemma 6.5.3).
The quadratic relation for θ_Sen, which is θ_h of the lower-right idempotent (LA.3/theta-h-is-the-sen-operator), controls the Z-action (Pan II Proposition 6.5.4, Corollary 6.5.5).
Compare N′_k with Ñ_k (Pan II §6.5.6, Lemma 6.5.7).

Both Ñ_k and d̄′_k are continuous O^sm-linear and preserve the dense n-finite parts, where they come from g-maps M^∨_{(0,1−k)} → M^∨_{(−k,1)}(k) between category-O modules; such maps form a one-dimensional space and neither is zero (Verma module of highest weight −ρ, translation functors), so they are proportional; Q-structures give c ∈ Q^× (Pan II §6.5.8–Remark 6.5.13, Lemmas 6.5.9–6.5.12). The necessary category-O/translation-functor input is absent from LieHighestWeight’s existing scope (its README explicitly excludes full category O). This step requires the Part II contract below or an explicit rank-one calculation proving its nonzero one-dimensional Hom statement.
acceptance: The n-finite part of the Hodge–Tate sequence is ω^{2,sm} ⊗ (0 → M^∨_{(−1,1)}(1) → V(1) ⊗ M^∨_{(0,−1)} → M^∨_{(0,0)} → 0) (Pan II Lemma 6.5.10).

sources.match: Exactness of the gr^k Poincaré sequence after taking invariants, the action of the centre, the operator Ñ_k from the shifted Casimir, and its proportionality with d̄′_k through category O, with a rational constant.

nodes.title: The intertwining operator is Fontaine's operator
nodes.statement: For every integer k ≥ 1 there is c_k ∈ Q_p^× (in fact in Q^×, Pan II Remark 6.5.13) with N_k = c_kI_{k−1} as maps O^{la,(1−k,0)}_{K^p} → O^{la,(1,−k)}_{K^p}(k). On cohomology: for k ≥ 2, I¹_{k−1} = c_k^{−1}N on H̃¹(K^p, C)^{la,(1−k,0)} = W_0 → W_k(k); for k = 1, the restriction of I¹_0 to H¹(Fl, O^{la,(0,0)})[λ_τ] agrees with c₁^{−1}N on W_0[λ_τ] (Theorem 1.2.10).
hypotheses: k ≥ 1; for k = 1 the statement on cohomology is on λ_τ-isotypic parts because H¹(Fl, O^{la,(0,0)}) → W_0 is not an isomorphism (extra H̃⁰ term).
proofSteps: Local identity on U ∈ 𝔅 from LA.11/reduction-to-two-comparisons with (A) LA.11/first-comparison and (B) LA.11/second-comparison: N_k(U) = −c_k d̄′_k ∘ d_k, i.e. a rational multiple of I_{k−1} (Pan II Theorem 6.2.6).
Glue over 𝔅 and pass to H¹ through LA.11/sheaf-fontaine-operator (Pan II Corollary 6.2.15); the constant is rational (Remark 6.5.13; Remark 6.2.7 notes it is not needed).
acceptance: Consequence: for V ⊂ H̃¹(K^p, Q_p)^{la,χ̃_k} two-dimensional irreducible, V is de Rham iff I¹_{k−1} vanishes on (V ⊗ C)_0.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.2.6, Remark 6.2.7, Corollary 6.2.15, pp. 94–96; Theorem 1.2.10, p. 8
sources.match: N_k is a nonzero rational multiple of the intertwining operator I_{k−1}, on sheaves and on cohomology.

nodes.title: The Banach representation Π_ρ and its locally analytic vectors
nodes.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite and ρ: G_Q → GL_2(E) continuous, two-dimensional, absolutely irreducible. Π_ρ := Hom_{E[G_Q]}(ρ, H̃¹(K^p, E)) with H̃¹(K^p, E) = H̃¹(K^p, Z_p) ⊗ E, an admissible E-Banach representation of GL_2(Q_p); H̃¹(K^p, E)[ρ] is the image of the evaluation map ρ ⊗ Π_ρ → H̃¹(K^p, E). Π_ρ^la is its subspace of GL_2(Q_p)-locally analytic vectors. With λ the cyclotomic twist of the Hecke eigensystem with ρ_λ(−1) = ρ, H̃¹(K^p, E)[ρ] is the λ-isotypic part, and H̃¹(K^p, E)[ρ] ⊗̂ C = W_0 ⊕ W_k (Hodge–Tate weights 0, k) when ρ|G_{Q_p} has Hodge–Tate weights 0, k. If ρ is attached to a cuspidal eigenform, fixing τ: E → C gives an irreducible π^∞ = ⊗′π_l of GL_2(A_f), the finite part of an automorphic representation, with (π^∞)^{K^p} the λ_τ-part of M_{k+1} ⊗ D₀^{−1}.
hypotheses: ρ appears in H̃¹(K^p, E), i.e. Π_ρ ≠ 0.
The two-weight decomposition assumes k>0; the classical automorphic weight is k+1. This corrects the unreindexed k+2 in Pan II §7.3.1 (E7).
proofSteps: Admissibility from that of completed cohomology (CC.5); Π_ρ^la ≠ 0 by Schneider–Teitelbaum (Pan II §1.2.2).
The λ-isotypic decomposition from LA.5/pro-modular-representations (Pan II §7.2.1).
π^∞ from the classical eigensystem (Pan II §7.3.1).
acceptance: For ρ attached to a weight-two newform of tame level K^p, Π_ρ is the multiplicity space studied by Emerton, and Π_ρ^la ≠ 0.

sources.match: Completed cohomology with E-coefficients, the multiplicity space Π_ρ, its locally analytic vectors, the λ-isotypic part and the automorphic representation π^∞ attached to a classical ρ.

api.name: PiRho.isotypic

api.name: PiRho.hodgeTate
api.statement: H̃¹(K^p, E)[ρ] ⊗̂ C = W_0 ⊕ W_k when ρ|G_{Q_p} is Hodge–Tate of weights 0, k. Assume k>0 so the two weights are distinct.

api.name: PiRho.automorphic
api.statement: For classical ρ of Hodge–Tate weights 0,k with k>0 and τ:E→C, π^∞ has (π^∞)^{K^p} = (M_{k+1} ⊗ D₀^{−1})[λ_τ], using the Hecke normalisation of §7.2.1. The k+2 in §7.3.1 is the index slip E7.

tests.name: PiRho.nonzero_la
tests.statement: If Π_ρ ≠ 0 then Π_ρ^la ≠ 0 (Schneider–Teitelbaum, admissibility).

tests.name: PiRho.twist
tests.statement: Π_{ρ⊗ε} ≅ Π_ρ ⊗ (twist by t): twisting ρ by the cyclotomic character corresponds to multiplying completed cohomology by t.

tests.name: PiRho.zero
tests.statement: If ρ does not occur in H̃¹(K^p, E) then Π_ρ = 0.

tests.name: PiRho.not_galois_rep
tests.statement: Π_ρ is a representation of GL_2(Q_p) (and of Hecke operators), not of G_Q: the G_Q-action is absorbed by Hom_{G_Q}(ρ, −).

nodes.title: Completed cohomology with period coefficients and the de Rham kernel
nodes.statement: Let ρ be as in LA.12/multiplicity-space-pi-rho with ρ|G_{Q_p} de Rham of Hodge–Tate weights 0, k (k > 0), and λ as there. (1) For k ≥ 1 there is a natural G_{Q_p}-equivariant isomorphism of B⁺_{dR,k}-modules H̃^i(K^p, B⁺_{dR,k}) ≅ H^i(Fl, B⁺_{dR,k}) (imported: CP.6/pan-truncated-period-isomorphism, Pan II Proposition 7.2.3). (2) The locally analytic λ-isotypic part of H̃¹(K^p, B⁺_{dR,k+1} ⊗ E) is H¹(Fl, B^{+,la,χ̃_k}_{dR,k+1}) ⊗ E at λ. (3) (Theorem 7.2.2) There is a natural GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant isomorphism (H̃¹(K^p, E)[ρ] ⊗̂ C)_0^{la} ≅ (ker I¹_{k−1} ⊗ E)[λ] between the locally analytic vectors of the Hodge–Tate weight-0 part and the λ-part of ker I¹_{k−1}. More generally, on H̃¹(K^p, Q_p)^{la,χ̃_k} ⊗̂ C = W_0 ⊕ W_k there is a natural continuous N: W_0 → W_k(k), equal to c_kI¹_{k−1} in the convention N_k = c_kI_{k−1} of LA.11, whose restriction to (V ⊗ C)_0 is Fontaine's operator of V for every two-dimensional irreducible G_Q-subrepresentation V (Pan II §1.2.2).
hypotheses: ρ_λ has Hodge–Tate weights −1, k − 1 (Pan's convention), so the locally analytic vectors of the isotypic part have infinitesimal character χ̃_k.
proofSteps: (1): the comparison map on the étale site and the limit arguments are imported (CP.6/pan-etale-site-truncated-comparison-map, pan-bounded-torsion-inverse-limit, pan-completed-coefficient-and-flag-descent; CC.4/completed-coefficient-interchange).
(2): infinitesimal character χ̃_k by LA.5/infinitesimal-character-of-eigenspaces, then (1) with LA.11/sheaf-fontaine-operator's comparison with Banach cohomology (Pan II Lemma 7.2.7).

(3): ρ de Rham makes Fontaine's operator of the λ-part vanish (Fontaine, requested with the PadicHodgeTheory Part II); by functoriality and LA.11/intertwining-operator-is-fontaine-operator that operator is I¹_{k−1} on the weight-0 part, which is therefore exactly the kernel (Pan II proof of Theorem 7.2.2).
acceptance: For k = 1 the statement is on the λ_τ-isotypic part, where H¹(Fl, O^{la,(0,0)})[λ_τ] = W_0[λ_τ] (Pan II §1.2.5).

sources.locator: §7.2.1, Theorem 7.2.2, Proposition 7.2.3, Lemma 7.2.7 and the conclusion, pp. 117–120
sources.match: Completed cohomology with truncated period-sheaf coefficients equals the cohomology on Fl; the locally analytic λ-part is the cohomology of the χ̃_k-isotypic period sheaf; for de Rham ρ the weight-0 locally analytic part is ker I¹_{k−1} at λ.
The Fontaine operator N on the χ̃_k-isotypic locally analytic completed cohomology and its compatibility with Fontaine's operator of each two-dimensional subrepresentation.

nodes.title: Emerton's classicality theorem, proved geometrically, and finiteness of n-invariants
nodes.statement: Let ρ: G_Q → GL_2(E) be continuous, two-dimensional and absolutely irreducible, such that (1) ρ appears in H̃¹(K^p, E), and (2) ρ|G_{Q_p} is de Rham with Hodge–Tate weights 0 and k for some k > 0. Then (1) ρ arises from a cuspidal eigenform of weight k + 1; (2) for K_p = 1 + p^nM_2(Z_p) with n ≥ 2, the n-invariants of the K_p-analytic vectors of H̃¹(K^p, E)[ρ] (equivalently of Π_ρ) form a finite-dimensional E-vector space. The proof uses no input from the p-adic local Langlands correspondence.
hypotheses: Hodge–Tate weights in Pan's convention; ρ absolutely irreducible; no hypothesis on ρ̄ or on ρ|G_{Q_p} beyond de Rham with distinct weights 0, k.
proofSteps: By LA.12/period-cohomology-comparison the weight-0 locally analytic part of H̃¹(K^p, E)[ρ] ⊗̂ C is (ker I¹_{k−1})[λ], nonzero since Π_ρ^la ≠ 0.

By LA.10/spectral-decomposition the generalised eigenspaces of ker I¹_{k−1} occur only at classical eigensystems of weight k + 1 (or weight-zero ones, excluded by irreducibility), so λ is classical (Pan II proof of Theorem 7.1.2).
Finiteness from LA.7/finiteness-of-analytic-n-invariants.
acceptance: Theorem 1.1.2 is a case of the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture (Pan II Remark 1.1.4); Emerton proved it via local–global compatibility and p-adic local Langlands, Dospinescu–Paškūnas–Schraen proved the finiteness by representation theory (Remark 7.1.3).

sources.locator: Theorem 7.1.2, Remark 7.1.3 and the proof after Theorem 7.2.2, pp. 116–118; Theorems 1.1.2 and 1.1.14, Remarks 1.1.3–1.1.4, pp. 2–5
sources.match: Classicality of two-dimensional de Rham representations with distinct Hodge–Tate weights appearing in completed cohomology, and finiteness of the n-invariants of analytic vectors, by the geometric route.

nodes.title: Π_ρ^la in the supercuspidal case (Breuil–Strauch)
nodes.statement: Let ρ be as in LA.12/classicality-theorem with k ≥ 1 and suppose the attached π_p is supercuspidal; let π′_p be its Jacquet–Langlands transfer to D_p^×. Then there is a GL_2(Q_p)⁰-equivariant isomorphism (upgraded to a GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant one by summing over Z-translates as in LA.9/kernel-on-omega-is-quaternionic) (H̃¹(K^p, C)[λ_τ])_0^{la} ≅ (π^{∞,p})^{K^p} ⊗ [((H¹(Fl, j_!(D_p^×-smooth part of ω^{−k+1}_Dr)) ⊗ π′_p)^{O_{D_p}^×}·ε′_p^{−k+1})/(Sym^{k−1}V* ⊗ π_p)], the embedding of π_p coming from the position of the Hodge filtration of ρ|G_{Q_p}, with a short exact sequence whose sub is (π^∞)^{K^p} ⊗ Sym^{k−1}V* and whose quotient is (H¹(Fl,j_!ω^{k+1,D_p^×-sm}_Dr) ⊗ π′^∞)^{K^p×O_{D_p}^×} ⊗ det^{k+1}·ε′_p^{−k} (Remark 7.3.4). For k = 1 the quaternionic term is (H¹(P¹, j_!π^{(0)}_{Dr,n*}O) ⊗ π′_p)^{O_{D_p}^×} and, by the vanishing-cycle sequence, its subspace from H¹_{dR,c} is D_dR(ρ|G_{Q_p}) ⊗ π_p with π_p embedded as Fil¹D_dR ⊗ π_p; with Emerton's local–global compatibility this is the Breuil–Strauch conjecture for ρ|G_{Q_p} in dual form (proved in general by Dospinescu–Le Bras). Since H̃¹(K^p, E)^la is admissible, the quaternionic cohomology is 'admissible' over C, although C is not spherically complete.
hypotheses: π_p supercuspidal; k ≥ 1 (introduction: k = 1, i.e. weight 2).
proofSteps: Combine LA.12/period-cohomology-comparison with LA.10/de-rham-cohomology-and-eigenspaces (1), moving the away-from-p factor out using new vectors (Pan II proof of Theorem 7.3.2).
GL_2(Q_p)-equivariance from the extension in Pan II Remark 5.4.13 (Remark 7.3.3); the whole Hom space is determined by the weight-0 part (Remark 7.3.4); admissibility remark (Remark 7.3.5).

Comparison with Breuil–Strauch through LA.10/vanishing-cycle-sequence, Emerton's local–global compatibility and Dospinescu–Le Bras (Pan II Remark 7.3.6; inputs requested, used for the comparison only).
acceptance: At k=1 (Theorem 1.1.7), tensor the away-from-p factor with the quotient [(colim_n H¹(P¹,j_!π^{(0)}_{Dr,n*}O)⊗π′_p)^{O_{D_p}^×}/i_π(π_p)]. Take invariants after tensoring with π′_p, and take this quotient before tensoring with (π^{∞,p})^{K^p}; ε′_p^{−k+1} is trivial in this case. The identification with Π_ρ^la⊗̂C uses the multiplicity-space comparison.

sources.locator: §7.3.1, Theorem 7.3.2, Remarks 7.3.3–7.3.6, pp. 121–123; Theorem 1.1.7 and Remark 1.1.8, p. 4
sources.match: Geometric description of the locally analytic vectors in the supercuspidal case through compactly supported cohomology of the Drinfeld tower and quaternionic forms, and its relation to the Breuil–Strauch conjecture.

nodes.title: Π_ρ^la in the principal series case (Berger–Breuil–Emerton)
nodes.statement: Let ρ be as in LA.12/classicality-theorem with k ≥ 1 and π_p a principal series. Then there is a GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant isomorphism (H̃¹(K^p, C)[λ_τ])_0^{la} ≅ (Ind_B^{GL_2(Q_p)}(H¹_rig(Ig(K^p), Sym^{k−1})·ε^{−k+1}(e′₂)^{k−1})^{la})[λ]/((π^∞)^{K^p} ⊗ Sym^{k−1}V*), with the corresponding short exact sequence whose quotient is the induction twisted by ε^{−k+1}(e′₁)^k(e′₂)^{−1} at λ. For k = 1, Remark 7.3.9 sketches the further identification H¹_rig(Ig(K^p))[λ] ≅ (π^{∞,p})^{K^p} ⊗ D_cris,K_N(ρ|G_{Q_p}), where K_N=Q_p(μ_{p^N}) is sufficiently large and D_cris,K_N(V)=(V⊗B_cris)^{G_{K_N}}. This is a potentially crystalline module over K_N, not necessarily D_cris,Q_p(V). With the congruence-relation B-action and the embedding through Fil¹, it gives the Berger–Breuil–Emerton quotient after local–global compatibility. This comparison, and any extension to Sym^{k−1} coefficients, is conditional on the missing Igusa log-rigid/log-crystalline Galois comparison; the geometric formula above remains the target of Theorem 7.3.7.
hypotheses: π_p a principal series; k ≥ 1.
proofSteps: Combine LA.12/period-cohomology-comparison with LA.10/de-rham-cohomology-and-eigenspaces (2) (Pan II Theorem 7.3.7, Remark 7.3.8).

The optional D_cris,K_N comparison of Remark 7.3.9, pp. 123–124, needs the Igusa log-rigid/log-crystalline comparison, Galois eigenspace identification and Carayol congruence relation. RD.4/proper-log-rigid-convergent-comparison only covers constant coefficients and does not supply these identifications. Record the comparison as conditional rather than deduce it from RD.4.
acceptance: Theorem 1.1.10 is the case k = 1: Π_ρ^la ⊗̂ C ≅ (Ind_B^{GL_2(Q_p)}H¹_rig(Ig(K^p))[λ_τ])^{la}/i_π((π^∞)^{K^p}).

sources.locator: Theorem 7.3.7, Remarks 7.3.8–7.3.9, pp. 123–124; Theorem 1.1.10 and Remark 1.1.11, pp. 4–5
sources.match: Geometric description of the locally analytic vectors in the principal series case as a quotient of the locally analytic induction of Igusa rigid cohomology, and its identification with Ind D_cris modulo π_p.

nodes.title: The uniform description Π_ρ^la ⊗̂ C = H¹(DR_{k−1})[λ]/Fil¹
nodes.statement: In both the supercuspidal and the principal series cases, the canonical weight-zero completed-cohomology space W₀^{la}[λ] is H¹(DR_{k−1})[λ]/Fil¹. Choosing a nonzero vector in the one-dimensional Hodge–Tate weight-zero line of ρ⊗_{E,τ}C identifies it noncanonically with Π_ρ^la ⊗̂_{E,τ} C; thus, after that choice, Π_ρ^la ⊗̂_{E,τ} C ≅ H¹(DR_{k−1})[λ]/Fil¹H¹(DR_{k−1})[λ], with DR_{k−1} the two-term de Rham complex of d_k on Fl and Fil its Hodge filtration; for k = 1, Fil¹H¹(DR_0)[λ] = Fil¹colim_{K_p}H¹_dR,log(X_{K^pK_p})[λ] = (π^∞)^{K^p}. Thus the Breuil–Strauch and Berger–Breuil–Emerton descriptions are two instances of one statement; H¹(DR_{k−1})[λ] itself does not see the Hodge filtration, in analogy with Kashiwara–Schmid's constructions for real groups.
hypotheses: π_p supercuspidal or a principal series.
proofSteps: ker I¹_{k−1}[λ] = H¹(DR_{k−1})[λ]/Fil¹ in both cases (LA.10/de-rham-cohomology-and-eigenspaces, Pan II Remark 5.5.15) and LA.12/period-cohomology-comparison (Pan II Remarks 1.1.13, 7.3.10).

Distinguish the canonical W₀ statement from the choice needed to identify Π_ρ⊗C with W₀ (Pan II Remark 7.3.5, p. 122). For the displayed k=1 cuspidal λ, the boundary contribution to log de Rham cohomology vanishes.
acceptance: The expected special-case analogue is LA.12/special-case-claim.

sources.match: The uniform description of Π_ρ^la ⊗̂ C as H¹ of the de Rham complex on the flag variety modulo its Hodge filtration.

nodes.title: Claim (conditional): the special case
nodes.statement: Claim, sketched but not proved in the source (Remark 7.3.11; Remarks 1.2.4 and 5.5.15 assert that it can be shown with p-adic local Langlands inputs): let k = 1, π_p special and ρ|G_{Q_p} absolutely irreducible. Then the inclusion (H̃¹(K^p, C)[λ_τ])_0^{la} ⊂ (ker I¹_0)~[λ_τ] of LA.12/period-cohomology-comparison is an equality, so the generalised eigenspace is the eigenspace. Sketch given by the author: Emerton's local–global compatibility identifies the left side with (π^{∞,p})^{K^p} ⊗̂ Π(ρ|G_{Q_p})^la, whose structure is known by Liu–Xie–Zhang and Colmez; a Serre-duality analysis would identify Fil² of the three-step filtration with (π^{∞,p})^{K^p} ⊗̂ Σ(2, L) (Breuil) and gr³ with the induction in Emerton's conjectural sequence.
hypotheses: Conditional on Emerton's local–global compatibility, the Liu–Xie–Zhang–Colmez description of Π(V)^la in the special case, Breuil's Σ(2, L), and the unproved Serre-duality analysis of Pan II Remark 7.3.11.
proofSteps: The three-step filtration at λ_τ (LA.10/three-step-filtration) has graded pieces (π^{p,∞})^{K^p} ⊗ π_p, the quaternionic term and the Igusa induction (Pan II Remark 7.3.11).
Compare piece by piece with the p-adic local Langlands description (inputs requested from R31.4 and R30.4); the identification of Fil² and gr³ is asserted, not proved, in the source.
acceptance: Recorded as a gap: a direct proof is asked for in Pan II Remark 5.5.15.

sources.match: The special case: the paper claims, with a sketch relying on p-adic local Langlands inputs, that the generalised eigenspace is an eigenspace; it is not proved.

requests.need: Coherent cohomology of the compactified modular curves with automorphic coefficients: for K = K^pK_p and k ∈ Z, the finite-dimensional spaces H^i(X_{K,C}, ω^k) (i = 0, 1), their GAGA comparison with the complex-analytic spaces of modular forms, their GL_2(A_f)-equivariant transition maps in K and the prime-to-p Hecke action (Pan I §1, p. 3, and Lemma 5.3.5, p. 60). Also supply Serre duality on the smooth proper compactified curve, with Ω¹(log cusps) identified by logarithmic Kodaira–Spencer, the induced Hecke adjoints/twists, and compatibility with localising at a non-Eisenstein eigensystem, as used in Pan I proof of Theorem 6.2.2, pp. 70–71.

R31.1 specialises completed cohomology to modular curves: for a tame level K^p, H̃^i(K^p, Z_p) = lim_n colim_{K_p} H^i(Y_{K^pK_p}(C), Z/p^n) with its continuous admissible GL_2(Q_p)- and Hecke actions, vanishing for i ≥ 2, unchanged after taking the direct limit over p-level when Y is replaced by the compactified curves (using unbounded p-power ramification at the cusps; no finite-level equality is asserted) (Pan I §4.4.1, pp. 43–44), and with O_C- and C-coefficient versions H̃^i(K^p, O_C) = H̃^i(K^p, Z_p) ⊗̂ O_C, H̃^i(K^p, C) (Pan I p. 45).

The big Hecke algebra of completed cohomology of modular curves and its Galois determinant: for a tame level K^p = K_SK^S with K^S hyperspecial outside a finite set S ∋ p, T(K^p) = lim_{K_p} image of Z_p[GL_2(A_f^S)//K^S] in End H¹(Y_{K^pK_p}(C), Z_p), independent of S; a two-dimensional determinant D_S of G_{Q,S} valued in T(K^p); for λ: T(K^p) → Q̄_p the semisimple odd ρ_λ: G_{Q,S} → GL_2(Q̄_p) with det = λ∘D_S and tr ρ_λ(Frob_l) = λ(T_l)l^{−1} for l ∉ S (Frob_l geometric); and the Eichler–Shimura relation giving H̃¹(K^p, Q̄_p)[p_λ] = ρ_λ(−1) ⊗ Hom_{G_Q}(ρ_λ(−1), H̃¹(K^p, Q̄_p)) for irreducible ρ_λ (Pan I §6.1.1, pp. 67–68; Pan II §7.1.4, pp. 116–117).

Supply Emerton’s local–global compatibility under its original hypotheses, and the dense classical/algebraic vectors with Hecke semisimplicity used in Pan I Lemmas 6.3.8–6.3.9. LA.5/local-global-compatibility-at-eisenstein-ideals proves Pan I Theorem 6.3.5 and Corollary 6.3.6 from these inputs and Paškūnas–Tung; this request does not import those same conclusions. For the comparisons only, supply the factorisation through Π(ρ|G_{Q_p}) used in Pan II Remarks 7.3.6, 7.3.9 and 7.3.11.

Emerton's promodularity theorem: for p > 2 and a continuous irreducible odd ρ: G_Q → GL_2(Q̄_p) unramified outside finitely many primes, with ρ̄|G_{Q(μ_p)} irreducible and (ρ̄|G_{Q_p})^{ss} irreducible or η₁ ⊕ η₂ with η₁/η₂ ≠ 1, ω^{±1}, ρ is pro-modular (Emerton 2011, Theorem 1.2.3; Pan I Theorem 6.4.8).

Locally analytic vectors of representations, at the generality of Pan I §2 and Pan II §2 (the owner named by the extraction PAPER-PAN-26, route 11, is the proposed roadmap LocallyAnalyticRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, whose design has not run; L0 is the existing layer that already supplies the locally convex foundations and is named by CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.6 as the owner of the derived locally-analytic functor): for a compact p-adic Lie group G with a uniform open subgroup G_0 and G_n = G_0^{p^n}, the Banach space C^an(G_n, B) of B-valued analytic functions with its norm, the G_n-analytic vectors B^{G_n-an} of a Q_p-Banach representation B and B^la = colim_n B^{G_n-an} with the inductive-limit topology (Pan I Definition 2.1.6, p. 11), the Lie-algebra action and its bound (Pan I Lemmas 2.1.5 and 2.1.8), R^iLA(B) = colim_n H^i_cont(G_n, B ⊗̂ C^an(G_n, Q_p)), LA-acyclicity and strong LA-acyclicity (Pan I Definition 2.2.1, pp. 11–12), the long exact sequence and the two acyclicity transfers of Pan I Lemma 2.2.2, strong LA-acyclicity of admissible Banach representations and of their completed tensor products with trivial Banach spaces (Pan I Theorem 2.2.3 and Corollary 2.2.4, pp. 12–13); and for Hausdorff LB-space representations the locally analytic vectors and the criteria of Pan II §2 (Proposition 2.1.5, Proposition 2.2.3, Corollary 2.2.4, Lemma 2.2.5, Proposition 2.3.3, Corollary 2.3.4, Proposition 2.3.6, pp. 12–17). Locally analytic induction from the Borel B ⊂ GL_2(Q_p) of a Hausdorff LB-space representation on which B acts locally analytically, as a GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant sheaf on P¹(Q_p) with global sections the induced representation (Pan II §5.1.10, p. 55; the extraction PAPER-PAN-26 routes this to the proposed LocallyAnalyticRepresentationsOfLocalGroups).

Scholze's comparison of the two B⁺_dR-lattices (Proposition 7.9 of 'p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties'), in its logarithmic form on the modular curve: V̂_log ⊗ B⁺_dR ⊇ (D_dR,log ⊗ OB⁺_dR,log)^{∇=0} ⊇ V̂_log ⊗ ker θ, and the resulting inclusion of the determinant of the de Rham bundle into t times the determinant of V (Pan I (4.1.2), Pan II §§6.4.1–6.4.2 and the proof of Lemma 6.4.6; extraction item /567, routed to the PadicHodgeTheory Part II).

Part II (PadicHodgeTheoryPartII; its design DESIGN-PadicHodgeTheoryPartII has not run, and the extraction PAPER-PAN-26 route 12 proposing it has no review verdict yet): Fontaine's almost de Rham theory in the generality of Pan II §6.1 — Banach B⁺_dR/(t^k)-modules W with continuous semilinear G_K-action, flatness and graded pieces W_i = W_0(i) (§6.1.2); the decompletion W ↦ W^K and Fontaine's generalisation of Sen theory (Proposition 6.1.5, Lemmas 6.1.6–6.1.7); kernels and cokernels of strict maps (Proposition 6.1.8); Hodge–Tate modules of weights 0, l (Definition 6.1.9, §6.1.10, Lemma 6.1.11); the Fontaine operator N_W: W_{0,0} → W_{0,−k}(k) of a flat Hodge–Tate B⁺_dR/(t^{k+1})-module of weights 0, k from the action of Lie Gal(K_∞/K) on the generalised 0-eigenspace E_0(W^K) (§6.1.12, Definition 6.1.13, Remark 6.1.14); N_W = 0 iff V is de Rham for W = V ⊗ B⁺_dR/(t^{k+1}) (Theorem 6.1.16, Fontaine); the LB-module versions (§6.1.17, Proposition 6.1.18, §6.1.19) and exactness with compatibility of Fontaine operators (Proposition 6.1.20, Corollary 6.1.21, read with B⁺_dR/(t^{k+1}) — the printed B⁺_dR/(t^k) is the misprint E4 of the extraction). PadicHodgeTheory already owns Fontaine's classification of B_dR-representations (P7/fontaine-bdr-indecomposable-classification) and almost C-representations (R06.2); the request is for the Banach and LB extension and the operator N_W.

Colmez's Kirillov model for the locally analytic vectors of Π(V): for a two-dimensional E-representation V of G_{Q_p}, a P-equivariant embedding C_c(Q_p^×, D⁻_dif(V))^Γ → Π(V)^la_E, P the mirabolic subgroup (Colmez 2010, Chapitre VI; Pan I Theorem 6.4.3), and the bijection between two-dimensional absolutely irreducible E-representations of G_{Q_p} and nonordinary admissible unitary E-Banach representations of GL_2(Q_p) (Colmez–Dospinescu–Paškūnas, Theorem 1.1; Pan I p. 73). For the comparisons of Pan II Remarks 7.3.6, 7.3.9 and 7.3.11 only: the locally analytic vectors of Π(V) for V two-dimensional absolutely irreducible — Π(V)^la ⊗̂ C = Ind_B^{GL_2(Q_p)} D_cris(V)/π_p in the crystalline principal series case and Emerton's conjectured structure in the semistable special case (Liu–Xie–Zhang 2012, Colmez 2014; extraction item /565), and Breuil's locally analytic representation Σ(2, L) attached to an L-invariant (Breuil 2004, §§2–3; item /566).

Paškūnas's and Paškūnas–Tung's results on blocks of locally admissible representations of GL_2(Q_p) with a central character: the finite map from the pseudodeformation ring R^{ps,ζε_p}_{ρ̄_𝔅} to the Bernstein centre Z_𝔅 compatible with Colmez's functor, and the faithful exact functor m to R^{ps}-modules sending admissible representations to finitely generated modules (Pan I Theorem 6.3.3, quoting Paškūnas–Tung, Theorem 1.2). For the comparison of Pan II Remark 7.3.6 only: the Breuil–Strauch conjecture as proved by Dospinescu–Le Bras (Annals 2017, Théorème 1.4), describing Π(ρ_p)^la for de Rham ρ_p of Hodge–Tate weights 0, 1 with supercuspidal π_p through the compactly supported cohomology of the Drinfeld tower.

The supersingular uniformization of the perfectoid modular curve at infinite level (the extraction PAPER-PAN-26, route 3, accepted, names S3/S5 as its owner, but the accepted packet has no node for it): with E₀ supersingular over F̄_p, D = End(E₀) ⊗ Q (ramified at p and ∞, D ⊗ Q_p = D_p) and K^p viewed in (D ⊗ A_f^p)^× via a fixed trivialisation of H¹_ét(E₀, A_f^p), a GL_2(Q_p)-equivariant isomorphism, functorial in K^p, π_HT^{-1}(Ω) ≅ D^×\(M_{LT,∞} × (D ⊗ A_f^p)^×/K^p) identifying π_HT with π_{LT,HT} and ω_{K^p}|Ω with the pull-back of ω_LT, D^× acting through the main involution (Pan II Theorem 5.4.2, from Scholze 2015 Lemma III.3.6 and Rapoport–Zink); and its consequence that π_HT^{-1}(Ω) is a finite disjoint union of copies of the height-zero Lubin–Tate space M^{(0)}_{LT,∞}, GL_2(Q_p)⁰-equivariantly (Pan II Lemma 5.4.4).

LieHighestWeight layer 7 supplies the semisimple sl_2 Harish–Chandra isomorphism and dot action.
